literature.headline_zh: HPV疫苗与筛查研究进展:治疗性疫苗免疫原性良好但清除率未显著,自采样与合并检测优化筛查策略。
literature.lead_zh: 近期多项研究聚焦人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)的预防、筛查与治疗。一项1b/2期试验显示,新型治疗性HPV疫苗VTP-200虽安全且诱导T细胞应答,但未显著提高高危HPV清除率[10.1093/cid/ciaf658]。同时,系统综述和荟萃分析发现HPV与前列腺癌存在正相关,尤其高危型HPV[10.1002/ijc.70663]。在筛查方面,尿液自采样诊断准确性低于临床采样,但便利性可提高参与度[10.1177/09691413261471634];合并检测策略在低流行区可大幅减少检测量[10.7189/jogh.16.04275]。此外,研究揭示了特定人群的行为风险因素和疫苗接受度障碍,为精准干预提供依据。
key_findings_zh: VTP-200治疗性疫苗在持续高危HPV感染女性中安全且诱导T细胞应答,但12个月时HPV清除率与安慰剂无差异(31.3% vs 33.3%)[10.1093/cid/ciaf658]。
荟萃分析显示,前列腺标本中检测到致癌HPV DNA与前列腺癌风险增加相关(合并OR=2.35),高危型HPV关联更强(OR=2.75)[10.1002/ijc.70663]。
尿液自采样检测高危HPV的敏感性(75%)低于阴道(92%)和宫颈样本(95%),但特异性相当,可作为不愿参与筛查女性的替代方案[10.1177/09691413261471634]。
在HPV低流行区(如孟加拉国,2.10%),合并检测可节省71%-77%的检测量,但可能增加假阴性率[10.7189/jogh.16.04275]。
中国大学男男性行为者中,高风险行为特征(如临时性行为、物质使用)与肛门HPV感染率升高显著相关(52.90% vs 25.55%)[10.1186/s12889-026-28509-4]。
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 治疗性HPV疫苗研发仍面临挑战,现有候选疫苗虽具免疫原性但临床终点改善有限;HPV与前列腺癌的关联需进一步明确病因学意义;筛查技术优化(自采样、合并检测)有助于提高覆盖率,但需权衡敏感性与便利性。
literature.caveats_zh: 部分研究为横断面或模拟设计,无法推断因果关系;治疗性疫苗试验样本量较小,需更大规模验证;荟萃分析纳入研究异质性较高。
literature.headline_en: HPV Vaccine and Screening Advances: Therapeutic Vaccine Immunogenic but Lacking Clearance Benefit, Self-Sampling and Pooled Testing Optimize Strategies.
literature.lead_en: Recent studies on human papillomaviruses (HPV) highlight progress and challenges in prevention, screening, and treatment. A phase 1b/2 trial found that the therapeutic vaccine VTP-200 was safe and immunogenic but did not significantly improve high-risk HPV clearance [10.1093/cid/ciaf658]. A meta-analysis reported a positive association between HPV and prostate cancer, especially for high-risk types [10.1002/ijc.70663]. Urine self-sampling showed lower sensitivity than clinician-collected samples but may increase screening uptake [10.1177/09691413261471634], while pooled testing could reduce costs in low-prevalence settings [10.7189/jogh.16.04275]. Behavioral risk factors and vaccine acceptance barriers were also identified in specific populations.
key_findings_en: The therapeutic vaccine VTP-200 was safe and induced T-cell responses in women with persistent high-risk HPV, but 12-month HPV clearance did not differ from placebo (31.3% vs 33.3%) [10.1093/cid/ciaf658].

A meta-analysis found that detection of oncogenic HPV DNA in prostate specimens was associated with increased prostate cancer risk (pooled OR=2.35), with a stronger association for high-risk HPV (OR=2.75) [10.1002/ijc.70663].

Urine self-sampling for high-risk HPV detection had lower sensitivity (75%) than vaginal (92%) and cervical samples (95%), but comparable specificity, offering an alternative for women who decline clinician-based screening [10.1177/09691413261471634].
In low HPV prevalence settings (e.g., Bangladesh, 2.10%), pooled testing saved 71%–77% of tests but may increase false-negative rates [10.7189/jogh.16.04275].

Among university-attending MSM in China, a high-risk behavioral profile (e.g., casual sex, substance use) was significantly associated with higher anal HPV infection prevalence (52.90% vs 25.55%) [10.1186/s12889-026-28509-4].
literature.trend_or_risk_en: Therapeutic HPV vaccines remain challenging, with current candidates showing immunogenicity but limited clinical efficacy; the etiological role of HPV in prostate cancer requires further clarification; screening innovations (self-sampling, pooling) can enhance coverage but involve trade-offs between sensitivity and convenience.
literature.caveats_en: Some studies are cross-sectional or simulation-based, limiting causal inference; the therapeutic vaccine trial had a small sample size; the meta-analysis included heterogeneous studies.
literature.brief_en: Recent HPV research shows therapeutic vaccine VTP-200 is safe but lacks clearance benefit; meta-analysis links HPV to prostate cancer; urine self-sampling and pooled testing offer screening alternatives with trade-offs; behavioral risks identified in MSM.

news.headline_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期人乳头瘤病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 石药集团(石药集团)宣布在中国启动SYS 6026注射液治疗HPV16或18相关HSIL的II期临床试验。该试验是一项多中心、随机、双盲、安慰剂对照研究,评估疗效和安全性。 [news-e72f371db32b07fd]
HPV16阳性癌症的市场分析和预测报告,涵盖流行病学、当前疗法、管道开发和市场趋势。包括临床试验、监管指定和治疗方法的最新信息。 [news-786657a50dd2e01d]
大连市疾病预防控制中心(CDC)发布针对青少年的HPV 疫苗接种权威指南。文章确认HPV 疫苗自2025年11月10日起已纳入国家免疫规划,并对家长普遍关心的疫苗接种问题进行了详细解答。 [news-6b0ca6e41112b66f]
健康指导文章强调了 HPV 阳性女性的五个要点。不是 暴发 报告或已确认的疾病事件。 [news-c1783980c80a7f07]
KP 卫生部门寻求神职人员对人类乳头状瘤病毒 疫苗接种 活动的支持。这是一项旨在提高 疫苗接种 率的公共卫生举措,所提供的证据中没有报告确诊病例或死亡病例。 [news-6ae33506906e1316]

news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Human papillomaviruses news developments.
key_findings_en: Shijiazhuang Pharmaceutical Group (CSPC) announced the initiation of a Phase II clinical trial in China for SYS 6026 injection to treat HPV16 or 18-related HSIL. The trial is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study evaluating efficacy and safety. [news-e72f371db32b07fd]

Market analysis and forecast report on HPV16-positive cancers, covering epidemiology, current therapies, pipeline developments, and market trends. Includes updates on clinical trials, regulatory designations, and therapeutic approaches. [news-786657a50dd2e01d]

The Dalian Disease Control and Prevention Center (CDC) has issued authoritative guidance on HPV vaccination for adolescents. The article confirms that HPV vaccine has been included in the national immunization program since November 10, 2025, and provides detailed answers to common parental concerns about vaccination. [news-6b0ca6e41112b66f]
Health guidance article emphasizing five key points for women with HPV positive results. Not an outbreak report or confirmed disease event. [news-c1783980c80a7f07]

KP health department seeks clerics’ support for human papilloma virus vaccination drive. This is a public health initiative aimed at increasing vaccination rates, with no confirmed cases or deaths reported in the supplied evidence. [news-6ae33506906e1316]

papers.title: A Phase 1b/2, Randomised, Placebo-controlled Study to Evaluate Safety, Tolerability, Efficacy, and Immunogenicity of VTP-200, a Chimpanzee Adenovirus and Modified Vaccinia Ankara-vectored Multigenotype High-risk Human Papillomavirus Vaccine in Women With Low-grade Cervical Lesions.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The clearance of high-risk oncogenic human papillomaviruses (hrHPV) and related cervical lesions is associated with the development of a robust T-cell response. Therapeutic vaccination that induces HPV antigen-specific T cells is a promising approach. METHOD: A 2-vector dosing strategy using Chimpanzee Adenovirus Oxford 1-HPV and Modified Vaccinia virus Ankara-HPV, both encoding the same multiantigen HPV cassette was given on a 0/28-day schedule to participants with persistent cervical hrHPV and a history of low-grade cervical lesions. An open-label lead-in was followed by a randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled main phase. The primary endpoint was the safety of the different dose regimens; secondary endpoints included immunogenicity, and clearance of hrHPV and associated lesions at 12 months. Nine participants were enrolled in the lead-in and 99 were randomized 67:32 to 5 active dose arms or placebo, respectively. RESULTS: The regimens were well-tolerated with no grade 3-related treatment emergent adverse events or serious adverse reactions. All dosing regimens generated antigen-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell responses. There was no difference in hrHPV clearance between the pooled active groups and placebo (20/64 [31.3%] versus 10/30 [33.3%]; P > .99), nor in lesion clearance. A trend toward higher hrHPV clearance (60%) was observed with the highest Chimpanzee Adenovirus Oxford 1-HPV doses. No association between the peripheral immune response and clearance was demonstrated. CONCLUSIONS: A heterologous, multiantigenic HPV 2-component immunotherapy regimen was well-tolerated and immunogenic but did not result in a statistically significant clearance of either hrHPV or the associated cervical lesions in women with persistent high-risk HPV infections. TRIAL REGISTRATION: EudraCT 2019-001890-98; NCT04607850.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The clearance of high-risk oncogenic human papillomaviruses (hrHPV) and related cervical lesions is associated with the development of a robust T-cell response. Therapeutic vaccination that induces HPV antigen-specific T cells is a promising approach.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An open-label lead-in was followed by a randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled main phase. Nine participants were enrolled in the lead-in and 99 were randomized 67:32 to 5 active dose arms or placebo, respectively.
analysis.methods: A 2-vector dosing strategy using Chimpanzee Adenovirus Oxford 1-HPV and Modified Vaccinia virus Ankara-HPV, both encoding the same multiantigen HPV cassette was given on a 0/28-day schedule to participants with persistent cervical hrHPV and a history of low-grade cervical lesions.
analysis.main_results: The regimens were well-tolerated with no grade 3-related treatment emergent adverse events or serious adverse reactions. All dosing regimens generated antigen-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell responses. There was no difference in hrHPV clearance between the pooled active groups and placebo (20/64 [31.3%] versus 10/30 [33.3%]; P > .99), nor in lesion clearance.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: A heterologous, multiantigenic HPV 2-component immunotherapy regimen was well-tolerated and immunogenic but did not result in a statistically significant clearance of either hrHPV or the associated cervical lesions in women with persistent high-risk HPV infections.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that while the vaccine is safe and induces immune responses, it does not significantly improve hrHPV clearance or lesion resolution in this population, indicating a need for further optimization of therapeutic HPV vaccines.

analysis.summary_en: This phase 1b/2 randomized, placebo-controlled study evaluated the safety, tolerability, efficacy, and immunogenicity of VTP-200, a chimpanzee adenovirus and modified vaccinia Ankara-vectored multigenotype high-risk human papillomavirus vaccine in women with low-grade cervical lesions. The study included an open-label lead-in with 9 participants and a main phase with 99 randomized participants (67 active, 32 placebo). The vaccine was well-tolerated with no serious adverse events and induced antigen-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell responses. However, there was no statistically significant difference in hrHPV clearance (31.3% vs 33.3%; P > .99) or lesion clearance between active and placebo groups. The highest dose showed a trend toward higher hrHPV clearance (60%). The authors conclude that while the vaccine is immunogenic, it did not significantly improve hrHPV clearance or lesion resolution in this population.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 高风险致癌 人乳头瘤病毒 (hrHPV) 和相关宫颈病变的清除与强大的 T 细胞反应的发展相关。诱导 HPV 抗原特异性 T 细胞的治疗性 疫苗接种 是一种有前途的方法。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 开放标签导入期之后是随机、盲法、安慰剂对照的主要阶段。9 名参与者参加了导入试验,99 名参与者以 67:32 的比例分别随机分配到 5 个活性剂量组或安慰剂组。
elements_zh.methods: 使用黑猩猩腺病毒 Oxford 1-HPV 和改良痘苗病毒 Ankara-HPV 的 2-媒介 剂量策略(两者均编码相同的多抗原 HPV 盒)按 0/28 天的计划给予患有持续性宫颈 hrHPV 和有低度宫颈病变史的参与者。
elements_zh.main_results: 该方案耐受性良好,没有出现 3 级相关的 治疗 紧急不良事件或严重不良反应。所有给药方案均产生抗原特异性 CD4+ 和 CD8+ T 细胞反应。合并的活性组和安慰剂组之间的 hrHPV 清除率没有差异(20/64 [31.3%] 与 10/30 [33.3%];P > .99),病灶清除率也没有差异。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 异源、多抗原 HPV 2 成分免疫治疗方案具有良好的耐受性和免疫原性,但在持续 高危型HPV 感染的女性中,并没有导致 hrHPV 或相关宫颈病变的统计学显着清除。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,虽然 疫苗 是安全的并能诱导 免疫应答,但它并没有显着改善该人群中 hrHPV 的清除或病变消退,表明需要进一步优化治疗性 HPV 疫苗。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到样本量的限制,并且 hrHPV 清除率缺乏统计学上的显着差异,尽管最高剂量显示出清除率较高的趋势。由于随机设计,证据强度中等,但受到样本量小和缺乏长期随访的限制。

papers.title: The Association Between Human Papillomavirus and Prostate Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Human papillomavirus (HPV), the necessary cause of cervical cancer, is associated with an increased risk of other anogenital cancers. While HPV has frequently been detected in prostate specimens, its role in prostate carcinogenesis remains controversial. We synthesized and meta‐analyzed the epidemiological literature on the association between HPV and prostate cancer. We completed a systematic search of Embase, MEDLINE, Scopus and Cochrane on January 31, 2025. Two reviewers independently screened articles and extracted data on study design and population, sample characteristics, HPV and prostate cancer ascertainment methods, and results. We pooled risk estimates using a random effects model and performed subgroup meta‐analyses by HPV risk level, genotype, and control group. Our search identified 1874 unique records. Of 84 included articles (1990–2025), 57 were cross‐sectional, 15 case–control, 6 nested case–control, and 6 were cohort studies. HPV detection methods reported were HPV DNA ( n = 57); HPV serology ( n = 17); subjects' self‐report ( n = 5); chart review, registry or claims data ( n = 4); RNA ( n = 3); and immunohistochemistry ( n = 2). Most studies (58.3%) reported HPV prevalence below 20%. Our meta‐analysis (39 studies) produced a pooled odds ratio (OR) of 2.35 (95% CI: 1.87–2.95). When restricted to high‐risk HPV, the pooled OR was 2.75 (95% CI: 1.69–4.46). HPV16, HPV18, and HPV33 had positive associations with prostate cancer (pooled ORs: 2.28, 95% CI: 1.18–4.40; 2.37, 95% CI: 1.16–4.87; 3.73, 95% CI: 0.46–30.30, respectively) and the association was strongest when using normal tissue as controls (pooled OR:4.81, 95% CI: 1.83–12.69). Our findings support a positive association between the detection of oncogenic HPV DNA in prostate specimens and prostate cancer, although its etiologic significance remains unclear.

papers.title: Self-collected versus clinician-collected human papillomavirus samples.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to evaluate the comparability of self-collected and clinician-collected samples for human papillomavirus detection, cytological findings, and identification of infectious agents. METHODS: This prospective controlled clinical trial enrolled 124 women aged 30-65 years due for routine cervical cancer screening. This prospective comparative study enrolled 124 women aged 30-65 years who were eligible for routine cervical cancer screening. Participants were allocated to either a clinician-collected control group (n=51) or a self-collected group (n=73) via systematic allocation based on clinic registration order. Viral deoxyribonucleic acid analysis was performed by multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction; cytological evaluation followed the Bethesda classification system. Infectious agents and participant satisfaction were also assessed. Laboratory personnel were blinded to group allocation. RESULTS: Overall human papillomavirus positivity was 21.8% (27/124), with rates of 27.5% (14/51) in the control group and 17.8% (13/73) in the self-collected group (p=0.200). Cytological abnormalities were detected in 5.5% of self-collected samples (three cases of atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance, one case of atypical squamous cells cannot exclude high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion) versus 0% in the control group (p=0.236). Inflammatory smear findings, Candida (9.8 vs. 8.2%), and Trichomonas vaginalis (0 vs. 1.4%) detection rates were similar between groups. Mean satisfaction score was 12.6±1.62 out of 16 (78.8% positive responses). CONCLUSION: Self-collected human papillomavirus sampling yields results diagnostically comparable to clinician-collected specimens. Self collected human papillomavirus sampling demonstrated similar human papillomavirus detection rates compared with clinician-collected specimens. Given its feasibility and high acceptability, self-collection may serve as an effective complementary approach in cervical cancer screening programs, particularly for reaching women who have not previously participated in screening.

papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to evaluate the comparability of self-collected and clinician-collected samples for human papillomavirus detection, cytological findings, and identification of infectious agents. METHODS: This prospective controlled clinical trial enrolled 124 women aged 30-65 years due for routine cervical cancer screening. This prospective comparative study enrolled 124 women aged 30-65 years who were eligible for routine cervical cancer screening. Participants were allocated to either a clinician-collected control group (n=51) or a self-collected group (n=73) via systematic allocation based on clinic registration order. Viral deoxyribonucleic acid analysis was performed by multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction; cytological evaluation followed the Bethesda classification system. Infectious agents and participant satisfaction were also assessed. Laboratory personnel were blinded to group allocation. RESULTS: Overall human papillomavirus positivity was 21.8% (27/124), with rates of 27.5% (14/51) in the control group and 17.8% (13/73) in the self-collected group (p=0.200). Cytological abnormalities were detected in 5.5% of self-collected samples (three cases of atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance, one case of atypical squamous cells cannot exclude high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion) versus 0% in the control group (p=0.236). Inflammatory smear findings, Candida (9.8 vs. 8.2%), and Trichomonas vaginalis (0 vs. 1.4%) detection rates were similar between groups. Mean satisfaction score was 12.6±1.62 out of 16 (78.8% positive responses). CONCLUSION: Self-collected human papillomavirus sampling yields results diagnostically comparable to clinician-collected specimens. Self collected human papillomavirus sampling demonstrated similar human papillomavirus detection rates compared with clinician-collected specimens. Given its feasibility and high acceptability, self-collection may serve as an effective complementary approach in cervical cancer screening programs, particularly for reaching women who have not previously participated in screening.

papers.title: The cervicovaginal microbiome: an emerging determinant of HPV infection and disease
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Human papillomaviruses (HPVs) are epitheliotropic viruses that cause diseases ranging from cutaneous warts to invasive cancers. HPVs exhibit tropism for the epithelial lining of the skin, oral cavity, and anogenital tract. A subset of HPVs, known as high-risk HPVs, have oncogenic potential and cause nearly one-third of all virus-associated cancers worldwide, including essentially all cervical cancers, most other anogenital cancers, and a growing percentage of head and neck cancers. A large and growing body of clinical and epidemiological research has established the host microbiome, or the collection of microorganisms on and within the body, as a key determinant of HPV infection, persistence, and disease development. In this review, an overview of the current understanding of associations between bacterial components of the host cervicovaginal microbiome (CVM) and aspects of HPV pathogenesis is discussed. Potential mechanisms through which the CVM influences HPV infection and neoplastic disease development are also presented. The inherent challenges of studying HPVs and the microbiome have impeded progress to define not only the underlying mechanisms involved in HPV-CVM interactions, but also the ability to address remaining questions such as causality, temporal dynamics, and the directionality of this relationship. Emerging in vitro and in vivo models provide powerful opportunities to address these outstanding questions and increase our understanding of trans-kingdom interactions that contribute to HPV infection and subsequent disease.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on human papillomaviruses (HPVs), specifically their role in causing diseases ranging from cutaneous warts to invasive cancers, with emphasis on high-risk HPVs that are oncogenic and associated with cervical, anogenital, and head and neck cancers. The central question examines how the cervicovaginal microbiome (CVM) influences HPV infection, persistence, and disease development.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative overview that synthesizes clinical and epidemiological research on the host microbiome as a determinant of HPV pathogenesis. It does not report specific databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or study counts, nor does it employ a meta-analysis or consensus process.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: There is strong agreement that the host microbiome, particularly the bacterial components of the cervicovaginal microbiome, is a key determinant of HPV infection, persistence, and disease development. High-risk HPVs are established as the primary cause of nearly one-third of all virus-associated cancers worldwide, including cervical and other anogenital cancers.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Challenges in studying HPVs and the microbiome have hindered progress in defining underlying mechanisms, causality, temporal dynamics, and directionality of HPV-CVM interactions. Evidence gaps remain regarding these unresolved aspects and the specific mechanisms through which the CVM influences HPV pathogenesis.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should focus on addressing outstanding questions through emerging in vitro and in vivo models to better understand trans-kingdom interactions contributing to HPV infection and disease. This includes investigating causality, temporal dynamics, and the directionality of the relationship between the CVM and HPV.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the role of the cervicovaginal microbiome (CVM) as a determinant of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection and disease. High-risk HPVs are established as the cause of nearly one-third of virus-associated cancers, including cervical and other anogenital cancers. While clinical and epidemiological research confirms the CVM's influence on HPV pathogenesis, challenges in studying these interactions have limited progress in defining mechanisms, causality, and temporal dynamics. Emerging models offer opportunities to address these gaps and enhance understanding of trans-kingdom interactions in HPV infection and disease development.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一篇叙述性概述,综合了 宿主 微生物组作为 HPV 发病机制 决定因素的临床和流行病学研究。它不报告具体的数据库、检索日期、资格标准或研究计数,也不采用荟萃分析或共识过程。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 人们一致认为,宿主 微生物组,特别是宫颈阴道微生物组的细菌成分,是 HPV 感染、持续存在和疾病发展的关键决定因素。高危型HPV 被确定为全世界近三分之一的病毒相关癌症的主要原因,包括宫颈癌和其他肛门生殖器癌。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 研究 HPV 和微生物组的挑战阻碍了定义 HPV-CVM 相互作用的潜在机制、因果关系、时间动态和方向性的进展。关于这些未解决的方面以及 CVM 影响 HPV 发病机制 的具体机制,证据仍然存在差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的研究应侧重于通过新兴的体外和体内模型解决突出问题,以更好地了解导致 HPV 感染和疾病的跨界相互作用。这包括调查 CVM 和 HPV 之间关系的因果关系、时间动态以及方向性。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV),特别是它们在引起从皮肤疣到侵袭性癌症等疾病中的作用,重点是具有致癌性并与宫颈癌、肛门生殖器癌和头颈癌相关的 高危型HPV。核心问题是检查宫颈阴道微生物组 (CVM) 如何影响 HPV 感染、持续性和疾病发展。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一篇叙述性概述,综合了 宿主 微生物组作为 HPV 发病机制 决定因素的临床和流行病学研究。它不报告具体的数据库、检索日期、资格标准或研究计数,也不采用荟萃分析或共识过程。

papers.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of diagnostic accuracy of urine self-sampling for human papillomavirus detection in cervical cancer screening
papers.abstract: Objective This review assessed the diagnostic accuracy of urine self-sampling for human papillomavirus (HPV) detection compared with clinician-collected cervical and vaginal samples. Methods A systematic search of PubMed, and Embase (January 2013–October 2023) identified full-text English studies evaluating urine-based HPV testing conducted in clinical settings and compared with provider-collected samples. Data were extracted using a standardised form, with sensitivity and specificity as primary outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and QUADAS-C tools. The review followed PRISMA-P guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024511154). A random-effects meta-analysis summarised diagnostic accuracy. Results Of 1657 citations, 13 studies met the inclusion criteria. Urine sampling showed lower sensitivity for detecting high-risk HPV and high-risk HPV-associated high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) than vaginal samples, although specificities were comparable (87% for urine vs. 88% for vaginal samples). Sensitivity for detecting high-risk HPV-HSIL was 75% for urine, compared with 92% for vaginal and 95% for cervical samples. Cervical samples demonstrated the highest diagnostic accuracy, followed by vaginal samples, while urine samples performed the lowest on the summary receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve. Conclusion Urine self-sampling is a non-invasive and acceptable option but demonstrates reduced sensitivity compared with vaginal and cervical sampling. Despite lower accuracy, its convenience may support screening among women who might otherwise not participate.

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述评估了与临床医生在 宫颈癌 筛查项目中收集的宫颈和阴道样本相比,尿液自我取样检测 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染和 HPV 相关的高级鳞状上皮内病变 (HSIL) 的诊断准确性。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这项系统评价遵循 PRISMA-P 指南,在 PROSPERO 中注册 (CRD42024511154),并检索了 PubMed 和 Embase(2013 年 1 月至 2023 年 10 月)的英文全文研究,比较了基于尿液的 HPV 检测与临床环境中提供者收集的样本。使用 QUADAS-2 和 QUADAS-C 工具评估偏倚风险,并通过随机效应荟萃分析总结诊断准确性。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 宫颈样本在检测 高危型HPV 和 HPV 相关 HSIL 方面表现出最高的诊断准确性,其次是阴道样本,而尿液样本的表现最低。尿液中 高危型HPV-HSIL 的检测灵敏度为 75%,而阴道样本和宫颈样本的灵敏度分别为 92% 和 95%。尿液样本 (87%) 和阴道样本 (88%) 的特异性相当。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调,尽管特异性相当,但与阴道和宫颈取样相比,尿液自我取样检测 高危型HPV 和 HPV 相关 HSIL 的敏感性较低。尿液样本的较低诊断性能引起了人们对其筛查可靠性的担忧。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 对于那些可能不会参与的女性来说,尿液自我采样可能是一种非侵入性且可接受的筛查选择,尽管其敏感性较低。需要进一步研究来优化基于尿液的 HPV 检测方案并提高诊断准确性,以匹配或接近阴道和宫颈采样方法的性能。

papers.title: Behavioral profiles associated with anal HPV infection among MSM attending university in China: a latent class analysis
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a prevalent sexually transmitted infection (STI) among men who have sex with men (MSM) attending university. Our study aimed to identify distinct behavioral profiles for anal HPV infection in this population using Latent Class Analysis (LCA) and assess factors associated with high-risk behavior. METHODS: We recruited MSM attending university in the University Student HIV Test Intervention Study (UniTest Study) between January and April 2019 in China. Participants completed a self-administered online questionnaire on socio-demographic and sexual behavior characteristics. Participants self-collected anal swabs for HPV genotyping. LCA classified individuals into high and low-risk groups for anal HPV infection based on sexual and related risk behaviors. RESULTS: LCA identified two distinct groups among 292 MSM attending university. The class 2 group exhibited a significantly elevated anal HPV infection rate (52.90%, P < 0.001) compared to the class 1 group (25.55%). Notably, the class 2 group was characterized by higher engagement in casual sex (74.15% vs. 42.87%), having non-student sex partners (77.24% vs. 38.22%), involvement in drunken sex in the past year (26.40% vs. 10.90%), Novel Psychoactive Substances (NPS) use sex history (53.13% vs. 12.88%), and a higher prevalence of HIV testing history (98.80% vs. These findings indicate that the higher-risk behavioral profile was associated with a higher observed prevalence of anal HPV infection. CONCLUSION: Our study identified distinct behavioral profiles associated with anal HPV infection among MSM attending university in China. Tailored interventions addressing substance use (alcohol and NPS), sexual health education emphasizing consistent condom use, and the promotion of HPV vaccination within student health programs are warranted. On-campus HPV testing services represent a potentially valuable service model, but their feasibility, acceptability, and integration into existing health infrastructure require further evaluation before routine implementation. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, www.chictr.org.cn : ChiCTR1900020645. Date of Registration: 2019.09.11.

papers.title_zh: 中国大学 MSM 肛门 HPV 感染相关行为特征:潜在类别分析
papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVE: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a prevalent sexually transmitted infection (STI) among men who have sex with men (MSM) attending university. Our study aimed to identify distinct behavioral profiles for anal HPV infection in this population using Latent Class Analysis (LCA) and assess factors associated with high-risk behavior. METHODS: We recruited MSM attending university in the University Student HIV Test Intervention Study (UniTest Study) between January and April 2019 in China. Participants completed a self-administered online questionnaire on socio-demographic and sexual behavior characteristics. Participants self-collected anal swabs for HPV genotyping. LCA classified individuals into high and low-risk groups for anal HPV infection based on sexual and related risk behaviors. RESULTS: LCA identified two distinct groups among 292 MSM attending university. The class 2 group exhibited a significantly elevated anal HPV infection rate (52.90%, P < 0.001) compared to the class 1 group (25.55%). Notably, the class 2 group was characterized by higher engagement in casual sex (74.15% vs. 42.87%), having non-student sex partners (77.24% vs. 38.22%), involvement in drunken sex in the past year (26.40% vs. 10.90%), Novel Psychoactive Substances (NPS) use sex history (53.13% vs. 12.88%), and a higher prevalence of HIV testing history (98.80% vs. These findings indicate that the higher-risk behavioral profile was associated with a higher observed prevalence of anal HPV infection. CONCLUSION: Our study identified distinct behavioral profiles associated with anal HPV infection among MSM attending university in China. Tailored interventions addressing substance use (alcohol and NPS), sexual health education emphasizing consistent condom use, and the promotion of HPV vaccination within student health programs are warranted. On-campus HPV testing services represent a potentially valuable service model, but their feasibility, acceptability, and integration into existing health infrastructure require further evaluation before routine implementation. papers.title: Perceived facilitators and barriers against human papillomavirus vaccine among rural parents with eligible daughters in the Alle district, Southern Ethiopia
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Human papillomavirus vaccine acceptance is influenced by the parental perceptions of the vaccine, but there are few related studies in Ethiopia, and most have focused on quantitative approaches. Therefore, this qualitative study intended to explore parental perceptions about the human papillomavirus vaccine acceptance. OBJECTIVE: To explore the perceived facilitators and barriers against human papillomavirus among rural parents with eligible daughters in the Alle district, southern Ethiopia. METHODS: A qualitative study using focus group discussion and in-depth interviews was conducted from April 25, 2023, to May 25, 2023, among eligible parents of daughters in the Alle district, southern Ethiopia. A convenience sample of 53 parents was recruited for focus group discussions, and 15 parents were purposely sampled for in-depth interviews. The data were collected by a semi-structured focus group discussion guide and in-depth interview questionnaires. The interview data were translated into English after transcription, and thematic analysis was done by Atlas software version 7.1.16. RESULTS: Among the total participants, 66.2% were female parents and 60.2% were protestant religious followers. Findings were split between two major themes: perceived facilitators and barriers to human papillomavirus vaccine acceptance. The perceived facilitators identified were preventing cervical cancer, seeing it as an expression of parental role and responsibility, and believing in the recommendation of health professionals as facilitators of human papillomavirus vaccination. The identified perceived barriers to human papillomavirus vaccination included: a lack of awareness, a lack of reliable information sources, a lack of trust in the vaccine, misconceptions, fear of side effects, and cultural and religious factors affecting the acceptance of human papillomavirus vaccination. CONCLUSION: Parents identified various facilitators and barriers to accepting the human papillomavirus vaccine. Therefore, we recommend that the government and concerned institutions work in collaboration to address the identified challenges to improve the acceptance of human papillomavirus vaccination.

papers.abstract_zh: 简介:人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗 的接受程度受到家长对 疫苗 认知的影响,但埃塞俄比亚的相关研究很少,大多数都集中在定量方法上。因此,本定性研究旨在探讨家长对 人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗 接受的看法。目的:探讨埃塞俄比亚南部阿勒地区有符合条件的女儿的农村父母对 人乳头瘤病毒 的感知促进因素和障碍。方法:2023 年 4 月 25 日至 2023 年 5 月 25 日,对埃塞俄比亚南部阿勒地区符合条件的女儿家长进行了一项定性研究,采用焦点小组讨论和深入访谈的方式进行。我们随机抽取了 53 名家长进行焦点小组讨论,并特意抽取了 15 名家长进行深度访谈。数据通过半结构化焦点小组讨论指南和深度访谈问卷收集。访谈资料转录后翻译成英文,并通过Atlas软件7.1.16版进行主题分析。结果:在所有参与者中,66.2%是女性父母,60.2%是新教信徒。调查结果分为两个主要主题:人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗 接受的感知促进因素和障碍。所确定的感知促进者正在阻止 宫颈癌,将其视为父母角色和责任的表达,并相信卫生专业人员作为 人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗接种 促进者的建议。已确定的 人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗接种 感知障碍包括:缺乏认识、缺乏可靠的信息来源、对 疫苗 缺乏信任、误解、对副作用的恐惧以及影响 人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗接种 接受的文化和宗教因素。结论:家长确定了接受 人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗 的各种促进因素和障碍。因此,我们建议政府和相关机构合作解决已发现的挑战,以提高 人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗接种 的接受度。

papers.title: Type-specific sensitivity versus detection breadth in HPV diagnostics: improved analytical detection of HPV16/18 by nested PCR
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate detection of high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) is central to cervical cancer screening. Current diagnostic strategies increasingly prioritize broad-spectrum assays to maximize genotype coverage. However, theoretical genotype breadth does not necessarily translate into effective sample-level detection when clinically dominant targets are present at low copy number. Here, we evaluated this analytical trade-off using conventional PCR as a controlled experimental framework. Type-specific nested PCR assays targeting HPV16 and HPV18 were developed and applied to 41 cervical samples. Nested PCR showed markedly higher relative analytical sensitivity than single-round amplification and produced a greater proportion of specific and interpretable detections than the broad-spectrum consensus systems tested here (MY09/11 and GP5/6). HPV16 and/or HPV18 DNA was detected by nested PCR in 22/41 samples, whereas MY09/11 and GP5/6 detected 11/41 and 2/41 samples, respectively, under the tested conditions. These findings indicate that broad genotype coverage and effective detection of positive samples are distinct analytical properties. In settings where prevalent HPV targets occur at low abundance, a highly sensitive genotype-focused assay may reveal more target-positive samples than a broader but less sensitive consensus approach. The results are not intended to replace clinically validated broad-spectrum screening assays, but they support explicit preservation of per-target analytical sensitivity in reflex testing and future multi-target HPV assay design.
authors: Beatriz Helena Dantas Rodrigues De Albuquerque
Maryana Thalyta Ferreira Câmara De Oliveira

However, theoretical genotype breadth does not necessarily translate into effective sample-level detection when clinically dominant targets are present at low copy number. Here, we evaluated this analytical trade-off using conventional PCR as a controlled experimental framework. Type-specific nested PCR assays targeting HPV16 and HPV18 were developed and applied to 41 cervical samples. Nested PCR showed markedly higher relative analytical sensitivity than single-round amplification and produced a greater proportion of specific and interpretable detections than the broad-spectrum consensus systems tested here (MY09/11 and GP5/6). HPV16 and/or HPV18 DNA was detected by nested PCR in 22/41 samples, whereas MY09/11 and GP5/6 detected 11/41 and 2/41 samples, respectively, under the tested conditions. These findings indicate that broad genotype coverage and effective detection of positive samples are distinct analytical properties. In settings where prevalent HPV targets occur at low abundance, a highly sensitive genotype-focused assay may reveal more target-positive samples than a broader but less sensitive consensus approach. The results are not intended to replace clinically validated broad-spectrum screening assays, but they support explicit preservation of per-target analytical sensitivity in reflex testing and future multi-target HPV assay design.

papers.title: Occupational human papillomavirus exposure risks for laryngeal surgeons and phoniatricians: A joint European Laryngological Society (ELS) and Union of European Phoniatricians (UEP) Delphi clinical consensus statement
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose Laser surgical management of human papillomavirus (HPV)-related disease, such as recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP), in the upper aerodigestive tract generates surgical smoke, which may represent a source of occupational viral exposure for laryngeal surgeons, phoniatricians, anesthesia providers and scrub nurses. Despite growing awareness, protective measures remain inconsistently implemented. This study aimed to develop an evidence-informed clinical consensus statement (CCS) to guide occupational HPV risk management in laryngology. Methods A modified Delphi consensus process was conducted under the auspices of the European Laryngological Society (ELS) and the Union of the European Phoniatricians (UEP). A panel of 26 international experts undertook three rounds of voting on 18 statements across five domains: definitions and risk perception, personal protective measures, smoke evacuation and ventilation, preventive vaccination, and areas for further research. Results All panellists completed all three rounds. Of the 18 statements, one reached strong consensus, seven reached consensus, one reached near consensus and six did not reach consensus. Three statements were merged across rounds. Key areas of consensus included the recognition of surgical smoke as a potential occupational HPV exposure risk, the inadequacy of standard surgical masks, the importance of offering HPV vaccination to healthcare workers with potential occupational exposure, alongside areas for further research. Conclusion This joint ELS and UEP CCS represents the first internationally coordinated effort to address occupational HPV exposure in laryngology. While consensus was reached in several key areas, the findings underscore the need for targeted research and greater consistency in protective measures, educational provision and regulatory frameworks.

papers.title_zh: 喉外科医生和听力医师的职业 人乳头瘤病毒 暴露风险:欧洲喉科协会 (ELS) 和欧洲听力医师联盟 (UEP) 德尔菲联合临床共识声明
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Purpose Laser surgical management of human papillomavirus (HPV)-related disease, such as recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP), in the upper aerodigestive tract generates surgical smoke, which may represent a source of occupational viral exposure for laryngeal surgeons, phoniatricians, anesthesia providers and scrub nurses. Despite growing awareness, protective measures remain inconsistently implemented. This study aimed to develop an evidence-informed clinical consensus statement (CCS) to guide occupational HPV risk management in laryngology. Methods A modified Delphi consensus process was conducted under the auspices of the European Laryngological Society (ELS) and the Union of the European Phoniatricians (UEP). A panel of 26 international experts undertook three rounds of voting on 18 statements across five domains: definitions and risk perception, personal protective measures, smoke evacuation and ventilation, preventive vaccination, and areas for further research. Results All panellists completed all three rounds. Of the 18 statements, one reached strong consensus, seven reached consensus, one reached near consensus and six did not reach consensus. Three statements were merged across rounds. Key areas of consensus included the recognition of surgical smoke as a potential occupational HPV exposure risk, the inadequacy of standard surgical masks, the importance of offering HPV vaccination to healthcare workers with potential occupational exposure, alongside areas for further research. Conclusion This joint ELS and UEP CCS represents the first internationally coordinated effort to address occupational HPV exposure in laryngology. While consensus was reached in several key areas, the findings underscore the need for targeted research and greater consistency in protective measures, educational provision and regulatory frameworks.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 目的 对上呼吸消化道中的 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 相关疾病(如复发性呼吸道乳头状瘤病 (RRP))进行激光手术治疗时会产生手术烟雾,这可能是喉外科医生、语音科医生、麻醉人员和护士的职业病毒暴露来源。尽管人们的认识不断提高,但保护措施的实施仍然不一致。本研究旨在制定一份循证临床共识声明 (CCS),以指导喉科职业 HPV 风险管理。方法 在欧洲喉科协会 (ELS) 和欧洲语音医师联盟 (UEP) 的支持下进行了修改后的德尔菲共识流程。由 26 名国际专家组成的小组对 18 项声明进行了三轮投票,涉及五个领域:定义和风险认知、个人防护措施、排烟和通风、预防性 疫苗接种 以及进一步研究领域。结果 所有小组成员都完成了全部三轮。18份声明中,1份达成强烈共识,7份达成共识,1份达成接近共识,6份未达成共识。各轮中合并了三份声明。达成共识的关键领域包括认识到手术烟雾是潜在的职业 HPV 暴露风险、标准手术口罩的不足、向可能职业暴露的医护人员提供 HPV 疫苗接种 的重要性,以及需要进一步研究的领域。结论 ELS 和 UEP CCS 联合代表了第一个国际协调行动,旨在解决喉科职业 HPV 暴露问题。虽然在几个关键领域达成了共识,但研究结果强调需要进行有针对性的研究,并在保护措施、教育提供和监管框架方面提高一致性。

papers.title: Attitudes and Knowledge About Human Papillomavirus and Cervical Cancer among Women Referred to a Tertiary Gynecologic Oncology Clinic, Tehran, Iran
papers.abstract: Background & Objective: Cervical cancer is a major public health concern worldwide. This study was conducted with aim to assess the attitudes and knowledge about Human Papillomavirus (HPV) and cervical cancer among women attending a tertiary gynecologic clinic.Materials & Methods: This descriptive, cross-sectional survey was conducted among 139 women referred to the gynecologic clinics of Yas Hospital Complex, affiliated with Tehran University of Medical Sciences, from 2023 to 2024. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews. Data analysis was performed using SPSS (IBM SPSS Statistics for Windows, Version 25). P<0.05 was considered statistically significant.Results: The mean total knowledge score was 25.07±5.92 out of a possible 33 points. Participants demonstrated strong foundational awareness, correctly identifying HPV as a sexually transmitted infection, recognizing that HPV affects both genders, and recognizing its role in causing cervical cancer. However, knowledge of the risks of vertical transmission and the lack of a specific antiviral treatment for HPV was low. Educational attainment was significantly associated with knowledge levels (P=0.01). Indeed, educational attainment was the strongest predictor of knowledge scores.Conclusion: In this clinical setting, basic HPV awareness was high among women. However, substantial misconceptions persisted regarding treatment options, vertical transmission, and vaccination efficacy. These findings highlight an urgent need for educational interventions targeting these knowledge gaps, particularly among women with lower educational attainment. They also underscore the need for structured HPV education and culturally tailored awareness campaigns.

Introduction Cervical cancer is a major public health concern worldwide. It is the fourth most common cancer among women globally. In 2020, about 604 new cases and 342 deaths per 1000 occurred worldwide. Over 85% of these deaths occur in low- and middle-income countries. Preventive strategies, such as Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination and regular screening, remain underused in these areas (1-4). Knowledge gaps and attitudinal barriers continue to impede the implementation of preventive strategies. Among women in Iran, cervical cancer is the tenth most frequent cancer. It is the seventh most common among women aged 15-44 years. There is a lack of a national HPV vaccination program in Iran. Routine cervical cancer screening with Pap smears is not available everywhere (5). Additional barriers include cultural sensitivities around Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) and limited public awareness of HPV. Since knowledge and attitudes directly affect screening behaviors and Elham Shirali, et al. 684 Volume 11, August 2026 Journal of Obstetrics, Gynecology and Cancer Research vaccine acceptance, these factors reduce uptake of preventive measures (6,7). Significant problems include misconceptions about HPV transmission, infection-related stigma, and poor understanding of disease progression. These barriers are particularly strong in conservative societies like Iran. HPV awareness among university students, healthcare workers, and women in urban screening centers has been the focus of previous Iranian research. Ghojazadeh et al., (8) found that although most participants had heard of HPV, medical students in Tabriz had limited detailed knowledge of its transmission and complications. Pooyanmehr and Sarmadi (9) reported similar results in Kermanshah province. Persistent misconceptions about HPV persisted even among educated youth. However, few studies have specifically examined knowledge and attitudes among women actively using gynecologic oncology services. This group is at higher risk for HPV- related diseases and may be undergoing diagnostic or screening procedures. Therefore, the present study was conducted with aims to assess the attitude and knowledge about HPV and cervical cancer among women referred to a gynecological oncology clinic. 2. Materials and Methods This descriptive, cross-sectional survey was conducted among 139 women referred to the gynecologic clinics of Yas Hospital Complex, affiliated with Tehran University of Medical Sciences, from 2023 to 2024. During clinic visits, we recruited participants using non-probability convenience sampling. Women with a prior history of treating cervical lesions (such as cervical surgery and medication), a current pregnancy, prior HPV vaccination, or reluctance to participate in the study were excluded from the study. The sample size was estimated as 139 subjects according to the values reported in Wright et al., (11), a power of 80%, a significance level of 0.05. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews. A structured, previously validated questionnaire was used. The validity and internal consistency of the questionnaire was confirmedas 0.79 by Mojahed et al., (10). Demographic variables (age, marital status, education level, gravidity, parity, smoking/hookah history, and contraceptive methods) were addressed in separate sections. HPV infection knowledge was also assessed. This included its effects on different genders, prevalence and sexual transmission, the role of condom use in decreasing transmission, vertical transmission from mother to baby, related diseases (genital warts and cervical cancer), and knowledge of available treatment and vaccination. Responses were used to assess overall awareness and attitude. Statistical Analysis The data were analyzed using SPSS (IBM SPSS Statistics for Windows, Version 25.0, Armonk, NY). Continuous variables were presented as means±standard deviations. Categorical variables were presented as frequencies and percentages. One-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) was used to compare knowledge scores across categorical variables (education level, marital status). Relationships between continuous variables (age, knowledge score) were assessed using the Pearson correlation coefficient. P<0.05 was considered statistically significant. 3. Results A total of 139 women participated in this study. The mean age of the participants was 36.92±10.00 years, with a range of 15 to 64 years. The largest group of participants (42.45%) held a bachelor's degree or higher. Most were married (69.8%), with a mean gravidity of 1.35±1.38 pregnancies. Most participants (65.5%) did not use contraception, while 23.7% used a condom. Smoking was reported by 10.1% of participants, and hookah use by 23.0%. The mean total knowledge score was 25.07±5.92 out of a maximum possible score of 33 points. Nearly all participants (92.8%) correctly identified HPV as a sexually transmitted infection. About 88% recognized that HPV infection affects both men and women. Knowledge of HPV's clinical implications was notably high. Most participants (83.5%) identified HPV as a cause of cervical cancer in women, and 84.9% knew of its association with genital warts. However, knowledge gaps were evident regarding vertical transmission. Only 42.4% were aware that HPV could be transmitted from mother to child during pregnancy or childbirth. Participants demonstrated a good understanding of prevention methods and risk factors. Most (76.3%) knew that condom use could reduce the risk of HPV transmission. Moreover, 90.6% correctly acknowledged that having multiple sexual partners increases the risk of infection. However, only 57.6% were aware that the early onset of sexual activity increases the risk of HPV infection. Knowledge of HPV treatment was limited. Only 31.7% correctly understood that no specific antiviral treatment exists for HPV infection. About 50% believed such treatment was available, an incorrect belief. Vaccination awareness was relatively high, with 86.3% agreeing that pre-sexual activity vaccination is preferable. However, only 54.0% believed that vaccination remains effective after sexual debut, while 36.0% were uncertain (Figure 1). Correlation analysis between age and overall knowledge score revealed no statistically significant relationship (r= -0.019, P=0.82). However, there was a significant correlation between educational attainment and knowledge levels (P=0.01). Educational attainment emerged as the strongest predictor of HPV knowledge. Women with higher diplomas had the 685 Attitudes and Knowledge about HPV Volume 11, August 2026 Journal of Obstetrics, Gynecology and Cancer Research highest knowledge scores. Across marital status categories, no statistically significant differences were found in knowledge scores (P=0.85) (Table 1). Figure 1. HPV Knowledge and Attitudes Table 1. Discussion The vast majority of participants demonstrated strong foundational HPV knowledge. Moreover, HPV was correctly identified as a sexually transmitted infection by 92.8%, and that it affects both men and women was recognized by 87.8%. These awareness levels are substantially higher than those reported in previous Iranian studies. In a study by Ghojazadeh et al., (8) among medical students in Tabriz found that 76% of students recognized STIs. Similar trends have been reported in international studies. Multiparous women demonstrate greater awareness of reproductive health risks. However, the non-significant association in our study indicates that healthcare providers should not assume that reproductive experience automatically confers HPV knowledge. Instead, these findings support the systematic integration of HPV education into routine maternal care visits (12). Behavioral risk factors revealed patterns linking lifestyle choices with deficits in health knowledge. In the present study, women with a smoking history (10.1%) and hookah use (23.0%) had lower HPV knowledge scores than non-users; however, the difference was not significant in our sample. This trend aligns with established research showing that tobacco users consistently have lower engagement with preventive health services and lower health literacy across multiple domains (13-15). Despite Iran's absence of a national HPV vaccination program, awareness regarding vaccination was high. The vaccine's preventive potential when administered before sexual debut was recognized by 86.3% of participants. This level of awareness suggests effective informal dissemination of health information. This may occur through healthcare providers, the media, or international health sources (16,17). An important association between protective behaviors and HPV knowledge was revealed by contraceptive use patterns. In the present study, women using barrier contraceptives, particularly condoms (23.7%), demonstrated slightly higher knowledge scores than non-users. That condom use reduces HPV transmission risk was correctly understood by 76.3%. This relationship between contraceptive choice and health knowledge likely reflects broader patterns of health-conscious behavior. Sexual health literacy and proactive healthcare engagement extend beyond contraception alone (18,19). However, a critical knowledge gap emerged regarding asymptomatic transmission dynamics. That HPV can be transmitted between carriers was correctly understood by 62.6% of participants in the current research. A concerning 38.8% misunderstood the potential for asymptomatic individuals to transmit the virus. About this mechanism, 30.9% were uncertain. This represents a fundamental misconception with significant implications for prevention behaviors. The majority of HPV infections are asymptomatic. Individuals may unknowingly transmit the virus to partners (20). This study's primary strength lies in its real-world clinical setting. It provides insights into HPV knowledge among women actively engaged in gynecologic care, a population at potentially heightened risk for HPV-related diseases. The use of a validated questionnaire and a comprehensive assessment of sociodemographic factors enhance the reliability and interpretability of the findings. However, several important limitations warrant consideration. The cross-sectional design precludes causal inferences about factors influencing HPV knowledge. Unicentric and the use of convenience sampling limit generalizability. 5. Conclusion Educational attainment emerged as the strongest predictor of HPV knowledge. Women with higher educational degrees scored 13-16% higher than those with a basic education. This underscores education's critical role in health literacy. These findings have immediate clinical implications for Iranian healthcare providers. 6. Declarations Acknowledgments The authors would like to thank all women who participated in the study. Department of Infectious Diseases, Yas Hospital Complex, School of Medicine, Tehran University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran Article Info ABSTRACT 10.24200/jogcr.11.8.683 Background & Objective: Cervical cancer is a major public health concern worldwide. This study was conducted with aim to assess the attitudes and knowledge about Human Papillomavirus (HPV) and cervical cancer among women attending a tertiary gynecologic clinic. Materials & Methods: This descriptive, cross-sectional survey was conducted among 139 women referred to the gynecologic clinics of Yas Hospital Complex, affiliated with Tehran University of Medical Sciences, from 2023 to 2024. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews. Data analysis was performed using SPSS (IBM SPSS Statistics for Windows, Version 25). P<0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results: The mean total knowledge score was 25.07±5.92 out of a possible 33 points. Participants demonstrated strong foundational awareness, correctly identifying HPV as a sexually transmitted infection, recognizing that HPV affects both genders, and recognizing its role in causing cervical cancer. However, knowledge of the risks of vertical transmission and the lack of a specific antiviral treatment for HPV was low. Educational attainment was significantly associated with knowledge levels (P=0.01). Indeed, educational attainment was the strongest predictor of knowledge scores. Conclusion: In this clinical setting, basic HPV awareness was high among women. However, substantial misconceptions persisted regarding treatment options, vertical transmission, and vaccination efficacy. These findings highlight an urgent need for educational interventions targeting these knowledge gaps, particularly among women with lower educational attainment. They also underscore the need for structured HPV education and culturally tailored awareness campaigns. Introduction Cervical cancer is a major public health concern worldwide. It is the fourth most common cancer among women globally. In 2020, about 604 new cases and 342 deaths per 1000 occurred worldwide. Over 85% of these deaths occur in low- and middle-income countries. Preventive strategies, such as Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination and regular screening, remain underused in these areas (1-4). Knowledge gaps and attitudinal barriers continue to impede the implementation of preventive strategies. Among women in Iran, cervical cancer is the tenth most frequent cancer. It is the seventh most common among women aged 15-44 years. There is a lack of a national HPV vaccination program in Iran. Routine cervical cancer screening with Pap smears is not available everywhere (5). Additional barriers include cultural sensitivities around Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) and limited public awareness of HPV. Since knowledge and attitudes directly affect screening behaviors and Elham Shirali, et al. 684 Volume 11, August 2026 Journal of Obstetrics, Gynecology and Cancer Research vaccine acceptance, these factors reduce uptake of preventive measures (6,7). Significant problems include misconceptions about HPV transmission, infection-related stigma, and poor understanding of disease progression. These barriers are particularly strong in conservative societies like Iran. HPV awareness among university students, healthcare workers, and women in urban screening centers has been the focus of previous Iranian research. Ghojazadeh et al., (8) found that although most participants had heard of HPV, medical students in Tabriz had limited detailed knowledge of its transmission and complications. Pooyanmehr and Sarmadi (9) reported similar results in Kermanshah province. Persistent misconceptions about HPV persisted even among educated youth. However, few studies have specifically examined knowledge and attitudes among women actively using gynecologic oncology services. This group is at higher risk for HPV- related diseases and may be undergoing diagnostic or screening procedures. Therefore, the present study was conducted with aims to assess the attitude and knowledge about HPV and cervical cancer among women referred to a gynecological oncology clinic. 2. Materials and Methods This descriptive, cross-sectional survey was conducted among 139 women referred to the gynecologic clinics of Yas Hospital Complex, affiliated with Tehran University of Medical Sciences, from 2023 to 2024. During clinic visits, we recruited participants using non-probability convenience sampling. Women with a prior history of treating cervical lesions (such as cervical surgery and medication), a current pregnancy, prior HPV vaccination, or reluctance to participate in the study were excluded from the study. The sample size was estimated as 139 subjects according to the values reported in Wright et al., (11), a power of 80%, a significance level of 0.05. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews. A structured, previously validated questionnaire was used. The validity and internal consistency of the questionnaire was confirmedas 0.79 by Mojahed et al., (10). Demographic variables (age, marital status, education level, gravidity, parity, smoking/hookah history, and contraceptive methods) were addressed in separate sections. HPV infection knowledge was also assessed. This included its effects on different genders, prevalence and sexual transmission, the role of condom use in decreasing transmission, vertical transmission from mother to baby, related diseases (genital warts and cervical cancer), and knowledge of available treatment and vaccination. Responses were used to assess overall awareness and attitude. Statistical Analysis The data were analyzed using SPSS (IBM SPSS Statistics for Windows, Version 25.0, Armonk, NY). Continuous variables were presented as means±standard deviations. Categorical variables were presented as frequencies and percentages. One-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) was used to compare knowledge scores across categorical variables (education level, marital status). Relationships between continuous variables (age, knowledge score) were assessed using the Pearson correlation coefficient. P<0.05 was considered statistically significant. 3. analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the attitudes and knowledge about Human Papillomavirus (HPV) and cervical cancer among 139 women attending a tertiary gynecologic clinic in Tehran, Iran, between 2023 and 2024. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews and analyzed using SPSS. The mean total knowledge score was 25.07±5.92 out of 33 points, indicating strong foundational awareness of HPV as a sexually transmitted infection and its role in cervical cancer. However, knowledge of the risks of vertical transmission and the lack of a specific antiviral treatment for HPV was low. The evidence strength is moderate due to the cross-sectional design and potential for self-reporting bias.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景和目标:宫颈癌 是全球主要的公共卫生问题。本研究的目的是评估在三级妇科诊所就诊的女性对 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 和 宫颈癌 的态度和知识。材料和方法:这项描述性横断面调查对 2023 年至 2024 年德黑兰医科大学附属亚斯综合医院妇科诊所转诊的 139 名女性进行。数据收集通过面对面采访。使用 SPSS(IBM SPSS Statistics for Windows,版本 25)进行数据分析。P<0.05 被认为具有统计学显着性。结果:平均总知识得分为 25.07±5.92,满分为 33 分。参与者表现出很强的基础意识,正确地将 HPV 识别为性传播感染,认识到 HPV 影响两性,并认识到其在导致 宫颈癌 中的作用。然而,对垂直 传播 风险的了解以及缺乏针对 HPV 的特定 抗病毒药物 治疗 的知识很少。教育程度与知识水平显着相关(P=0.01)。事实上,教育程度是知识得分的最强预测因素。结论:在这种临床环境中,女性对 HPV 的基本认知度较高。然而,对于 治疗 选项、垂直 传播 和 疫苗接种 功效仍然存在严重误解。这些发现凸显了针对这些知识差距的教育干预措施的迫切需要,特别是在教育程度较低的女性中。他们还强调需要进行结构化的 HPV 教育和针对文化的宣传活动。

papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: To investigate whether vaginal dysbiosis is associated with an increased risk of cervical lesions infected with non-16/18 high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) genotypes and to inform risk-stratified cervical cancer screening strategies. METHODS: This cross‐sectional study included 2,264 women attending Jiaxing Maternal and Child Health Hospital between June 2023 and October 2024. HPV genotyping, vaginal microecological assessment, and Thinprep cytologic test (TCT) were performed. HR- HR-HPV infections were classified as HPV16/18-positive or non-16/18 HR-HPV infections. Logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations, adjusting for age. Multiplicative interaction was assessed using Wald tests for product terms. Benjamini‐Hochberg FDR correction was applied for multiple comparisons. RESULTS: The overall HPV prevalence was 49.87%, with HR-HPV detected in 36.13%. HR‐HPV infection was significantly associated with cervical lesions in both normal (OR = 11.45) and dysbiotic (OR = 4.40) vaginal microbiota (both P < 0.001). Stratified analyses showed higher point estimates for HPV58 and HPV59 in the dysbiosis group (OR = 10.98 and 9.51, respectively) than in the normal group (OR = 7.50 and 6.44, respectively). However, formal multiplicative interaction tests did not reach statistical significance (Wald P = 0.526 and 0.559, respectively; FDR‐adjusted q = 0.559 for both). No HPV subtype remained significantly associated with ASC‐US after FDR correction. CONCLUSIONS: In this cross‐sectional study, vaginal dysbiosis is specifically associated with cervical lesions among women with non‐16/18 HR‐HPV infections, particularly HPV58 and HPV59, which showed elevated point estimates in the presence of dysbiosis. However, formal multiplicative interaction tests did not reach statistical significance. These findings are exploratory and hypothesis‐generating; causality cannot be inferred due to the cross‐sectional design. Prospective studies are needed to validate the observed associations before any clinical application can be considered. Our results should be interpreted with caution and do not support changes to current screening practice.

papers.abstract_original: BACKGROUND: To investigate whether vaginal dysbiosis is associated with an increased risk of cervical lesions infected with non-16/18 high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) genotypes and to inform risk-stratified cervical cancer screening strategies. METHODS: This cross‐sectional study included 2,264 women attending Jiaxing Maternal and Child Health Hospital between June 2023 and October 2024. HPV genotyping, vaginal microecological assessment, and Thinprep cytologic test (TCT) were performed. HR- HR-HPV infections were classified as HPV16/18-positive or non-16/18 HR-HPV infections. Logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations, adjusting for age. Multiplicative interaction was assessed using Wald tests for product terms. Benjamini‐Hochberg FDR correction was applied for multiple comparisons. RESULTS: The overall HPV prevalence was 49.87%, with HR-HPV detected in 36.13%. HR‐HPV infection was significantly associated with cervical lesions in both normal (OR = 11.45) and dysbiotic (OR = 4.40) vaginal microbiota (both P < 0.001). Stratified analyses showed higher point estimates for HPV58 and HPV59 in the dysbiosis group (OR = 10.98 and 9.51, respectively) than in the normal group (OR = 7.50 and 6.44, respectively). However, formal multiplicative interaction tests did not reach statistical significance (Wald P = 0.526 and 0.559, respectively; FDR‐adjusted q = 0.559 for both). No HPV subtype remained significantly associated with ASC‐US after FDR correction. CONCLUSIONS: In this cross‐sectional study, vaginal dysbiosis is specifically associated with cervical lesions among women with non‐16/18 HR‐HPV infections, particularly HPV58 and HPV59, which showed elevated point estimates in the presence of dysbiosis. However, formal multiplicative interaction tests did not reach statistical significance. These findings are exploratory and hypothesis‐generating; causality cannot be inferred due to the cross‐sectional design. Prospective studies are needed to validate the observed associations before any clinical application can be considered. Our results should be interpreted with caution and do not support changes to current screening practice.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 旨在调查阴道生态失调是否与感染非 16/18 高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (HR-HPV) 基因型的宫颈病变风险增加相关,并为风险分层 宫颈癌 筛查策略提供信息。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项横断面研究纳入了 2023 年 6 月至 2024 年 10 月期间在嘉兴市妇幼保健院就诊的 2,264 名女性。
elements_zh.methods: 进行了 HPV 基因分型、阴道微生态评估和 Thinprep 细胞学检测 (TCT)。使用逻辑回归模型来评估关联性,并根据年龄进行调整。使用乘积项的 Wald 检验评估乘法交互作用,并应用 Benjamini-Hochberg FDR 校正进行多重比较。
elements_zh.main_results: HPV 患病率 总体检出率为 49.87%,其中 HR-HPV 检出率为 36.13%。在正常 (OR = 11.45) 和失调 (OR = 4.40) 阴道微生物群中,HR-HPV 感染与宫颈病变显着相关(均 P < 0.001)。分层分析显示,生态失调组中 HPV58 和 HPV59 的点估计值(分别为 OR = 10.98 和 9.51)高于正常组(分别为 OR = 7.50 和 6.44),但正式的乘性相互作用检验并未达到统计显着性(分别为 Wald P = 0.526 和 0.559;两者的 FDR 调整 q = 0.559)。FDR 校正后,没有 HPV 亚型与 ASC-US 保持显着相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在这项横断面研究中,阴道菌群失调与非 16/18 HR-HPV 感染女性的宫颈病变特别相关,特别是 HPV58 和 HPV59,在存在菌群失调的情况下,点估计值升高。然而,正式的乘性交互作用检验并未达到统计学显着性,并且研究结果是探索性的和假设生成的;由于横截面设计,无法推断因果关系。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能会为风险分层的 宫颈癌 筛查策略提供信息,特别是对于非 16/18 HR-HPV 感染和阴道生态失调的女性,但在考虑任何临床应用之前,需要进行前瞻性研究来验证观察到的关联。结果应谨慎解释,并且不支持对当前筛查实践的改变。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 横断面设计限制了因果推断,研究结果的探索性需要在前瞻性研究中进行验证。由于样本量大和严格的统计调整,证据强度中等,但缺乏显着的相互作用测试和横截面设计降低了建立因果关系的信心。

papers.title: Effects of a Message‐Framing Video Intervention on Maternal Vaccine Confidence Regarding HPV Vaccination for Daughters: A Quasi‐Experimental Study Among Mothers With Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Increasing HPV vaccination coverage is pivotal, necessitating effective vaccination strategies. This research assessed the impact of a message‐framing (MF) video intervention on boosting vaccine confidence among mothers diagnosed with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), targeting HPV vaccination for their daughters. Methods Conducted from January to June 2024, this interventional study took place at the gynecological cervical clinic of a university‐affiliated hospital and targeted CIN patients from adjacent communities. Mothers with daughters aged 9–14 years, who were unvaccinated and whose mothers were diagnosed with CIN, participated. They were allocated to receive either standard health education or a targeted message‐framing video intervention. Outcome data were collected by trained researchers after a 10‐week intervention period, focusing on maternal knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors toward their daughters’ HPV vaccination. Results A total of 101 patients were analyzed. Those exposed to the message‐framing video intervention exhibited significantly improved knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors towards HPV vaccination ( Z = −3.376, P = 0.001), and demonstrated lower vaccine hesitancy scores ( Z = −2.924, P = 0.003) compared to their counterparts receiving standard health education. However, differences in the rates of scheduling vaccine appointments were not statistically significant between the groups ( χ 2 = 0.934, P = 0.334). Conclusions The message‐framing video intervention significantly enhanced vaccine confidence by improving the knowledge and willingness of CIN patients to vaccinate their daughters against HPV. Further studies are required to explore the intervention's influence on actual vaccination rates.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 增加 HPV 疫苗接种 覆盖率至关重要,需要有效的 疫苗接种 策略。这项研究评估了信息框架视频干预对增强被诊断患有宫颈上皮内瘤变 (CIN) 的母亲的 疫苗 信心的影响,针对其女儿的 HPV 疫苗接种。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项介入研究于2024年1月至6月进行,在一所大学附属医院的妇科宫颈诊所进行,针对来自邻近社区的CIN患者。有 9 至 14 岁女儿、未接种疫苗且母亲被诊断患有 CIN 的母亲参加了这项活动。
elements_zh.methods: 他们被分配接受标准健康教育或有针对性的信息框架视频干预。结果数据由经过培训的研究人员在 10 周干预期后收集,重点关注母亲对其女儿 HPV 疫苗接种 的了解、态度和行为。
elements_zh.main_results: 总共分析了 101 名患者。与接受标准健康教育的人相比,接受信息框架视频干预的人对 HPV 疫苗接种 的知识、态度和行为显着改善(Z = -3.376,P = 0.001),并且 疫苗 犹豫得分较低(Z = -2.924,P = 0.003)。然而,各组之间安排 疫苗 预约的比率差异不具有统计学意义(χ2 = 0.934,P = 0.334)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 消息框架视频干预通过提高 CIN 患者为其女儿接种 HPV 疫苗的知识和意愿,显着增强了 疫苗 的信心。需要进一步研究来探索干预措施对实际 疫苗接种 率的影响。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,消息框架干预措施可以有效提高高危人群对 疫苗 的信心,可能有助于增加 HPV 疫苗接种 覆盖率。这种方法对于患有 CIN 的母亲可能特别有价值,因为她们可能提高了对 HPV 相关风险的认识。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是准实验性的,并没有证明各组之间实际的 疫苗接种 预约安排存在显着差异。由于研究设计和缺乏实际 疫苗接种 率的长期随访数据,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Nonavalent HPV vaccination induces robust systemic and mucosal HPV16-neutralizing antibody responses in previously infected women
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Neutralizing antibody responses to human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines are typically assessed in serum, while mucosal immunity at sites of infection remains less well characterized, particularly in HPV-positive individuals. We evaluated systemic and mucosal HPV16-neutralizing antibody responses following nonavalent HPV vaccination in women with a recent HPV16/18-positive cervical test. Methods In this longitudinal RIFT-HPV study, 39 previously unvaccinated adult women with an HPV16/18-positive cervical test done in the previous 12 months received a three-dose schedule of the nonavalent HPV vaccine (Gardasil-9). Paired serum, cervical, and oral samples were collected before and during vaccination. Neutralizing activity against HPV16 pseudovirions was measured using an enhanced green fluorescent protein pseudovirion-based neutralization assay (EGFP-PBNA). Results Vaccination significantly increased HPV16-neutralizing antibody responses in serum, cervical, and oral samples, irrespective of baseline HPV16 positivity. Serum EC 50 detection increased from 33% at baseline to 100% after three doses, while cervical and oral detection increased from 8% and 10% after one dose, to 100% and 80% after three doses, respectively. With assay conditions exceeding physiological viral exposure levels, cervical HPV16 pseudovirion neutralization progressively increased from 36% before vaccination to 61%, 68% and 78% after one, two and three vaccine doses, respectively. Systemic and mucosal neutralizing responses were positively correlated. The EGFP-PBNA demonstrated high reproducibility (ICC = 0.98) and good concordance with the reference method. Conclusions Nonavalent HPV vaccination induced strong systemic and mucosal HPV16-neutralizing antibody responses, regardless of current HPV16 positivity. These findings demonstrate enhanced mucosal HPV16-neutralizing immunity following nonavalent vaccination in previously infected women and support further investigation of its potential role in reducing viral infectivity and transmission. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05334706. Registered on 19 April 2022.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估最近进行 HPV16/18 阳性宫颈检测的女性在非价 HPV 疫苗接种 后的全身和粘膜 HPV16 中和抗体反应,因为对 HPV 疫苗 的中和抗体反应通常在血清中评估,而粘膜免疫的特征仍然较少,特别是在 HPV 阳性个体中。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一项纵向 RIFT-HPV 研究,对象是 39 名之前未接种疫苗、在过去 12 个月内宫颈检测呈 HPV16/18 阳性的成年女性,她们接受了三剂非价 HPV 疫苗 (Gardasil-9)。
elements_zh.methods: 在 疫苗接种 之前和期间收集配对血清、宫颈和口腔样本。使用增强型绿色荧光蛋白假病毒体中和测定 (EGFP-PBNA) 测量针对 HPV16 假病毒体的中和活性,测定条件超过生理病毒暴露水平。
elements_zh.main_results: 无论基线 HPV16 阳性程度如何,疫苗接种 均显着增加血清、宫颈和口腔样本中的 HPV16 中和抗体反应。血清 EC 50 检测从基线时的 33% 增加到三剂后的 100%,而宫颈和口腔检测分别从一剂后的 8% 和 10% 增加到三剂后的 100% 和 80%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,无论当前 HPV16 阳性如何,非价 HPV 疫苗接种 都会诱导强烈的全身和粘膜 HPV16 中和抗体反应,这是一个新颖的发现,因为它证明了 疫苗 对先前感染的女性的有效性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持粘膜 HPV16 中和免疫在降低病毒感染性和 传播 方面的潜在作用,这可以为未来 HPV 监测、诊断 和预防策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于单个中心和相对较小的样本量,但证据充足,因为它基于配对样本的纵向设计和可重复的测定方法(ICC = 0.98)。

papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Neutralizing antibody responses to human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines are typically assessed in serum, while mucosal immunity at sites of infection remains less well characterized, particularly in HPV-positive individuals. We evaluated systemic and mucosal HPV16-neutralizing antibody responses following nonavalent HPV vaccination in women with a recent HPV16/18-positive cervical test. Methods In this longitudinal RIFT-HPV study, 39 previously unvaccinated adult women with an HPV16/18-positive cervical test done in the previous 12 months received a three-dose schedule of the nonavalent HPV vaccine (Gardasil-9). Paired serum, cervical, and oral samples were collected before and during vaccination. Neutralizing activity against HPV16 pseudovirions was measured using an enhanced green fluorescent protein pseudovirion-based neutralization assay (EGFP-PBNA). Results Vaccination significantly increased HPV16-neutralizing antibody responses in serum, cervical, and oral samples, irrespective of baseline HPV16 positivity. Serum EC 50 detection increased from 33% at baseline to 100% after three doses, while cervical and oral detection increased from 8% and 10% after one dose, to 100% and 80% after three doses, respectively. With assay conditions exceeding physiological viral exposure levels, cervical HPV16 pseudovirion neutralization progressively increased from 36% before vaccination to 61%, 68% and 78% after one, two and three vaccine doses, respectively. Systemic and mucosal neutralizing responses were positively correlated. The EGFP-PBNA demonstrated high reproducibility (ICC = 0.98) and good concordance with the reference method. Conclusions Nonavalent HPV vaccination induced strong systemic and mucosal HPV16-neutralizing antibody responses, regardless of current HPV16 positivity. These findings demonstrate enhanced mucosal HPV16-neutralizing immunity following nonavalent vaccination in previously infected women and support further investigation of its potential role in reducing viral infectivity and transmission. papers.title: Trends in incidence and medical costs of human papillomavirus–related diseases in Korea: evidence from National Health Insurance claims
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is a major cause of cervical, anal and oropharyngeal cancers. Although Korea has implemented a national HPV vaccination programme since 2016, nationwide evidence on incidence trends and medical costs of HPV-related diseases remains limited. METHODS: This retrospective population-based study analysed Korean National Health Insurance Service claims data. Age-standardised incidence (ASI) rates of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN1 and CIN2/3), genital warts (GWs), and cervical, oropharyngeal and anal cancers from 2015 to 2022 were calculated using the 2022 Korean population as the standard. Trends in ASI were analysed using Joinpoint regression with a piecewise log-linear (Poisson) model. For diseases with and without statistically significant Joinpoints, trends were reported using pre-identified and post-identified segment-specific annual percentage changes (APCs) and the average annual percentage change (AAPC), respectively. Trends in total medical costs from 2015 to 2021 were evaluated using linear regression. RESULTS: ASI trends differed by sex and disease type. Cervical cancer incidence among females declined significantly during 2015-2022 (AAPC; -4.2%, p<0.001). Joinpoint regression identified significant inflection points in 2019 for both female and male GWs. Female GW incidence increased during 2015-2019 (APC; 3.7%, p=0.010) and then decreased significantly during 2019-2022 (APC; -14.0%, p<0.001). Male GW incidence increased significantly during 2015-2019 (APC; 11.3%, p<0.001) and then showed no statistically significant change during 2019-2022 (APC; 1.4%, p=0.290). CONCLUSIONS: These descriptive findings provide population-level evidence on HPV-associated disease burden in Korea but cannot establish causal attribution to vaccination, screening or other preventive interventions, necessitating continued surveillance with individual-level data linkage.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染是宫颈癌、肛门癌和口咽癌的主要原因。尽管韩国自 2016 年以来实施了国家 HPV 发病率 计划,但全国范围内有关 HPV 相关疾病的 发病率 趋势和医疗费用的证据仍然有限。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项基于人群的回顾性研究分析了韩国国民健康保险局的索赔数据。
elements_zh.methods: 以2022年韩国人口为标准,计算2015年至2022年宫颈上皮内瘤变(CIN1和CIN2/3)、尖锐湿疣(GW)以及宫颈癌、口咽癌和肛门癌的年龄标准化发病率(ASI)率。使用带有分段对数线性(泊松)模型的连接点回归来分析 ASI 的趋势。使用线性回归评估 2015 年至 2021 年总医疗费用的趋势。
elements_zh.main_results: ASI 趋势因性别和疾病类型而异。2015 年至 2022 年期间,女性中的 宫颈癌 发病率 显着下降(AAPC;-4.2%,p<0.001)。女性 GW 发病率 在 2015-2019 年期间有所增加(APC;3.7%,p=0.010),然后在 2019-2022 年期间显着下降(APC;-14.0%,p<0.001)。男性 GW 发病率 在 2015-2019 年期间显着增加(APC;11.3%,p<0.001),然后在 2019-2022 年期间没有显示出统计上显着的变化(APC;1.4%,p=0.290)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些描述性研究结果提供了韩国 HPV 相关疾病负担的人群水平证据,但无法确定 疫苗接种、筛查或其他预防性干预措施的因果归因,因此需要继续进行 监测 与个人水平的数据链接。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果通过记录 HPV 相关疾病和医疗费用的趋势,为 监测 和预防策略提供信息,强调需要持续监测以评估干预措施的影响。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其描述性性质和无法建立因果归因而受到限制,因为它依赖于没有个人层面联系的索赔数据。由于基于人口的数据集很大,但观察设计存在固有的局限性,证据强度中等。

Trends in ASI were analysed using Joinpoint regression with a piecewise log-linear (Poisson) model. For diseases with and without statistically significant Joinpoints, trends were reported using pre-identified and post-identified segment-specific annual percentage changes (APCs) and the average annual percentage change (AAPC), respectively. Trends in total medical costs from 2015 to 2021 were evaluated using linear regression. RESULTS: ASI trends differed by sex and disease type. Cervical cancer incidence among females declined significantly during 2015-2022 (AAPC; -4.2%, p<0.001). Joinpoint regression identified significant inflection points in 2019 for both female and male GWs. Female GW incidence increased during 2015-2019 (APC; 3.7%, p=0.010) and then decreased significantly during 2019-2022 (APC; -14.0%, p<0.001). Male GW incidence increased significantly during 2015-2019 (APC; 11.3%, p<0.001) and then showed no statistically significant change during 2019-2022 (APC; 1.4%, p=0.290).
