papers.title: Prevalence, genotype distribution, and viral load characteristics of high-risk HPV infection among 42,379 women in Beijing, China: a retrospective study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection is a necessary cause of cervical cancer, while its prevalence and genotype distribution show substantial regional variation. This study aimed to characterize HR-HPV infection among women in Beijing and provide region-specific epidemiological evidence for local prevention strategies. Methods This retrospective analysis included 42,379 women who underwent cervical HPV genotyping at Dongzhimen Hospital, Beijing University of Chinese Medicine, from March 2016 to December 2024. Fifteen HR-HPV genotypes were detected using fluorescent PCR. Age-specific infection patterns were assessed across seven age groups, and viral load was categorized into three levels. The study period was divided into three phases based on the temporal progression of the COVID-19 outbreak: pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic. Results The overall HR-HPV prevalence was 19.91% (8,438/42,379). HPV52 (20.17%), HPV58 (12.61%), and HPV16 (11.84%) were the most common genotypes. Single-type infections predominated (75.09%), while multiple-type infections accounted for 24.91%, with HPV52 + HPV58, HPV52 + HPV16, and HPV52 + HPV51 being the most frequent combinations. Age distribution showed a bimodal pattern, with peaks at 20–29 years (38.53%) and 60–69 years (29.55%). Moderate viral load was most common (40.08%); HPV31 and HPV16 had the highest proportions of high viral loads, while HPV52 displayed a "high prevalence–low viral load" pattern. High viral load proportion increased with infection complexity. Annual prevalence ranged from 17.9% to 22.0%, with the lowest rate in 2020. Across pandemic phases, overall prevalence was 20.53%, 19.40%, and 19.88%, while multiple-type infection rates declined consecutively from 27.39% to 21.65%. Conclusions HR-HPV infection in Beijing women is characterized by predominance of HPV52, HPV58, and HPV16, a bimodal age distribution, and genotype-specific viral load profiles. The pandemic-associated decline in overall prevalence and sustained decrease in multiple-type infections underscore the importance of targeted vaccination and screening strategies in the post-pandemic era.

papers.title: '...but look how many lives would have been saved if this was available then' Exploring the acceptability of future Human Papillomavirus self-sampling, and the barriers and facilitators of cervical cancer screening for those with intellectual disabilities in Scotland.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer screening attendance among women with intellectual disabilities (ID) in Scotland is approximately 30%, significantly below the general population rate of 69% and the WHO's recommended 70% target. HPV self-sampling could provide a more accessible screening option for this underserved population. This study aimed to understand the views and experiences of women with ID regarding cervical cancer screening and the acceptability of HPV self-sampling. METHODS: A qualitative study using focus groups was conducted with women with ID who attended third-sector community groups across Scotland, along with their carers. Four focus groups were held between September and October 2024, with a total of 13 participants (11 women with ID, 2 carers). Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. RESULTS: Five main themes emerged: (1) National Health Service (NHS) communication as a source of distress; (2) power imbalances between health care providers and women with ID: feeling unheard, dismissed and out of control; (3) enduring consequences of inadequate care; (4) past trauma shapes future avoidance; and (5) self-sampling as a pathway to empowerment. Participants demonstrated high acceptability of self-sampling, viewing it as a potential solution to overcome barriers to traditional screening. CONCLUSION: This research reveals significant systemic inadequacies in current cervical cancer screening services for women with ID, whilst highlighting self-sampling's transformative potential. Successful implementation requires comprehensive accessible information, enhanced health care professional training and trauma-informed care approaches. Self-sampling could significantly advance health equity goals whilst improving health care outcomes for this underserved population.

papers.title_zh: '...but look how many lives would have been saved if this was available then' 探讨未来人乳头瘤病毒自我采样的可接受性,以及苏格兰智力障碍人群进行宫颈癌筛查的障碍与促进因素
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer screening attendance among women with intellectual disabilities (ID) in Scotland is approximately 30%, significantly below the general population rate of 69% and the WHO's recommended 70% target. HPV self-sampling could provide a more accessible screening option for this underserved population. This study aimed to understand the views and experiences of women with ID regarding cervical cancer screening and the acceptability of HPV self-sampling. METHODS: A qualitative study using focus groups was conducted with women with ID who attended third-sector community groups across Scotland, along with their carers. Four focus groups were held between September and October 2024, with a total of 13 participants (11 women with ID, 2 carers). Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. RESULTS: Five main themes emerged: (1) National Health Service (NHS) communication as a source of distress; (2) power imbalances between health care providers and women with ID: feeling unheard, dismissed and out of control; (3) enduring consequences of inadequate care; (4) past trauma shapes future avoidance; and (5) self-sampling as a pathway to empowerment. Participants demonstrated high acceptability of self-sampling, viewing it as a potential solution to overcome barriers to traditional screening. CONCLUSION: This research reveals significant systemic inadequacies in current cervical cancer screening services for women with ID, whilst highlighting self-sampling's transformative potential. Successful implementation requires comprehensive accessible information, enhanced health care professional training and trauma-informed care approaches. Self-sampling could significantly advance health equity goals whilst improving health care outcomes for this underserved population.

papers.title: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma associated with cosmetic skin bleaching: Histological characteristics and the possible role of human papillomavirus
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The occurrence and clinical characteristics of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) associated with cosmetic skin bleaching have been well documented in the literature. However, the histopathological characteristics have not yet been reported. This study aimed to describe the histological abnormalities observed in cases of cSCC associated with cosmetic skin bleaching and to explore the potential contributing factors. METHODS: We re-analysed archived paraffin-embedded tissue blocks from all cases of cSCC diagnosed in different pathology laboratories in Dakar between November 2006 and October 2021. RESULTS: We collected 19 cases of cSCC, all occurring in women, with a mean age of 58 years. On average, the women had been practising cosmetic skin bleaching for 20 years. Most of them (14 cases) used bleaching products containing a mixture of hydroquinone and clobetasol propionate. All carcinomas were well-differentiated, and 17 cases (89.5%) were invasive. Histological abnormalities associated with the cSCC included intense fibrosis with a lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate in all cases, telangiectasias in 18 cases (94.7%), exogenous ochronosis deposits in 9 cases (47.4%), and solar elastosis in one case. In addition, koilocytes, histological markers of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, were identified in 10 cases (52.6%). CONCLUSION: cSCC associated with cosmetic skin bleaching exhibit a distinctive histopathological pattern with frequent koilocytosis (52.6%). These findings support a multifactorial pathogenesis in which HPV may act as a cofactor. Future studies using PCR and in situ hybridisation are needed to clarify this potential association.
papers.journal: Annales de Dermatologie et de Vénéréologie

papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: The occurrence and clinical characteristics of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) associated with cosmetic skin bleaching have been well documented in the literature. However, the histopathological characteristics have not yet been reported. This study aimed to describe the histological abnormalities observed in cases of cSCC associated with cosmetic skin bleaching and to explore the potential contributing factors. METHODS: We re-analysed archived paraffin-embedded tissue blocks from all cases of cSCC diagnosed in different pathology laboratories in Dakar between November 2006 and October 2021. RESULTS: We collected 19 cases of cSCC, all occurring in women, with a mean age of 58 years. On average, the women had been practising cosmetic skin bleaching for 20 years. Most of them (14 cases) used bleaching products containing a mixture of hydroquinone and clobetasol propionate. All carcinomas were well-differentiated, and 17 cases (89.5%) were invasive. Histological abnormalities associated with the cSCC included intense fibrosis with a lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate in all cases, telangiectasias in 18 cases (94.7%), exogenous ochronosis deposits in 9 cases (47.4%), and solar elastosis in one case. In addition, koilocytes, histological markers of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, were identified in 10 cases (52.6%). CONCLUSION: cSCC associated with cosmetic skin bleaching exhibit a distinctive histopathological pattern with frequent koilocytosis (52.6%). These findings support a multifactorial pathogenesis in which HPV may act as a cofactor. Future studies using PCR and in situ hybridisation are needed to clarify this potential association.

papers.title: Efficient high-risk human papillomavirus screening through pooled testing: a simulation study based on real-world data in low- and middle-income countries
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The World Health Organization recommends high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) testing as the primary method for cervical cancer screening. Combining samples in a pool can reduce the expense associated with large numbers of commercially available tests. This study simulated the potential test-saving impact of pooled hrHPV testing using real-world data from two low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). METHODS: We simulated a two- and three-stage hrHPV pooling in Bangladesh (hrHPV prevalence 2.10%) and Uganda (hrHPV prevalence 22.52%) using real-world laboratory data. Measurements included the number of tests per stage, the total number of tests, and the percentage of tests saved. We performed sensitivity analysis to assess the impact of a 1.00% loss of sensitivity and specificity per additional sample in the pool on the false-negative rate (FNR). RESULTS: In Bangladesh, the two-stage strategy (eight samples per pool) and the three-stage strategy saved 71.21% and 77.21% of tests, respectively, compared to testing individually. In Uganda, the two-stage strategy (three samples per pool) reduced the number of tests by 15.34% compared to testing individually. Assuming loss of sensitivity and specificity due to pooling, the FNR was higher (FNR = 0.012-0.134) when hrHPV prevalence was low under the two-stage strategy. CONCLUSIONS: Pooled hrHPV testing has the potential to reduce the number of tests used and enhance screening capacity in resource-limited settings. Notably, a lower prevalence of hrHPV allows for more efficient pooled testing. Despite the potential loss of sensitivity and specificity, pooled hrHPV testing could offer benefits for LMICs and warrant further verification.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项研究使用来自两个低收入和中等收入国家 (LMIC) 的真实数据模拟了合并 hrHPV 检测的潜在测试节省影响。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 合并 hrHPV 检测可以通过降低检测成本和提高筛查能力为低收入和中等收入国家带来好处,尽管可能会损失敏感性和特异性,但仍需要进一步验证。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是基于真实世界数据的模拟,由于合并可能会损失敏感性和特异性,因此证据强度中等,这可能会影响假阴性率,特别是在低 患病率 设置中。

papers.title: Rewired DDR-TGF-β-β-catenin-PD-L1 axis accelerates progression and shapes therapy in human papillomavirus-driven cancer
papers.abstract: Understanding Human papillomavirus (HPV) oncogenic mechanisms is essential for developing preventive and therapeutic strategies and overcoming therapy resistance in HPV-related cancers. These challenges may arise from the ability of high-risk HPV to subvert host tumor suppressors such as p53 and Rb, and to drive oncogenesis through homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) and multi-network dysregulation. Mechanistically, HPV exerts context-dependent effects on the host DNA damage response (DDR). During episomal replication, E6/E7 activate DDR and recruit BRCA1/RAD51 to replication foci to support viral replication without significantly compromising host HR repair. Upon viral integration, however, sustained E6/E7 expression drives HRD and shifts DNA repair toward error-prone end joining, generating genomic instability that fuels malignant transformation. These alterations are most clearly established in cervical cancer, whereas evidence in HPV-positive non-cervical cancer is more variable and requires further context-specific validation. In parallel, HPV E6/E7 antagonize transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β)-mediated tumor suppression and, potentially through FAT Atypical Cadherin 4 (FAT4) down-regulation, engage Wnt/β-catenin signaling. The resultant elevation of nuclear β-catenin induces programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression promotes immune evasion, stemness, and invasiveness. Of note, while the DDR-TGF-β-β-catenin-PD-L1 axis is backed by substantial evidence in HPV-related cancers, certain connections within this pathway are extrapolated from non-HPV models or general pathway biology and are explicitly denoted as such in the main text. With residual p53 activity, HRD may confer initial sensitivity to DNA-damaging agents, but resistance frequently develops—a pattern reminiscent of the initial response followed by acquired resistance observed with immunotherapies in HPV-related cancers. Integrating these mechanistic insights, we propose ablative therapies (e.g., ablation, photodynamic therapy, surgery) for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), and for advanced or resistant disease, a synthetic-lethality framework combining genotoxic therapies with DDR inhibitors, targeting DDR-TGF-β-β-catenin-PD-L1 axis, and antiviral approaches. The proposed therapeutic strategies, however, should be interpreted with caution, as their evidence base varies across tumor types and warrants further investigation.

analysis.study_design_and_population: These challenges may arise from the ability of high-risk HPV to subvert host tumor suppressors such as p53 and Rb, and to drive oncogenesis through homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) and multi-network dysregulation.
analysis.methods: Mechanistically, HPV exerts context-dependent effects on the host DNA damage response (DDR).
analysis.main_results: During episomal replication, E6/E7 activate DDR and recruit BRCA1/RAD51 to replication foci to support viral replication without significantly compromising host HR repair. Upon viral integration, however, sustained E6/E7 expression drives HRD and shifts DNA repair toward error-prone end joining, generating genomic instability that fuels malignant transformation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These alterations are most clearly established in cervical cancer, whereas evidence in HPV-positive non-cervical cancer is more variable and requires further context-specific validation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Integrating these mechanistic insights, we propose ablative therapies (e.g., ablation, photodynamic therapy, surgery) for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), and for advanced or resistant disease, a synthetic-lethality framework combining genotoxic therapies with DDR inhibitors, targeting DDR-TGF-β-β-catenin-PD-L1 axis, and antiviral approaches.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The proposed therapeutic strategies, however, should be interpreted with caution, as their evidence base varies across tumor types and warrants further investigation.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the oncogenic mechanisms of human papillomavirus (HPV), focusing on its role in subverting host tumor suppressors and driving genomic instability through DDR and multi-network dysregulation. It highlights the context-dependent effects of HPV on the DNA damage response (DDR), particularly during episomal replication and viral integration. The research identifies the DDR-TGF-β-β-catenin-PD-L1 axis as a key pathway in HPV-related cancers, with implications for therapeutic strategies such as ablative therapies and synthetic-lethality approaches. However, the evidence base for these strategies varies across tumor types, necessitating further investigation. The findings emphasize the need for context-specific validation, especially in non-cervical HPV-positive cancers, and underscore the importance of understanding HPV's impact on immune evasion and malignant transformation.

papers.title_zh: 重新连线的 DDR-TGF-β-β-连环蛋白-PD-L1 轴可加速 人乳头瘤病毒 驱动的癌症的进展并塑造治疗方法
papers.source_body_en: Understanding Human papillomavirus (HPV) oncogenic mechanisms is essential for developing preventive and therapeutic strategies and overcoming therapy resistance in HPV-related cancers. These challenges may arise from the ability of high-risk HPV to subvert host tumor suppressors such as p53 and Rb, and to drive oncogenesis through homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) and multi-network dysregulation. Mechanistically, HPV exerts context-dependent effects on the host DNA damage response (DDR). During episomal replication, E6/E7 activate DDR and recruit BRCA1/RAD51 to replication foci to support viral replication without significantly compromising host HR repair. Upon viral integration, however, sustained E6/E7 expression drives HRD and shifts DNA repair toward error-prone end joining, generating genomic instability that fuels malignant transformation. These alterations are most clearly established in cervical cancer, whereas evidence in HPV-positive non-cervical cancer is more variable and requires further context-specific validation. In parallel, HPV E6/E7 antagonize transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β)-mediated tumor suppression and, potentially through FAT Atypical Cadherin 4 (FAT4) down-regulation, engage Wnt/β-catenin signaling. The resultant elevation of nuclear β-catenin induces programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression promotes immune evasion, stemness, and invasiveness. Of note, while the DDR-TGF-β-β-catenin-PD-L1 axis is backed by substantial evidence in HPV-related cancers, certain connections within this pathway are extrapolated from non-HPV models or general pathway biology and are explicitly denoted as such in the main text. With residual p53 activity, HRD may confer initial sensitivity to DNA-damaging agents, but resistance frequently develops—a pattern reminiscent of the initial response followed by acquired resistance observed with immunotherapies in HPV-related cancers. Integrating these mechanistic insights, we propose ablative therapies (e.g., ablation, photodynamic therapy, surgery) for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), and for advanced or resistant disease, a synthetic-lethality framework combining genotoxic therapies with DDR inhibitors, targeting DDR-TGF-β-β-catenin-PD-L1 axis, and antiviral approaches. The proposed therapeutic strategies, however, should be interpreted with caution, as their evidence base varies across tumor types and warrants further investigation.
papers.abstract_zh: 了解 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 致癌机制对于制定预防和治疗策略以及克服 HPV 相关癌症的治疗耐药性至关重要。这些挑战可能源于 高危型HPV 颠覆 宿主 肿瘤抑制因子(如 p53 和 Rb)的能力,并通过同源重组缺陷(HRD)和多网络失调驱动肿瘤发生。从机制上讲,HPV 对 宿主 DNA 损伤反应 (DDR) 产生环境依赖性影响。在附加型复制过程中,E6/E7 激活 DDR 并将 BRCA1/RAD51 招募到复制灶以支持病毒复制,而不会显着损害 宿主 HR 修复。然而,在病毒整合后,持续的 E6/E7 表达会驱动 HRD 并将 DNA 修复转向容易出错的末端连接,从而产生基因组不稳定,从而加剧恶性转化。这些改变在 宫颈癌 中最为明确,而 HPV 阳性非 宫颈癌 中的证据变化更大,需要进一步针对具体情况进行验证。与此同时,HPV E6/E7 拮抗转化生长因子-β (TGF-β) 介导的肿瘤抑制,并可能通过 FAT 非典型钙粘蛋白 4 (FAT4) 下调,参与 Wnt/β-连环蛋白信号传导。由此产生的核 β-连环蛋白升高会诱导程序性死亡配体 1 (PD-L1) 表达,从而促进免疫逃避、干性和侵袭性。值得注意的是,虽然 DDR-TGF-β-β-连环蛋白-PD-L1 轴得到 HPV 相关癌症的大量证据支持,但该通路内的某些联系是从非 HPV 模型或一般通路生物学推断出来的,并在正文中明确指出。凭借残留的 p53 活性,HRD 可能会赋予对 DNA 损伤剂的初始敏感性,但经常会产生耐药性,这种模式让人想起在 HPV 相关癌症的免疫疗法中观察到的初始反应,然后是获得性耐药。整合这些机制见解,我们提出了针对宫颈上皮内瘤变 (CIN) 的消融疗法(例如消融、光动力疗法、手术),以及针对晚期或耐药性疾病,提出了一种将基因毒性疗法与 DDR 抑制剂相结合、靶向 DDR-TGF-β-β-catenin-PD-L1 轴的合成致死框架,以及 抗病毒药物 方法。然而,所提出的治疗策略应谨慎解释,因为其证据基础因肿瘤类型而异,需要进一步研究。

papers.title: The Role of Pneumococcal and Human Papillomavirus Vaccination in Preventing Otolaryngological Diseases: Implications for Pediatric Practice
papers.abstract: Vaccinations are a cornerstone of primary prevention in pediatric otolaryngology and play a critical role in reducing the burden of pediatric infectious diseases, particularly acute otitis media (AOM) and HPV-related infections. The introduction and widespread use of pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCVs) have been associated with substantial changes in the epidemiology of pediatric AOM, particularly through reductions in vac-cine-serotype disease and complicated forms, while contributing to changes in pathogen distribution with an increased role of non-vaccine serotypes and non-pneumococcal bac-teria, requiring continuous epidemiological surveillance. Prophylactic human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination in adolescents and young adults effectively prevents oral infection with vaccine-type high-risk HPV, a necessary step in the pathogenesis of HPV-related oropharyngeal carcinoma. Clinical and epidemiological studies demonstrate robust antibody responses and significant reductions in oral HPV prevalence among vaccinated individuals. Although direct evidence of a reduction in oropharyngeal cancer incidence is not yet available, vaccination may consequently reduce the future burden of HPV-related oropharyngeal cancers. Long-term surveillance remains essential to confirm this potential benefit. Barriers to optimal vaccine coverage include unequal access, incomplete vaccination uptake, and limited awareness of HPV-related oral disease. In conclusion, vaccinations provide direct and clinically relevant benefits in pediatric otolaryngology by reducing recurrent AOM, severe complications and surgical interventions. HPV vaccination also reduces vaccine-type oral HPV infection and may consequently contribute to reducing the future burden of HPV-related oropharyngeal cancers. Achieving high vaccination coverage, coupled with continuous epidemiological monitoring, is essential to maximize individual and public health benefits and to inform the development of vaccines with broader serotype coverage.

papers.title: Awareness, factual knowledge, attitudes, and acceptability of human papillomavirus vaccination among adult women in Palestine: a cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a major preventable cause of cervical cancer, yet awareness and uptake of HPV vaccination remain suboptimal in many settings. Evidence regarding women's HPV-related awareness, factual knowledge, and vaccine acceptability in Palestine remains limited. This study assessed awareness, factual knowledge, attitudes, self-reported uptake, willingness, and perceived barriers related to HPV infection and HPV vaccination among adult women in Palestine. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted between October 2025 and February 2026 among women aged ≥18 years residing in Palestine. The questionnaire assessed sociodemographic characteristics, HPV and HPV vaccine awareness, factual knowledge, attitudes, vaccine uptake, willingness to receive or recommend vaccination, and perceived barriers. A 12-item factual knowledge score was calculated, and higher factual knowledge was defined as ≥7 correct responses. Descriptive statistics, subgroup analyses, and multivariable logistic regression were performed. Results Among 424 adult women included in the final analysis, 220 (51.9%) had heard of HPV and 146 (34.4%) had heard of the HPV vaccine. The mean factual knowledge score was 4.03 ± 2.72 out of 12, and 90 participants (21.2%) had higher factual knowledge. Self-reported HPV vaccine uptake was low (13.0%), whereas willingness to receive the vaccine was higher (55.2%). Lack of awareness (55.8%) and concern about vaccine safety (22.8%) were the most frequently reported barriers among unvaccinated women. In expanded adjusted analyses, prior HPV awareness, prior HPV vaccine awareness, and more supportive HPV-vaccination attitudes were independently associated with higher factual knowledge. Higher factual knowledge and supportive attitudes were associated with self-reported vaccine uptake, while willingness among unvaccinated women was most strongly associated with supportive vaccination attitudes. Conclusion Adult women in Palestine demonstrated limited HPV-related awareness and low factual knowledge, together with low self-reported HPV vaccine uptake. The gap between willingness and uptake, combined with the predominance of awareness and safety concerns as reported barriers, suggests a need for culturally appropriate education, provider-led counseling, and improved access to reliable HPV vaccine information. Findings should be interpreted cautiously given the cross-sectional design and online convenience sampling.

papers.source_body_en: Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a major preventable cause of cervical cancer, yet awareness and uptake of HPV vaccination remain suboptimal in many settings. Evidence regarding women's HPV-related awareness, factual knowledge, and vaccine acceptability in Palestine remains limited. This study assessed awareness, factual knowledge, attitudes, self-reported uptake, willingness, and perceived barriers related to HPV infection and HPV vaccination among adult women in Palestine. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted between October 2025 and February 2026 among women aged ≥18 years residing in Palestine. The questionnaire assessed sociodemographic characteristics, HPV and HPV vaccine awareness, factual knowledge, attitudes, vaccine uptake, willingness to receive or recommend vaccination, and perceived barriers. A 12-item factual knowledge score was calculated, and higher factual knowledge was defined as ≥7 correct responses. Descriptive statistics, subgroup analyses, and multivariable logistic regression were performed. Results Among 424 adult women included in the final analysis, 220 (51.9%) had heard of HPV and 146 (34.4%) had heard of the HPV vaccine. The mean factual knowledge score was 4.03 ± 2.72 out of 12, and 90 participants (21.2%) had higher factual knowledge. Self-reported HPV vaccine uptake was low (13.0%), whereas willingness to receive the vaccine was higher (55.2%). Lack of awareness (55.8%) and concern about vaccine safety (22.8%) were the most frequently reported barriers among unvaccinated women. In expanded adjusted analyses, prior HPV awareness, prior HPV vaccine awareness, and more supportive HPV-vaccination attitudes were independently associated with higher factual knowledge. Higher factual knowledge and supportive attitudes were associated with self-reported vaccine uptake, while willingness among unvaccinated women was most strongly associated with supportive vaccination attitudes. Conclusion Adult women in Palestine demonstrated limited HPV-related awareness and low factual knowledge, together with low self-reported HPV vaccine uptake. The gap between willingness and uptake, combined with the predominance of awareness and safety concerns as reported barriers, suggests a need for culturally appropriate education, provider-led counseling, and improved access to reliable HPV vaccine information. Findings should be interpreted cautiously given the cross-sectional design and online convenience sampling.

papers.title: Prevalence of human papillomavirus in the public health system of the central-northern region of Chile
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE Previously, we found a high prevalence of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in women attending the private health system. Therefore, the objective of this study was to determine the frequency of HR-HPV in a large cohort of women attending the public health system and to compare these findings. METHODS A total of 39,512 cervical samples from women aged 18 to 91 years who attended gynecological check-ups between 2020 and 2024 were analyzed using qPCR and the Papanicolaou technique. RESULTS The overall prevalence of HR-HPV infection between 2020 and 2024 was 13.70% (95% CI: 13.37-14.05%), with annual values of 13.07%, 12.64%, 14.80%, 14.24%, and 14.15% in 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024, respectively. In women under 25 years of age, the prevalence of HR-HPV was 34.03% during the evaluated period, compared to 16.35% in women aged 25 to 44 years, 10.47% in those aged 45 to 64 years, and 11.52% in women over 64 years of age. Pap smears showed 89.71% NILM results in HPV-negative women, compared to 74.59% in HPV-positive women. The rates of LSIL and HSIL were 0.14% and 0.07% in HPV-negative women, respectively; however, these values increased to 4.73% and 4.43% in HPV-positive women, respectively. Probable carcinoma was found in only 0.006% of HPV-negative women, but in 0.46% of HPV-positive women. CONCLUSIONS The prevalence of HR-HPV infection in women attending the public health system in the central-northern region appears to be similar to that previously reported in Chile, but lower than that reported in the same region for women attending the private health system.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to determine the frequency of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in women attending the public health system, as previous research had found a high prevalence in the private health system.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study analyzed 39,512 cervical samples from women aged 18 to 91 years who attended gynecological check-ups between 2020 and 2024 in the central-northern region of Chile.
analysis.methods: Samples were analyzed using qPCR and the Papanicolaou technique to detect HR-HPV infection and cytological abnormalities.
analysis.main_results: The overall prevalence of HR-HPV infection was 13.70% (95% CI: 13.37-14.05%), with higher rates in women under 25 years (34.03%) compared to older age groups. HPV-positive women had significantly higher rates of LSIL (4.73% vs. 0.14%) and HSIL (4.43% vs. 0.07%) than HPV-negative women.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that HR-HPV prevalence in the public health system was similar to previously reported national rates but lower than in the private health system in the same region, highlighting potential disparities in HPV infection rates between healthcare systems.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Findings inform public health surveillance and resource allocation by providing age-stratified prevalence data, which can guide targeted screening and prevention strategies for HPV-related diseases in the public health system.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's strength lies in its large sample size and longitudinal design, but limitations include potential selection bias as only women attending gynecological check-ups were included, and the evidence is moderate due to the abstract-only nature of the report.

analysis.summary_en: This study determined the prevalence of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in 39,512 women attending Chile's public health system between 2020-2024. The overall HR-HPV prevalence was 13.70%, with significantly higher rates in women under 25 years (34.03%) compared to older age groups. HPV-positive women had markedly increased rates of cytological abnormalities, including LSIL (4.73% vs. 0.14%) and HSIL (4.43% vs. 0.07%) compared to HPV-negative women. The prevalence was similar to national rates but lower than previously reported in the private health system, suggesting potential healthcare disparities. These findings provide valuable data for public health planning and targeted screening programs.

papers.full_text: Abstract Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is a major public health concern and a leading cause of cervical cancer among women worldwide. HPV vaccination remains an effective preventive strategy; however, vaccine acceptance among adolescents in low- and middle-income countries remains suboptimal. This study assessed factors associated with HPV vaccine acceptance among adolescent girls in selected public secondary schools in Abeokuta South Local Government Area, Ogun State, Nigeria. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 380 adolescent girls selected through a multistage sampling technique from two public secondary schools in Abeokuta South Local Government Area, Ogun State. Data were collected using a structured self-administered questionnaire. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS version 26. Descriptive statistics, chi-square test, Fisher’s exact test, and binary logistic regression were used for data analysis at a significance level of p < 0.05. Results The mean age of respondents was 15.46±.94years. More than half, 223 (58.7%) had heard of the HPV vaccine. Overall, 221 (41.8%) had good knowledge, 365 (96.1%) had good perception, and 285 (75.0%) demonstrated high acceptance of HPV vaccination. Bivariate analysis showed significant associations between HPV vaccine acceptance and age (p = 0.003), father’s education (p = 0.013), mother’s occupation (p = 0.030), father’s occupation (p < 0.001), living arrangement (p < 0.001), knowledge level (p = 0.005), and perception level (p = 0.003). Logistic regression analysis revealed that respondents aged 14–15 years (AOR = 2.81; 95% CI: 1.17–6.73), those whose mothers were professionals (AOR = 3.15; 95% CI: 1.42–6.99), and those with good knowledge and perception were more likely to accept HPV vaccination. Conversely, poor knowledge (AOR = 0.40; 95% CI: 0.22–0.76) and poor perception (AOR = 0.17; 95% CI: 0.04–0.76) significantly reduced the likelihood of vaccine acceptance. Conclusion Although acceptance of HPV vaccination among adolescent girls was relatively high, knowledge regarding HPV and its vaccine remained suboptimal. Knowledge, perception, parental characteristics, and living arrangement were significantly associated with reported HPV vaccine acceptance. Strengthening school-based health education and involving parents in HPV vaccine advocacy programs may improve informed acceptance and potentially support future vaccination uptake among adolescents. analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study investigated factors associated with HPV vaccine acceptance among 380 adolescent girls in Abeokuta South, Nigeria. While 75.0% showed high acceptance, knowledge remained suboptimal. Significant predictors included age (14-15 years), parental professional status, good knowledge, and positive perception. The study highlights the need for school-based health education and parental involvement to improve vaccination uptake. Limitations include the cross-sectional design, but the large sample size and robust analyses provide moderate evidence strength.

elements_en.main_results: Overall, 285 (75.0%) demonstrated high acceptance of HPV vaccination, and bivariate analysis showed significant associations between HPV vaccine acceptance and age, parental education and occupation, living arrangement, knowledge level, and perception level.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: Although acceptance of HPV vaccination among adolescent girls was relatively high, knowledge regarding HPV and its vaccine remained suboptimal, with knowledge, perception, parental characteristics, and living arrangement significantly associated with reported acceptance.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Strengthening school-based health education and involving parents in HPV vaccine advocacy programs may improve informed acceptance and potentially support future vaccination uptake among adolescents.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was cross-sectional, limiting causal inference, but the large sample size and rigorous statistical analyses provide moderate evidence strength.

papers.title: Association between HPV 16/18, HPV integration status, and CIN3 + in high-risk HPV-positive women: a multicenter cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the association between human papillomavirus (HPV) 16/18, HPV integration status, and cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 or worse (CIN3 +), and to provide evidence and theoretical support for the clinical translation of HPV integration testing. This was a multicenter cross-sectional study conducted within a cervical cancer screening program in China. HPV integration was detected using high-throughput viral integration detection (HIVID). Structural equation modeling (SEM) was employed to examine the mediating effect of HPV integration. A total of 3,077 high-risk HPV-positive women were included in the final analysis. Among these participants, 29.5% were infected with HPV 16/18, 12.9% tested positive for HPV integration, and 5.9% had biopsy-confirmed CIN3 + . Multivariable logistic regression analysis demonstrated that both HPV integration and HPV 16/18 were independently associated with CIN3 + . In mediation analysis, the standardized path coefficient for the direct effect of HPV 16/18 on CIN3 + was 0.087. For the indirect effect, the standardized path coefficient from HPV 16/18 to HPV integration was 0.404, and from HPV integration to CIN3 + was 0.771. The mediating effect of HPV integration accounted for 78.1% of the total effect. This study elucidates the mediating role of HPV integration in the progression from HPV 16/18 infection to CIN3 + , offering new insights into HPV risk stratification and clinical management.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomaviruses (HPV), particularly types 16 and 18, is a necessary cause of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 or worse (CIN3+). The study addressed a knowledge gap regarding whether HPV integration status mediates the association between HPV 16/18 and CIN3+ to inform clinical translation of HPV integration testing.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a multicenter cross-sectional study conducted within a cervical cancer screening program in China, enrolling 3,077 high-risk HPV-positive women between the study dates.
analysis.methods: HPV integration was detected using high-throughput viral integration detection (HIVID), and multivariable logistic regression and structural equation modeling (SEM) were used to assess associations and mediating effects between HPV 16/18, HPV integration, and CIN3+.
analysis.main_results: HPV 16/18 prevalence was 29.5%, HPV integration prevalence was 12.9%, and CIN3+ prevalence was 5.9%. Both HPV integration and HPV 16/18 were independently associated with CIN3+ in multivariable analysis.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates that HPV integration mediates 78.1% of the total effect of HPV 16/18 on CIN3+, providing new evidence that HPV integration status may refine risk stratification for CIN3+ in HPV-positive women.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that incorporating HPV integration testing into cervical cancer screening could improve identification of women at highest risk for CIN3+, potentially guiding more targeted clinical management and follow-up.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: As a cross-sectional study, temporality cannot be established, limiting causal inference; the evidence strength is moderate given the single-country setting and reliance on screening-program data.

analysis.summary_en: This multicenter cross-sectional study in China evaluated 3,077 high-risk HPV-positive women to investigate whether HPV integration mediates the association between HPV 16/18 and CIN3+. Using HIVID for integration detection and SEM for mediation analysis, the authors found that both HPV integration and HPV 16/18 were independently associated with CIN3+, and that HPV integration accounted for 78.1% of the total effect of HPV 16/18 on CIN3+. The study interprets these results as evidence that HPV integration status could refine risk stratification for CIN3+ in HPV-positive women, offering new insights for clinical translation of integration testing within cervical cancer screening programs.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomaviruses (HPV), particularly types 16 and 18, is a necessary cause of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 or worse (CIN3+). The study addressed a knowledge gap regarding whether HPV integration status mediates the association between HPV 16/18 and CIN3+ to inform clinical translation of HPV integration testing.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This was a multicenter cross-sectional study conducted within a cervical cancer screening program in China, enrolling 3,077 high-risk HPV-positive women between the study dates.
analysis_en.methods: HPV integration was detected using high-throughput viral integration detection (HIVID), and multivariable logistic regression and structural equation modeling (SEM) were used to assess associations and mediating effects between HPV 16/18, HPV integration, and CIN3+.
analysis_en.main_results: HPV 16/18 prevalence was 29.5%, HPV integration prevalence was 12.9%, and CIN3+ prevalence was 5.9%. Both HPV integration and HPV 16/18 were independently associated with CIN3+ in multivariable analysis.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates that HPV integration mediates 78.1% of the total effect of HPV 16/18 on CIN3+, providing new evidence that HPV integration status may refine risk stratification for CIN3+ in HPV-positive women.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that incorporating HPV integration testing into cervical cancer screening could improve identification of women at highest risk for CIN3+, potentially guiding more targeted clinical management and follow-up.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: As a cross-sectional study, temporality cannot be established, limiting causal inference; the evidence strength is moderate given the single-country setting and reliance on screening-program data.

papers.title_zh: 高危型HPV 阳性女性中 HPV 16/18、HPV 整合状态和 CIN3 + 之间的关联:一项多中心横断面研究
papers.source_body_en: This study aimed to investigate the association between human papillomavirus (HPV) 16/18, HPV integration status, and cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 or worse (CIN3 +), and to provide evidence and theoretical support for the clinical translation of HPV integration testing. This was a multicenter cross-sectional study conducted within a cervical cancer screening program in China. HPV integration was detected using high-throughput viral integration detection (HIVID). Structural equation modeling (SEM) was employed to examine the mediating effect of HPV integration. A total of 3,077 high-risk HPV-positive women were included in the final analysis. Among these participants, 29.5% were infected with HPV 16/18, 12.9% tested positive for HPV integration, and 5.9% had biopsy-confirmed CIN3 + . Multivariable logistic regression analysis demonstrated that both HPV integration and HPV 16/18 were independently associated with CIN3 + . In mediation analysis, the standardized path coefficient for the direct effect of HPV 16/18 on CIN3 + was 0.087. For the indirect effect, the standardized path coefficient from HPV 16/18 to HPV integration was 0.404, and from HPV integration to CIN3 + was 0.771. The mediating effect of HPV integration accounted for 78.1% of the total effect. This study elucidates the mediating role of HPV integration in the progression from HPV 16/18 infection to CIN3 + , offering new insights into HPV risk stratification and clinical management.

papers.title: Orientation of Gp96 and Calreticulin T-cell epitopes in a multiepitope HPV16 E7 vaccine construct affects predicted immunostimulatory properties: An in silico and expression validation study
papers.abstract: Heat shock proteins (HSPs) can be used as adjuvants to develop therapeutic vaccines, as they enhance the cross-presentation of related tumor antigens and stimulate T cells. In this study, the immunostimulatory properties of gp96 and calreticulin was evaluated to enhance HPV16 E7-based vaccines effectiveness. In silico evaluation was performed to select epitopes from HSPs based on high binding affinity to MHC-I/II, strong immunogenicity, and population coverage. Six novel multiepitope constructs harboring conserved epitopes of E7, gp96, and calreticulin were designed in different orientations. Molecular docking was performed between these constructs and signaling (TLRs) and endocytic (CD14, CD91, LOX-1, and SREC-1) receptors. After determination of an effective construct in molecular docking and MD simulation, prokaryotic expression plasmid containing eight (CTL/HTL) epitopes from HPV16 E7, gp96, and calreticulin in suitable orientation was prepared, and the recombinant multiepitope peptide was generated in E. Our data showed that the gp96-CRT-E7 construct had superior docking scores with receptors (especially TLR2 and LOX-1), suggesting stronger stimulation of both innate and adaptive immunity than other constructs. It was predicted to be non-toxic, non-allergenic, antigenic, immunogenic, and structurally stable. Moreover, the multiepitope gp96-CRT-E7 fusion peptide was expressed in the Rosetta strain under conditions of OD 600 : 0.6–0.7, 0.5 mM IPTG, temperature of 18oC, and 24 hours after IPTG induction, and purified through affinity chromatography under native conditions. Generally, successful results of in silico and expression validation of the multiepitope gp96-CRT-E7 fusion peptide showed its strong potential as a novel candidate for HPV16 vaccine development.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the immunostimulatory properties of gp96 and calreticulin to enhance HPV16 E7-based vaccine effectiveness. Six novel multiepitope constructs were designed and evaluated through in silico methods, including molecular docking with various receptors. The gp96-CRT-E7 construct showed superior docking scores, suggesting stronger stimulation of both innate and adaptive immunity. The construct was predicted to be non-toxic, non-allergenic, antigenic, immunogenic, and structurally stable. Successful expression and purification of the multiepitope gp96-CRT-E7 fusion peptide in a prokaryotic system validated its potential as a novel candidate for HPV16 vaccine development. This approach may contribute to improved immunotherapy strategies for HPV-related diseases, though further in vivo and clinical evaluations are needed.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 热休克蛋白 (HSP) 可用作佐剂来开发治疗性 疫苗,因为它们增强相关肿瘤抗原的交叉呈递并刺激 T 细胞。在这项研究中,评估了 gp96 和钙网蛋白的免疫刺激特性,以增强基于 HPV16 E7 的 疫苗 的有效性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 以不同方向设计了六种新型多表位构建体,其中包含 E7、gp96 和钙网蛋白保守表位。在这些构建体与信号传导 (TLR) 和内吞(CD14、CD91、LOX-1 和 SREC-1)受体之间进行分子对接。通过分子对接和MD模拟确定有效构建体后,制备了含有HPV16 E7、gp96和钙网蛋白8个合适方向表位的原核表达质粒,并在大肠杆菌中产生了重组多表位肽。
elements_zh.methods: 基于对 MHC-I/II 的高结合亲和力、强免疫原性和群体覆盖度,进行计算机评估以从 HSP 中选择表位。多表位gp96-CRT-E7融合肽在特定条件下在Rosetta菌株中表达,并通过亲和层析纯化。
elements_zh.main_results: 我们的数据表明,gp96-CRT-E7 构建体与受体(特别是 TLR2 和 LOX-1)具有优异的对接分数,表明比其他构建体对先天免疫和适应性免疫具有更强的刺激作用。预计它是无毒、非过敏性、抗原性、免疫原性和结构稳定的。一般来说,多表位 gp96-CRT-E7 融合肽的计算机模拟和表达验证的成功结果表明其作为 HPV16 疫苗 开发的新候选者的强大潜力。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 多表位 HPV16 E7 疫苗 构建体中 Gp96 和钙网蛋白 T 细胞表位的方向影响预测的免疫刺激特性,其中 gp96-CRT-E7 构建体表现出卓越的免疫刺激潜力。这项研究通过计算机模拟和表达验证为 HPV16 疫苗 开发提供了一种新的候选药物。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,gp96-CRT-E7 构建体具有作为 HPV16 疫苗 开发的新候选者的强大潜力,这可以增强 疫苗 治疗 HPV 相关癌症的有效性。这种方法可能有助于改善 HPV 相关疾病的免疫治疗策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于原核系统中的计算机预测和表达验证,没有体内或临床评估。证据强度中等,因为该研究证明了成功的表达和预测的免疫原性,但缺乏生物系统或人体试验的验证。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 热休克蛋白 (HSP) 可用作佐剂来开发治疗性 疫苗,因为它们增强相关肿瘤抗原的交叉呈递并刺激 T 细胞。在这项研究中,评估了 gp96 和钙网蛋白的免疫刺激特性,以增强基于 HPV16 E7 的 疫苗 的有效性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 以不同方向设计了六种新型多表位构建体,其中包含 E7、gp96 和钙网蛋白保守表位。在这些构建体与信号传导 (TLR) 和内吞(CD14、CD91、LOX-1 和 SREC-1)受体之间进行分子对接。通过分子对接和MD模拟确定有效构建体后,制备了含有HPV16 E7、gp96和钙网蛋白8个合适方向表位的原核表达质粒,并在大肠杆菌中产生了重组多表位肽。
analysis_zh.methods: 基于对 MHC-I/II 的高结合亲和力、强免疫原性和群体覆盖度,进行计算机评估以从 HSP 中选择表位。多表位gp96-CRT-E7融合肽在特定条件下在Rosetta菌株中表达,并通过亲和层析纯化。
analysis_zh.main_results: 我们的数据表明,gp96-CRT-E7 构建体与受体(特别是 TLR2 和 LOX-1)具有优异的对接分数,表明比其他构建体对先天免疫和适应性免疫具有更强的刺激作用。预计它是无毒、非过敏性、抗原性、免疫原性和结构稳定的。一般来说,多表位 gp96-CRT-E7 融合肽的计算机模拟和表达验证的成功结果表明其作为 HPV16 疫苗 开发的新候选者的强大潜力。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 多表位 HPV16 E7 疫苗 构建体中 Gp96 和钙网蛋白 T 细胞表位的方向影响预测的免疫刺激特性,其中 gp96-CRT-E7 构建体表现出卓越的免疫刺激潜力。这项研究通过计算机模拟和表达验证为 HPV16 疫苗 开发提供了一种新的候选药物。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,gp96-CRT-E7 构建体具有作为 HPV16 疫苗 开发的新候选者的强大潜力,这可以增强 疫苗 治疗 HPV 相关癌症的有效性。这种方法可能有助于改善 HPV 相关疾病的免疫治疗策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于原核系统中的计算机预测和表达验证,没有体内或临床评估。证据强度中等,因为该研究证明了成功的表达和预测的免疫原性,但缺乏生物系统或人体试验的验证。

source_records.title: Data from Tissue Context Shapes Distinct Premalignant Outcomes in an HPV16 E6/E7-Mutant Pik3ca Transgenic Mouse Model
source_records.abstract: Abstract High-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, particularly HPV16, is a major etiologic factor associated with multiple human cancers, including anal, cervical, and oropharyngeal carcinomas. However, the mechanisms underlying tissue-specific responses to HPV oncogene expression remain poorly understood. In this study, we developed and characterized a double-inducible transgenic mouse model enabling spatially and temporally controlled expression of HPV16 E6/E7 oncoproteins in K14-positive epithelial progenitor cells of both the anal and oral mucosae. Within 2 months of induction, HPV16 E6/E7 expression elicited epithelial hyperplasia and dysplasia in both tissues but with distinct outcomes: low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions in the anal canal and moderate to severe dysplasia in the tongue. Continuous oncogene expression was required for lesion maintenance, as doxycycline withdrawal reversed the proliferative phenotype, indicating a dynamic and reversible process. To assess whether activation of the PI3K pathway could cooperate with HPV oncogenes, we combined the E6/E7 model with a Pik3ca H1047R knock-in mouse line. Constitutive PI3K activation alone induced mild dysplasia in both epithelia, whereas its combination with E6/E7 enhanced dysplastic severity in the tongue but not in the anal mucosa. No progression to invasive carcinoma was observed within 6 months. These findings demonstrate that identical oncogenic signals—HPV16 E6/E7 expression and PI3K activation—produce distinct premalignant outcomes depending on epithelial context. This work highlights the critical role of local microenvironmental factors in HPV-driven carcinogenesis and provides a platform to identify tissue-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities in HPV-associated cancers. Significance: This work presents a double-inducible mouse model showing that HPV16 E6/E7 and PI3K activation drives distinct dysplastic outcomes in anal and oral epithelia. The study highlights how tissue context and microenvironment critically shape HPV oncogene effects, offering an important tool for uncovering mechanisms and therapeutic targets in HPV-related cancers.

source_records.abstract: Incidence of hyperplastic and dysplastic lesions in AM and tongue epithelia across all three experimental groups. Incidence was evaluated for all cases analyzed in the TG-E6/E7, K14/PI3K, and C.M. genotypes in both the anal mucosa (AM) and lingual mucosa (tongue). For statistical comparison between the two anatomic sites, cases in the AM were classified as the hyperplasia (HIPER) category including all lesions exhibiting hyperkeratosis, epithelial hyperplasia, or mild dysplasia (LSIL), whereas the dysplasia (DISP) category comprising lesions with a histopathologic diagnosis of moderate to severe dysplasia (HSIL). In the lingual mucosa, the HIPER category included lesions characterized by hyperkeratosis and epithelial hyperplasia, whereas the DISP category encompassed all dysplastic lesions, ranging from mild to severe. The normal category included histologically normal mucosa with morphology within normal limits. source_records.title: Figure 4 from Tissue Context Shapes Distinct Premalignant Outcomes in an HPV16 E6/E7-Mutant Pik3ca Transgenic Mouse Model
source_records.abstract: Morphologic changes developed in the anal and lingual mucosae of K14/PI3K animals. Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)–stained sections of the anal mucosa (AM) showing epithelial alterations at 2 and 4 months following transgene activation. A, AM from TG-E6/E7 mice displaying stratified squamous epithelium with hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, and areas of basal layer stratification (low magnification, 2 months). B, Region of AM exhibiting mild epithelial dysplasia. C, At 4 months, transgenic AM shows squamous epithelium with hyperkeratosis, epithelial hyperplasia, and mild dysplastic changes (low magnification). Inset, higher magnification of the area in C highlighting epithelial hyperplasia and hyperkeratosis. H&E-stained sections of tongue mucosa showing epithelial alterations at 2 and 4 months after transgene activation. D, Low-magnification view of TG-E6/E7 lingual epithelium showing marked hyperkeratosis. Bottom, a higher-magnification image reveals hyperplastic epithelium with cellular and nuclear irregularities in the basal layers and suprabasal hyperkeratosis (2 months). E, Low-magnification view of transgenic tongue epithelium showing hyperkeratosis and mild dysplasia (4 months). F, Area of a K14/PI3K transgenic tongue displaying mild dysplasia. G, Incidence of LSIL and HSIL in the AM of control mice ( N = 10) and K14/PI3K animals ( N = 7) as the percentage of the total number of animals per group. LSIL, cases diagnosed with mild dysplasia, hyperplasia, and cellular and tissue alterations involving the lower third of the epithelium; HSIL, diagnosed with moderate or severe dysplasia. Incidence of hyperplasia and dysplasia in the tongue epithelium of control mice ( N = 10) and TG-E6/E7 animals ( N = 9) as the percentage of the total number of animals per group. DISP, dysplasia; HIPER, hyperplasia(); diagnosed with mild, moderate, or severe dysplasia. *, P H, pS6 expression pattern in the anal canal of K14/PI3K mice (low magnification). Right, a higher-magnification view of the highlighted rectangular area in H shows pS6-positive cells in the suprabasal layers. I, Another area of K14/PI3K AM displaying dysplastic changes and pS6 immunoreactivity. J, Lingual epithelium from a K14/PI3K animal showing pS6 expression in the upper layers. Scale bars, 200 μm ( A , C–F , and H ); 50 μm ( B , I , J , and insets in C , D , and H ).

source_records.title: Figure 2 from Tissue Context Shapes Distinct Premalignant Outcomes in an HPV16 E6/E7-Mutant Pik3ca Transgenic Mouse Model
source_records.abstract: E6/E7 expression is sufficient to induce the development of squamous intraepithelial lesions in the anal canal of TG-E6/E7 mice. A, Panoramic view at low magnification of the genital area in a female mouse, showing the location of the murine anal canal (black dotted rectangle) in relation to the vagina (bottom left). B, Higher magnification of the area outlined in the rectangle in A , showing the normal histology of the anal canal in a control animal. C–F, Morphologic changes developed in the TG-E6/E7 anal mucosa. C, Representative histologic image of the anal mucosal epithelium from a control mouse. D–F, Representative examples of LSIL in TG-E6/E7 anal mucosa (AM). D, Anal mucosa lined by the hyperorthokeratotic squamous epithelium showing mild to moderate dysplastic changes 2 months after DOX treatment. E, AM with moderate dysplastic changes after 2 months of evolution. Note the hypergranulosis, basal stratification, and cellular and nuclear irregularities involving the lower and middle epithelial layers. F, AM with severe dysplastic changes (HSIL) after 4 months of evolution. Hyperkeratosis and cellular and nuclear irregularities involving the middle and upper epithelial layers. G, IHC expression of E6 in the anal mucosa of TG-E6/E7 mice. In G , a low-magnification image shows the patchy pattern of E6 expression along the anal canal. Black rectangles indicate areas with positive staining, shown at higher magnification to the right. Note the expression of E6 in the basal epithelial layer (top) as well as the cytoplasmic localization of E6 in individual suprabasal cells (bottom). H, Perianal skin from the E6/E7 transgenic mouse shown in G , lacking E6-positive cells. I, Control without primary antibody in TG-E6/E7 anal mucosa. J, Incidence of LSIL and HSIL in the anal mucosa of control mice ( N = 10) and TG-E6/E7 animals ( N = 17) as the percentage of the total number of animals per group. LSIL, cases diagnosed with mild dysplasia, hyperplasia, and cellular and tissue alterations involving the lower third of the epithelium; HSIL, diagnosed with moderate or severe dysplasia. TG-E6/E7: 2 months ( N = 7), 4 months ( N = 5), and 5–6 months ( N = 5). *, P K, IHC expression of K14. Low-magnification overview of TG-E6/E7 anal mucosa showing K14 expression. Right, a higher-magnification image of a hyperplastic and hyperkeratotic area shows K14 expression throughout the entire epithelial thickness. L, Immunostaining for K7. Low-magnification overview of TG-E6/E7 anal mucosa showing no K7 expression. M, Detailed view of an TG-E6/E7 anal mucosal area negative for K7. Inset, positive control for K7; glandular epithelium (intestine). N, Immunostaining for pS6 in the anal mucosa of TG-E6/E7 animals. Anal mucosa of a control animal showing minimal pS6 expression. pS6 expression in anal mucosa 2 months after E6/E7 induction, observed in the suprabasal layers; pS6 expression in anal mucosa of an animal 4 months after E6/E7 induction. Scale bars, 1 mm ( A ); 250 μm ( B ); 200 μm ( C ); 100 μm ( K and L ); 50 μm ( F–I and N ); 25 μm ( D , E , M , and insets in C and K ).

papers.title_original: Data from Tissue Context Shapes Distinct Premalignant Outcomes in an HPV16 E6/E7-Mutant Pik3ca Transgenic Mouse Model

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate how tissue context shapes distinct premalignant outcomes in an HPV16 E6/E7-mutant Pik3ca transgenic mouse model, focusing on the development of squamous intraepithelial lesions in the anal canal.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a transgenic mouse model (TG-E6/E7) with HPV16 E6/E7 expression and Pik3ca mutation, comparing anal mucosa lesions in transgenic animals (N=17) to controls (N=10) at different time points (2, 4, and 5-6 months).
analysis.methods: Histopathological analysis and immunohistochemistry (IHC) were performed to assess dysplastic changes, E6 expression, and markers like K14, K7, and pS6 in the anal mucosa of transgenic and control mice.
analysis.main_results: TG-E6/E7 mice developed low-grade (LSIL) and high-grade (HSIL) squamous intraepithelial lesions in the anal mucosa, with E6 expression localized to basal and suprabasal layers, while controls showed no lesions or E6 expression.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that tissue-specific factors in the anal canal drive distinct premalignant outcomes, with E6/E7 expression sufficient to induce lesions, and the study demonstrated the model's utility for studying HPV-associated carcinogenesis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide insights into HPV-driven carcinogenesis mechanisms and may inform surveillance and prevention strategies for HPV-associated anal lesions in humans.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the limited sample size and reliance on a single animal model, though the study provides detailed histopathological and molecular data.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated how tissue context influences premalignant outcomes in an HPV16 E6/E7-mutant Pik3ca transgenic mouse model. The researchers found that E6/E7 expression alone was sufficient to induce squamous intraepithelial lesions (LSIL and HSIL) in the anal canal of transgenic mice, with E6 expression localized to basal and suprabasal layers. Histopathological analysis revealed progressive dysplastic changes, while immunohistochemistry confirmed molecular alterations. The study demonstrates the model's utility for studying HPV-associated carcinogenesis and provides insights into tissue-specific mechanisms of HPV-driven lesions, with potential implications for human HPV-related disease prevention and surveillance.

papers.title: NFX1-123 is required for keratinocyte differentiation and HPV 16 DNA maintenance in early and persistent infection models
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR HPV) infections cause nearly 5% of cancers worldwide, including cervical and oropharyngeal cancers. HR HPVs sustain long-term infections in stratified epithelial tissues by maintaining copies of viral genomes in basal keratinocytes and utilizing the cellular differentiation processes in the upper layers to coordinate key steps in the viral life cycle. We have demonstrated previously that the endogenous host protein NFX1-123 bound directly to the HR HPV type 16 oncoprotein E6 (16E6), and that this partnership increased keratinocyte proliferation and differentiation, two processes that are both required for persistent HPV 16 infections. As there is a range of endogenous expression of NFX1-123 in normal basal keratinocytes, we aimed to investigate the role of NFX1-123 abundance on the initiation and persistence of HPV 16 infections. In this study, we utilized keratinocytes with overexpressed, endogenous, or reduced levels of NFX1-123 and infected these cells with an HPV 16 quasivirus (Qsv) to interrogate changes to keratinocyte growth and viral DNA copy numbers with NFX1-123 modulation. Keratinocytes with reduced NFX1-123 had blunted differentiation and stratification in raft cultures, and this correlated with decreased HPV 16 Qsv DNA copies. Similarly, when we reduced NFX1-123 in W12E cells, a cervical cell line harboring episomal HPV 16 genomes, we saw a decrease in raft culture differentiation and thickness, and fewer viral genome copies compared to W12E cells with endogenous NFX1-123. These findings indicate the importance of NFX1-123 on the initiation and maintenance of HPV 16 infections that may persist and progress to cancer. IMPORTANCE A high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection that persists for decades is the biggest risk factor for the development of cervical and other HPV-associated cancers. The ability of HPV to maintain its genome and persist in stratified epithelium is dependent on its partnership with host proteins and its co-opting of cellular pathways. analysis.research_question_and_background: Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR HPV) infections cause nearly 5% of cancers worldwide, including cervical and oropharyngeal cancers. The study aimed to investigate the role of NFX1-123 abundance on the initiation and persistence of HPV 16 infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study utilized keratinocytes with overexpressed, endogenous, or reduced levels of NFX1-123 and infected these cells with an HPV 16 quasivirus (Qsv) to model both early and persistent infection.
analysis.methods: Keratinocytes with modulated NFX1-123 levels were infected with HPV 16 Qsv, and changes to keratinocyte growth and viral DNA copy numbers were analyzed in monolayer and three-dimensional raft cultures.
analysis.main_results: Keratinocytes with reduced NFX1-123 had blunted differentiation and stratification in raft cultures, correlating with decreased HPV 16 Qsv DNA copies. Similarly, reducing NFX1-123 in W12E cells decreased raft culture differentiation, thickness, and viral genome copies.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that NFX1-123 is required for keratinocyte differentiation and stratification, and its disruption significantly impairs HPV 16's ability to maintain its episomal genome at consistent copy numbers.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings highlight the importance of NFX1-123 for the persistence of HPV 16 infections and suggest it as a potential therapeutic target in HPV 16-positive cancers and precancers.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in vitro using keratinocyte models, which may not fully replicate in vivo conditions. The evidence strength is moderate due to the use of cell culture models and the need for further validation in vivo.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of the host protein NFX1-123 in HPV 16 infection persistence. These findings demonstrate that NFX1-123 is essential for HPV 16 genome maintenance and suggest it as a potential therapeutic target for HPV-associated cancers.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 持续的高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (HR HPV) 感染导致全球近 5% 的癌症,包括宫颈癌和口咽癌。该研究旨在调查 NFX1-123 丰度对 HPV 16 感染的起始和持续性的作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究利用 NFX1-123 过度表达、内源性或降低水平的角质形成细胞,并用 HPV 16 准病毒 (Qsv) 感染这些细胞来模拟早期和持续感染。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,NFX1-123 是角质形成细胞分化和分层所必需的,其破坏会显着损害 HPV 16 将其附加型 基因组 维持在一致拷贝数的能力。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了 NFX1-123 对于 HPV 16 感染持续存在的重要性,并表明它是 HPV 16 阳性癌症和癌前病变的潜在治疗靶点。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是使用角质形成细胞模型在体外进行的,该模型可能无法完全复制体内条件。由于使用细胞培养模型并且需要进一步体内验证,证据强度中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 持续高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (HR HPV) 感染导致全球近 5% 的癌症,包括宫颈癌和口咽癌。HR HPV 通过在基底角质形成细胞中维持病毒 基因组 的拷贝并利用上层的细胞分化过程来协调病毒生命周期中的关键步骤,从而维持分层上皮组织中的长期感染。我们之前已经证明,内源性 宿主 蛋白 NFX1-123 直接与 HR HPV 16 型癌蛋白 E6 (16E6) 结合,并且这种伙伴关系增加了角质形成细胞增殖和分化,这两个过程都是持续 HPV 16 感染所必需的。由于正常基底角质形成细胞中存在一系列 NFX1-123 内源性表达,我们旨在研究 NFX1-123 丰度对 HPV 16 感染的起始和持续性的作用。在这项研究中,我们利用 NFX1-123 过度表达、内源性或降低水平的角质形成细胞,并用 HPV 16 准病毒 (Qsv) 感染这些细胞,以探究 NFX1-123 调制对角质形成细胞生长和病毒 DNA 拷贝数的变化。NFX1-123 减少的角质形成细胞在筏培养物中的分化和分层减弱,这与 HPV 16 Qsv DNA 拷贝数减少相关。同样,当我们减少 W12E 细胞(一种含有附加型 HPV 16 基因组 的宫颈细胞系)中的 NFX1-123 时,我们发现与含有内源性 NFX1-123 的 W12E 细胞相比,筏培养物分化和厚度减少,病毒 基因组 拷贝数减少。这些发现表明 NFX1-123 在 HPV 16 感染的启动和维持中的重要性,这种感染可能持续并进展为癌症。重要性 持续数十年的高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染是患宫颈癌和其他 HPV 相关癌症的最大危险因素。HPV 维持其 基因组 并在复层上皮中持续存在的能力取决于其与 宿主 蛋白的伙伴关系及其对细胞途径的选择。在这里,我们研究了 HPV 16 的 宿主 蛋白伴侣 NFX1-123 的丰度如何影响单层和三维培养物中病毒 基因组 的维持和复制,模拟早期和持续感染。这项研究表明,NFX1-123 是筏培养物中角质形成细胞分化和分层所必需的,并且这些过程的破坏显着阻碍了 HPV 16 将其附加型 基因组 维持在一致拷贝数的能力。这些发现表明 NFX1-123 对于 HPV 16 感染持续存在的重要性,并鼓励进一步研究 NFX1-123 作为 HPV 16 阳性癌症和癌前病变的潜在治疗靶点。

papers.title: Efficacy of live lactobacillus preparations in treating cervical inflammation and clearing viral infections in patients with HPV infection complicated by bacterial vaginosis
papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Dingjunsheng, a live Lactobacillus preparation, as adjuvant therapy in patients with human papillomavirus (HPV) infection complicated by bacterial vaginosis (BV). A retrospective analysis was conducted on 152 eligible patients, randomly divided into two groups: the observation group (n=87) receiving standard BV antibacterial therapy plus Dingjunsheng, and the control group (n=65) who received standard BV antibacterial therapy alone. The patients were followed up for six months. Primary outcomes included HPV clearance rate and cervical cytological inflammation improvement, while secondary outcomes involved BV recurrence rate and adverse reaction incidence. The results showed that the observation group had a significantly higher HPV clearance rate (73.6% vs 53.9%) and inflammation improvement rate (90.8% vs 76.9%), as well as a lower BV recurrence rate (3.1% vs 13.9%) compared to the control group. Dingjunsheng was identified as an independent protective factor for HPV clearance (OR=2.5, 95%CI:1.3–5.1). The incidence of adverse reactions was similar between both groups. We conclude that Dingjunsheng adjuvant therapy demonstrated effectiveness in improving HPV clearance, alleviating inflammation, and reducing BV recurrence, with good safety, making it a valuable treatment strategy for these patients.

papers.full_text: Abstract Background High-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) is a leading cause of anogenital cancers and disproportionately affects men who have sex with men (MSM), particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Few studies in sub-Saharan Africa have concurrently examined penile and rectal hrHPV infection and their site-specific behavioral and biological correlates. We assessed the prevalence, genotype distribution, and behavioral factors associated with penile and rectal hrHPV among MSM in Kisumu, Kenya. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from MSM aged 18–35 years. Clinician-collected penile and rectal swabs were tested for hrHPV using the ScreenFire HPV assay. Urine and rectal specimens were tested for Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae using GeneXpert, and HIV status was confirmed as per Kenyan national guidelines. hrHPV was analyzed separately by anatomical site. Log-binomial regression was used to estimate adjusted prevalence ratios (aPR) for associations with sociodemographic, behavioral, and biological factors. Results Penile hrHPV prevalence was 24.7% (39/158) and rectal hrHPV prevalence was 12.5% (22/176); 6.7% of participants tested at both sites had dual-site infection. Most infections at both sites involved a single genotype group. HPV-18/45 was the most common genotype group at both sites. Penile hrHPV was more likely among participants with HIV (aPR = 2.27, p = 0.050) and trended toward an association for those reporting insertive anal sex (aPR = 5.26, p = 0.062) and was less common among employed participants (aPR = 0.25, p = 0.048). Circumcision showed a protective trend (aPR = 0.52, p = 0.090). Rectal hrHPV was more common among participants with rectal chlamydia and/or gonorrhea infection (aPR = 3.34, p = 0.001), transgender or non-binary identity (aPR = 2.28, p = 0.036), with a possible association for those practicing receptive anal intercourse (aPR = 3.97, p = 0.062). Although HIV was associated with rectal hrHPV in unadjusted analyses, this relationship was attenuated after accounting for rectal bacterial STI infection. Conclusions hrHPV infection was common among MSM in Kisumu, Kenya, with distinct site-specific correlates. The strong association between rectal bacterial STIs and rectal hrHPV highlights the need for integrated HPV and STI screening. These findings support expansion of gender-neutral HPV vaccination and etiologic STI screening to reduce HPV-associated cancer risk among MSM in sub-Saharan Africa. Clinical trial number Not applicable. papers.title_original: Prevalence and behavioral factors associated with penile and rectal HPV infection among men who have sex with men in Kenya

analysis.research_question_and_background: High-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) is a leading cause of anogenital cancers and disproportionately affects men who have sex with men (MSM), particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Few studies in sub-Saharan Africa have concurrently examined penile and rectal hrHPV infection and their site-specific behavioral and biological correlates.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from MSM aged 18–35 years in Kisumu, Kenya. Clinician-collected penile and rectal swabs were tested for hrHPV using the ScreenFire HPV assay.
analysis.methods: Urine and rectal specimens were tested for Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae using GeneXpert, and HIV status was confirmed as per Kenyan national guidelines. Log-binomial regression was used to estimate adjusted prevalence ratios (aPR) for associations with sociodemographic, behavioral, and biological factors.
analysis.main_results: Penile hrHPV prevalence was 24.7% (39/158) and rectal hrHPV prevalence was 12.5% (22/176); 6.7% of participants tested at both sites had dual-site infection. HPV-18/45 was the most common genotype group at both sites. Penile hrHPV was more likely among participants with HIV (aPR = 2.27, p = 0.050) and less common among employed participants (aPR = 0.25, p = 0.048).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that hrHPV infection was common among MSM in Kisumu, Kenya, with distinct site-specific correlates. The strong association between rectal bacterial STIs and rectal hrHPV highlights the need for integrated HPV and STI screening.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support expansion of gender-neutral HPV vaccination and etiologic STI screening to reduce HPV-associated cancer risk among MSM in sub-Saharan Africa. Integrated screening could improve early detection and prevention of HPV-related diseases in this high-risk population.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was cross-sectional, limiting causal inference. The evidence strength is moderate due to the sample size and potential confounding factors, but the findings are consistent with biological plausibility and prior research.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prevalence and behavioral factors associated with penile and rectal hrHPV infection among MSM in Kisumu, Kenya. A cross-sectional analysis of 158-176 participants aged 18-35 years found penile hrHPV prevalence at 24.7% and rectal hrHPV at 12.5%, with HPV-18/45 as the most common genotype. Key correlates included HIV status for penile infection and rectal bacterial STIs for rectal infection. The authors concluded that hrHPV is common with site-specific factors, supporting integrated HPV and STI screening and gender-neutral vaccination to reduce cancer risk in this population. The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, but the evidence strength is moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 高风险 人乳头瘤病毒 (hrHPV) 是肛门生殖器癌症的主要原因,对男男性行为者 (MSM) 的影响尤为严重,特别是在低收入和中等收入国家。撒哈拉以南非洲地区很少有研究同时检查阴茎和直肠 hrHPV 感染及其特定部位的行为和生物学相关性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们对肯尼亚基苏木 18-35 岁 MSM 的基线数据进行了横断面分析。使用 ScreenFire HPV 检测对临床医生收集的阴茎和直肠拭子进行 hrHPV 检测。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 GeneXpert 对尿液和直肠标本进行沙眼衣原体和淋病奈瑟菌检测,并根据肯尼亚国家指南确认艾滋病毒状况。使用对数二项式回归来估计调整后的 患病率 比率 (aPR),以了解与社会人口统计学、行为和生物因素的关联。
elements_zh.main_results: 阴茎 hrHPV 患病率 为 24.7% (39/158),直肠 hrHPV 患病率 为 12.5% (22/176);在两个站点进行测试的参与者中有 6.7% 患有双站点感染。HPV-18/45 是两个地点最常见的基因型组。阴茎 hrHPV 在 HIV 感染者中更常见(aPR = 2.27,p = 0.050),而在就业参与者中则不太常见(aPR = 0.25,p = 0.048)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,hrHPV 感染在肯尼亚基苏木的 MSM 中很常见,并且具有明显的位点特异性相关性。直肠细菌性 STI 与直肠 hrHPV 之间的密切关联凸显了 HPV 和 STI 综合筛查的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持扩大性别中性 HPV 疫苗接种 和病因性 STI 筛查,以降低撒哈拉以南非洲 MSM 中 HPV 相关癌症风险。综合筛查可以改善这一高危人群中 HPV 相关疾病的早期发现和预防。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是横断面的,限制了因果推断。由于样本量和潜在的混杂因素,证据强度中等,但研究结果与生物学合理性和先前的研究一致。

papers.title: High-Risk Cervical Human Papillomavirus Prevalence in a Northeast Nigeria Community: A Descriptive Study.
papers.abstract: Background: Disparities in cervical screening result in disproportionate cervical cancer burdens in populations. This study assessed cervical human papillomavirus (HPV) infection prevalence in a rural northeast Nigeria community with low access to cervical screening. Methodology: A community health outreach was conducted at a primary healthcare facility in Azare, Bauchi State, Nigeria. The women who wished to and consented to undergo gynaecological consultations were non-randomly enrolled on the study and provided their sociodemographic data and cervical specimens (Pap smear and cytobrush exfoliates in viral transport media) for the study. These were analysed cytologically and for the presence of HPV deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA). Results: Of 62 women screened (mean age 38.5 ± 9.8 years), 34 (54.8%) tested positive for HPV DNA (95% confidence interval = 43-67%). Among these positive cases, 19 had no intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM), 8 were designated atypical squamous cell of undetermined significance (ASCUS), and 6 showed low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL). In contrast, one case was high-grade SIL (HSIL). Thirty single infections were seen, HPV 16 being the commonest (18 cases), followed by HPV 18 (9 cases), while non-16, non-18 genotypes (genotypes 31, 33, 35, 39, 45, 51, 52, 56, 58, 59, 66, 67, 68), collectively termed "Others", accounted for 3 cases. Coinfections among different genotype classes (genotypes 16, 18 and Others) occurred in 4 additional cases. Most of the women had a primary education or higher (43; 69.4%), were married (53; 85.5%), and were multiparous (52; 83.9%). However, the majority had not heard about cervical cancer (35; 56.5%), while 60 (96.8%) women had never been screened previously. Conclusions: The results suggest a high prevalence of cervical HR-HPV and SIL in Azare. Improved public enlightenment and access to cervical cancer screening services may help to decrease transmission of HPV and subsequent cervical cancer in the population.

papers.title: HPV vaccination intention and its association with vaccine hesitancy and health beliefs among unvaccinated Chinese medical college students: A cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection poses a significant public health challenge, and HPV vaccination uptake among Chinese college students remains suboptimal. Therefore, it is essential to conduct ongoing, in-depth investigations into the psychological and cognitive mechanisms of HPV vaccination intention. This study aims to explore the associations among HPV vaccination intention, vaccine hesitancy, and health beliefs among Chinese medical college students. METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted from June 16 to July 16, 2024, to assess sociodemographic characteristics, vaccine hesitancy, and health belief model (HBM) among college students at Guangdong Medical University. Descriptive statistics, univariate analysis, and binary logistic regression were performed to identify factors associated with HPV vaccination intentions among unvaccinated students. RESULTS: Among 3,584 unvaccinated participants, 73.16% expressed willingness to receive the HPV vaccine. The key significant associations identified included gender (male) (OR: 0.26; 95% CI: 0.22 ~ 0.31; p < 0.001), parental occupation (employees in enterprises, commercial, and service industries (including self-employed)) (OR: 1.43; 95% CI: 1.18 ~ 1.75; p < 0.001), and information sources (hospitals or doctors) (OR: 1.37; 95% CI: 1.15 ~ 1.64; p = 0.001).
