analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study investigated HPV vaccination intention and its association with vaccine hesitancy and health beliefs among unvaccinated Chinese medical college students. Conducted at Guangdong Medical University between June and July 2024, the study used descriptive statistics, univariate analysis, and binary logistic regression to identify factors influencing vaccination intention. Among 3,584 participants, 73.16% expressed willingness to receive the HPV vaccine. Key associations included gender, parental occupation, and information sources. The study highlights the importance of perceived necessity, importance, and benefits of vaccination in shaping intention. The findings suggest that targeted interventions, such as clinician-delivered counseling and gender-neutral policies, may improve vaccine uptake. However, the study is limited to a single institution and may not be generalizable to all populations.

papers.title_zh: 未接种中国医学院校学生 HPV 疫苗接种 意向及其与 疫苗 犹豫和健康信念的关联:一项横断面研究
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection poses a significant public health challenge, and HPV vaccination uptake among Chinese college students remains suboptimal. Therefore, it is essential to conduct ongoing, in-depth investigations into the psychological and cognitive mechanisms of HPV vaccination intention. This study aims to explore the associations among HPV vaccination intention, vaccine hesitancy, and health beliefs among Chinese medical college students. METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted from June 16 to July 16, 2024, to assess sociodemographic characteristics, vaccine hesitancy, and health belief model (HBM) among college students at Guangdong Medical University. Descriptive statistics, univariate analysis, and binary logistic regression were performed to identify factors associated with HPV vaccination intentions among unvaccinated students. RESULTS: Among 3,584 unvaccinated participants, 73.16% expressed willingness to receive the HPV vaccine. The key significant associations identified included gender (male) (OR: 0.26; 95% CI: 0.22 ~ 0.31; p < 0.001), parental occupation (employees in enterprises, commercial, and service industries (including self-employed)) (OR: 1.43; 95% CI: 1.18 ~ 1.75; p < 0.001), and information sources (hospitals or doctors) (OR: 1.37; 95% CI: 1.15 ~ 1.64; p = 0.001). Vaccination intention was also directly associated with the perceived necessity (OR: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.88 ~ 0.94; p < 0.001) and importance (OR: 1.07; 95% CI: 1.03 ~ 1.10; p < 0.001) of vaccine hesitancy, as well as the perceived benefits of behavior for the HBM (OR: 1.21; 95% CI: 1.12 ~ 1.32; p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: In this sample, Chinese medical college students demonstrated a relatively high willingness to receive HPV vaccination. Willingness was positively associated with perceived necessity, importance, and benefits of vaccination. Integrating structured clinician-delivered counseling into curricula, using parental occupation data for targeted subsidies, and embedding classroom sessions comparing personal HPV risk with vaccine safety data may improve uptake. Government evaluation of gender-neutral vaccination policies and provision of male-inclusive campus services are also recommended.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染构成了重大的公共卫生挑战,而中国大学生中 HPV 疫苗接种 的吸收率仍然不理想。因此,有必要对HPV 疫苗接种意向的心理和认知机制进行持续、深入的研究。本研究旨在探讨中国医学院校学生HPV 疫苗接种意向、疫苗犹豫与健康信念之间的关联。方法:于2024年6月16日至7月16日进行横断面调查,评估广东医科大学大学生的社会人口学特征、疫苗犹豫度和健康信念模型(HBM)。通过描述性统计、单变量分析和二元逻辑回归来确定与未接种疫苗的学生中 HPV 疫苗接种 意图相关的因素。结果:在 3,584 名未接种疫苗的参与者中,73.16% 表示愿意接受 HPV 疫苗。确定的关键显着关联包括性别(男性)(OR:0.26;95% CI:0.22 ~ 0.31;p < 0.001)、父母职业(企业、商业和服务业员工(包括个体经营者))(OR:1.43;95% CI:1.18 ~ 1.75;p < 0.001)和信息来源(医院或医院)。医生)(OR:1.37;95% CI:1.15 ~ 1.64;p = 0.001)。疫苗接种 意图还与 疫苗 犹豫的感知必要性(OR:0.91;95% CI:0.88 ~ 0.94;p < 0.001)和重要性(OR:1.07;95% CI:1.03 ~ 1.10;p < 0.001)以及行为对 疫苗 的感知益处直接相关。HBM(OR:1.21;95% CI:1.12 ~ 1.32;p < 0.001)。结论:在本样本中,中国医学院校学生表现出较高的接受 HPV 疫苗接种 的意愿。意愿与 疫苗接种 的必要性、重要性和好处呈正相关。将临床医生提供的结构化咨询纳入课程,使用父母职业数据进行有针对性的补贴,以及嵌入课堂课程以比较个人 HPV 风险与 疫苗 安全数据,可能会提高采用率。还建议政府对性别中立的 疫苗接种 政策进行评估并提供包容男性的校园服务。

papers.title: Implementation and impact of primary HPV testing in cervical cancer screening: Historical perspectives and institutional experience at a large academic medical center
papers.abstract: Abstract Recognition of high‐risk human papillomavirus (HPV) as the etiologic agent in nearly all cervical cancers has fundamentally reshaped screening strategies, driving the development and adoption of highly sensitive molecular HPV assays. Over the past several decades, cervical cancer screening guidelines have shifted from primarily cytology‐based approaches toward HPV‐based modalities, with primary HPV testing now recommended as the preferred method by the American Cancer Society and anticipated to be similarly endorsed by the United States Preventive Services Task Force. This article traces the evolution of cervical cancer screening, from the original Papanicolaou test to current guideline recommendations, and discusses the logistical requirements for transitioning to a primary HPV screening system, including triage strategies for HPV‐positive cases. The authors additionally present an institutional experience of initiating primary HPV testing, highlighting its impact on cytopathology laboratory workflow and specimen volumes.

analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a historical and institutional experience article, not a systematic review or meta-analysis. It traces the evolution of cervical cancer screening guidelines and presents an institutional case study of implementing primary HPV testing.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Primary HPV testing is now the preferred screening method recommended by the American Cancer Society and anticipated to be endorsed by the United States Preventive Services Task Force, due to its high sensitivity in detecting high-risk HPV.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not explicitly discuss controversies or evidence gaps, focusing instead on the transition to primary HPV testing and its institutional impact.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The implications include the need for logistical adjustments in cytopathology laboratories to accommodate increased specimen volumes and the development of triage strategies for HPV-positive cases.

The authors present institutional experience, noting the impact on laboratory workflow and specimen volumes. The review emphasizes the endorsement of primary HPV testing by major guidelines and anticipates further adoption, though it does not address controversies or evidence gaps.

papers.source_body_en: Abstract Recognition of high‐risk human papillomavirus (HPV) as the etiologic agent in nearly all cervical cancers has fundamentally reshaped screening strategies, driving the development and adoption of highly sensitive molecular HPV assays. Over the past several decades, cervical cancer screening guidelines have shifted from primarily cytology‐based approaches toward HPV‐based modalities, with primary HPV testing now recommended as the preferred method by the American Cancer Society and anticipated to be similarly endorsed by the United States Preventive Services Task Force. This article traces the evolution of cervical cancer screening, from the original Papanicolaou test to current guideline recommendations, and discusses the logistical requirements for transitioning to a primary HPV screening system, including triage strategies for HPV‐positive cases. The authors additionally present an institutional experience of initiating primary HPV testing, highlighting its impact on cytopathology laboratory workflow and specimen volumes.

papers.title: Factors Associated with HPV Vaccination Among Japanese Women: A Cross-Sectional Study Using the 7 C Vaccination Readiness Model
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination rates in Japan declined after the suspension of the government's proactive recommendation in 2013. Vaccination behavior is influenced by knowledge as well as psychological and social factors. This study examined factors associated with HPV vaccination among Japanese women using the 7 C vaccination readiness model. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among Japanese women aged 15-49 years in February 2025. Data on demographic characteristics, HPV vaccination status, self-reported knowledge of the HPV vaccine, and 7 C vaccination readiness were collected. Factors associated with HPV vaccination were analyzed using logistic regression, with separate analyses by student status (students vs. Among 1,200 participants, 339 (28.3%) had received the HPV vaccine. Multivariable analysis showed that younger age, non-student status, greater self-reported knowledge, and higher Constraints and Compliance scores were independently associated with vaccination. Associations were observed for self-reported knowledge (OR 2.12, 95% CI 1.88-2.38, p < 0.001), Constraints (OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.27-1.76, p < 0.001), and Compliance (OR 1.32, 95% CI 1.15-1.51, p < 0.001). In analyses stratified by student status, greater self-reported knowledge and higher Constraints and Compliance scores were significantly associated with vaccination in both groups. These findings suggest that HPV vaccine education may include vaccine-related information and practical guidance on vaccination sites, costs, eligibility, and appointment procedures. It may also include opportunities to discuss vaccination-related concerns to address barriers reflected in Constraints, as well as balanced explanations of public-health measures intended to promote high vaccination coverage to address attitudes captured by Compliance.

papers.title: The oral microbiota in oral squamous cell carcinoma: unravelling mechanisms and clinical potential
papers.abstract: Originating in the mucosal lining of the mouth, oral squamous cell carcinoma is the most common malignancy of the head and neck regions. Its pathogenesis is multifactorial, involving environmental exposures, genetic susceptibility, and lifestyle-related risk factors. Increasing evidence indicates that oral microbial dysbiosis contributes to the initiation and progression of OSCC. analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the oral microbiota in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), examining its role in carcinogenesis mechanisms and clinical potential. The central question involves understanding how microbial dysbiosis contributes to OSCC initiation and progression.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review provides an integrated overview of the oral microbiome in OSCC, focusing on composition, protective roles, stability factors, and carcinogenesis mechanisms. It also discusses microbiome-targeted strategies as potential adjunctive approaches.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: There is consensus that oral microbial dysbiosis contributes to OSCC initiation and progression. Pathogenic bacteria like Porphyromonas gingivalis and Treponema denticola activate oncogenic pathways, while high-risk HPV and Candida albicans act as cofactors. The oral microbiome is recognized as a source of non-invasive biomarkers.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not explicitly mention controversies or evidence gaps, but it highlights the need for further research on microbiome-targeted strategies and the specific mechanisms by which different microbial components contribute to carcinogenesis.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests microbiome-targeted strategies, including prebiotics, probiotics, and postbiotics, as promising adjunctive approaches to restore microbial balance and reduce tumor-promoting inflammation. It also emphasizes the potential of the oral microbiome as a source of non-invasive biomarkers.

It discusses the shift toward pathogenic bacterial communities, such as Porphyromonas gingivalis, which activate oncogenic pathways, and the involvement of high-risk HPV and Candida albicans as cofactors. The review emphasizes the oral microbiome's potential as a source of non-invasive biomarkers and proposes microbiome-targeted strategies like prebiotics, probiotics, and postbiotics to restore balance and reduce inflammation. The integrated overview provides insights into mechanisms and clinical applications for OSCC management.

papers.title_zh: 口腔鳞状细胞癌中的口腔微生物群:揭示机制和临床潜力
papers.source_body_en: Originating in the mucosal lining of the mouth, oral squamous cell carcinoma is the most common malignancy of the head and neck regions. Its pathogenesis is multifactorial, involving environmental exposures, genetic susceptibility, and lifestyle-related risk factors. Increasing evidence indicates that oral microbial dysbiosis contributes to the initiation and progression of OSCC. Under healthy conditions, the oral cavity harbors a diverse and functionally balanced microbial ecosystem that maintains mucosal integrity, supports immune homeostasis, and prevents colonization by pathogenic species. Disruption of this equilibrium, known as oral dysbiosis, is increasingly recognized as a key event in oral carcinogenesis. In OSCC, a shift toward pathogenic and pro-inflammatory microbial communities has been consistently observed, particularly involving periodontal bacteria such as Porphyromonas gingivalis, Treponema denticola, and Fusobacterium nucleatum. These organisms contribute to tumor progression by activating inflammatory and oncogenic signaling pathways, including NF-κB, STAT3, and PI3K/Akt; suppressing apoptosis; inducing epithelial–mesenchymal transition; and immune evasion, thereby creating a tumor-promoting microenvironment. In addition to bacterial dysbiosis, viral and fungal components of the oral microbiome may act as important cofactors in OSCC. High-risk Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) and human papillomavirus (HPV) have been implicated in disrupting tumor suppressor pathways, causing genomic instability, and modulating the immune response. Fungal species, particularly Candida albicans, may further contribute by producing carcinogenic metabolites and inducing chronic inflammation. This review provides an integrated overview of the oral microbiome in OSCC, focusing on the composition and protective roles of the core microbiota, factors influencing microbial stability, and mechanisms by which dysbiosis contributes to carcinogenesis. It also highlights the oral microbiome as a potential source of non-invasive biomarkers and discusses microbiome-targeted strategies, including prebiotics, probiotics, and postbiotics, as promising adjunctive approaches to restore microbial balance and reduce tumor-promoting inflammation.
papers.abstract_zh: 口腔鳞状细胞癌起源于口腔粘膜,是头颈部最常见的恶性肿瘤。其发病机制是多因素的,涉及环境暴露、遗传易感性和生活方式相关的危险因素。越来越多的证据表明口腔微生物失调有助于口腔鳞癌的发生和进展。在健康条件下,口腔拥有多样化且功能平衡的微生物生态系统,可维持粘膜完整性,支持免疫稳态,并防止病原菌定植。这种平衡的破坏被称为口腔生态失调,越来越多地被认为是口腔癌发生的关键事件。在口腔鳞癌中,一直观察到向致病性和促炎性微生物群落的转变,特别是涉及牙周细菌,如牙龈卟啉单胞菌、齿垢密螺旋体和具核梭杆菌。这些生物体通过激活炎症和致癌信号通路(包括 NF-κB、STAT3 和 PI3K/Akt)来促进肿瘤进展;抑制细胞凋亡;诱导上皮-间质转化;和免疫逃避,从而创造一个促进肿瘤的微环境。除了细菌失调外,口腔微生物组的病毒和真菌成分可能是口腔鳞癌的重要辅助因子。高风险 Epstein-Barr 病毒 (EBV) 和 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 与破坏肿瘤抑制途径、导致基因组不稳定和调节 免疫应答 有关。真菌物种,特别是白色念珠菌,可能进一步产生致癌代谢物并诱发慢性炎症。本综述对口腔鳞癌的口腔微生物群进行了综合概述,重点关注核心微生物群的组成和保护作用、影响微生物稳定性的因素以及生态失调导致癌变的机制。它还强调口腔微生物组作为非侵入性生物标志物的潜在来源,并讨论了针对微生物组的策略,包括益生元、益生菌和后生元,作为恢复微生物平衡和减少促肿瘤炎症的有前途的辅助方法。

papers.title: Evaluating the feasibility of using SMS to recruit women for cervical cancer screening in Rwanda: A pilot study.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study evaluates the feasibility and acceptability of using short message service (SMS) as a recruitment strategy for cervical cancer screening in an urban sector of Kigali, Rwanda. METHODS: This pilot invited 300 women who had not attended cervical screening during the local campaign and had access to a mobile phone to provide a mobile number for cervical cancer screening invitation. Up to three SMSs were sent out, inviting women to visit a local health center for cervical cancer screening. There, attendance rates were recorded, self-collected vaginal samples for human papillomavirus testing were taken, and a short survey was administered. Those who did not attend received a phone call and were surveyed on reasons for non-attendance. A descriptive analysis was used to detail attendance rates and evaluate survey questions on the perceived feasibility and acceptability of the intervention. RESULTS: A total of 294 women met the inclusion criteria. Of these women, 86.4% (254/294) attended the health center for cervical cancer screening and 92.9% (236/254) of attendees reported they participated due to the SMS reminder. Survey items evaluating acceptability and feasibility indicated high message comprehension, strong attendance following a single SMS prompt, and high agreement that SMS was a helpful reminder to attend screening. Most non-attendees reported having received the SMSs but not attending due to circumstantial factors. CONCLUSION: SMS recruitment was highly feasible and well accepted in this pilot study in an urban sector of Kigali, Rwanda. Future research should aim to understand the efficacy of this strategy compared to usual recruitment methods across diverse settings in Rwanda.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本研究评估了在卢旺达基加利市区使用短信服务 (SMS) 作为 宫颈癌 筛查招募策略的可行性和可接受性。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该试点项目邀请了 300 名在当地活动期间未参加宫颈筛查且能够使用手机的女性提供手机号码以进行 宫颈癌 筛查邀请。最多发出了三条短信,邀请女性前往当地卫生中心进行 宫颈癌 筛查。在那里,记录了出勤率,采集了自我采集的阴道样本用于 人乳头瘤病毒 测试,并进行了一项简短的调查。那些没有出席的人会接到电话并接受调查,了解缺席的原因。使用描述性分析来详细说明出勤率并评估有关干预措施的可行性和可接受性的调查问题。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 共有 294 名女性符合纳入标准。在这些女性中,86.4% (254/294) 前往健康中心进行 宫颈癌 筛查,92.9% (236/254) 的参与者表示由于短信提醒而参与了筛查。评估可接受性和可行性的调查项目表明,消息理解程度高,单个短信提示后的出席率很高,并且高度同意短信是参加筛选的有用提醒。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 大多数未出席者表示已收到短信,但由于环境因素而没有出席。未来的研究应旨在了解该策略与卢旺达不同环境中通常的招募方法相比的有效性。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 在卢旺达基加利城市地区的这项试点研究中,短信招聘非常可行并得到广泛接受。

papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVE: This study evaluates the feasibility and acceptability of using short message service (SMS) as a recruitment strategy for cervical cancer screening in an urban sector of Kigali, Rwanda. METHODS: This pilot invited 300 women who had not attended cervical screening during the local campaign and had access to a mobile phone to provide a mobile number for cervical cancer screening invitation. Up to three SMSs were sent out, inviting women to visit a local health center for cervical cancer screening. There, attendance rates were recorded, self-collected vaginal samples for human papillomavirus testing were taken, and a short survey was administered. Those who did not attend received a phone call and were surveyed on reasons for non-attendance. A descriptive analysis was used to detail attendance rates and evaluate survey questions on the perceived feasibility and acceptability of the intervention. RESULTS: A total of 294 women met the inclusion criteria. Of these women, 86.4% (254/294) attended the health center for cervical cancer screening and 92.9% (236/254) of attendees reported they participated due to the SMS reminder. Survey items evaluating acceptability and feasibility indicated high message comprehension, strong attendance following a single SMS prompt, and high agreement that SMS was a helpful reminder to attend screening. Most non-attendees reported having received the SMSs but not attending due to circumstantial factors. CONCLUSION: SMS recruitment was highly feasible and well accepted in this pilot study in an urban sector of Kigali, Rwanda. Future research should aim to understand the efficacy of this strategy compared to usual recruitment methods across diverse settings in Rwanda.

papers.title: Health economic impact and cost threshold for switching from bivalent to nonavalent HPV vaccination for preadolescent girls in KwaZulu Natal, South Africa: A mathematical modeling analysis accounting for the HIV epidemic.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus bivalent (2vHPV) and nonavalent (9vHPV) vaccines protect against HPV types causing 70% and 90% of cervical cancers, respectively. South African guidelines recommend vaccinating girls ages 9-14 with one dose of 2vHPV. Switching recommendations to 9vHPV could avert more cervical cancer burden, but the cost-effectiveness and cost-threshold of 9vHPV in South Africa is unknown. METHODS: Using a validated compartmental HPV and HIV transmission model parameterized to KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, we simulated scenarios of 2vHPV and 9vHPV implementation over 100 years with two doses (72% coverage) and one dose (80% and 90% coverage) with lifelong or waning single-dose vaccine efficacy. We evaluated cervical cancer cases and deaths averted. We also estimated the maximum cost/dose for 9vHPV to be cost-effective using willingness-to-pay thresholds from $500/DALY averted to $3,015/DALY averted (2023 USD). We also assessed the incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) of 9vHPV at current costs ($110/dose) compared to 2vHPV ($9.23/dose). RESULTS: Single-dose 9vHPV at 80% coverage could avert 7.9% more cervical cancer cases and 6.4% more deaths than 2vHPV (lifelong efficacy). The maximum 9vHPV price to be cost-effective (lifelong efficacy, 80% coverage) ranged from $15 ($500/DALY averted threshold) to $45/dose ($3,015/DALY averted threshold). At current market costs, single-dose 9vHPV at 90% coverage exceeds commonly used cost-effective thresholds with ICERs of $10,480/DALY averted (lifelong efficacy) and $8,806/DALY averted (waning efficacy). CONCLUSION: Implementing 9vHPV can result in a greater reduction in cervical cancer burden than 2vHPV, but vaccine costs need to be reduced for 9vHPV to be cost-effective in KwaZulu-Natal.

papers.title_zh: 南非夸祖鲁纳塔尔省青春期前女孩从二价 HPV 疫苗接种 转换为非价 HPV 疫苗接种 的健康经济影响和成本阈值:针对艾滋病毒流行的数学模型分析。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus bivalent (2vHPV) and nonavalent (9vHPV) vaccines protect against HPV types causing 70% and 90% of cervical cancers, respectively. South African guidelines recommend vaccinating girls ages 9-14 with one dose of 2vHPV. Switching recommendations to 9vHPV could avert more cervical cancer burden, but the cost-effectiveness and cost-threshold of 9vHPV in South Africa is unknown. METHODS: Using a validated compartmental HPV and HIV transmission model parameterized to KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, we simulated scenarios of 2vHPV and 9vHPV implementation over 100 years with two doses (72% coverage) and one dose (80% and 90% coverage) with lifelong or waning single-dose vaccine efficacy. We evaluated cervical cancer cases and deaths averted. We also estimated the maximum cost/dose for 9vHPV to be cost-effective using willingness-to-pay thresholds from $500/DALY averted to $3,015/DALY averted (2023 USD). We also assessed the incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) of 9vHPV at current costs ($110/dose) compared to 2vHPV ($9.23/dose). RESULTS: Single-dose 9vHPV at 80% coverage could avert 7.9% more cervical cancer cases and 6.4% more deaths than 2vHPV (lifelong efficacy). The maximum 9vHPV price to be cost-effective (lifelong efficacy, 80% coverage) ranged from $15 ($500/DALY averted threshold) to $45/dose ($3,015/DALY averted threshold). At current market costs, single-dose 9vHPV at 90% coverage exceeds commonly used cost-effective thresholds with ICERs of $10,480/DALY averted (lifelong efficacy) and $8,806/DALY averted (waning efficacy). CONCLUSION: Implementing 9vHPV can result in a greater reduction in cervical cancer burden than 2vHPV, but vaccine costs need to be reduced for 9vHPV to be cost-effective in KwaZulu-Natal.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:人乳头瘤病毒 二价 (2vHPV) 和非价 (9vHPV) 疫苗 可预防分别导致 70% 和 90% 宫颈癌 的 HPV 类型。南非指南建议为 9-14 岁的女孩接种一剂 2vHPV 疫苗。将建议改为 9vHPV 可以避免更多的 宫颈癌 负担,但 9vHPV 在南非的成本效益和成本阈值尚不清楚。方法:使用参数化于南非夸祖鲁-纳塔尔省的经过验证的区室 HPV 和 HIV 传播 模型,我们模拟了 100 年来 2vHPV 和 9vHPV 实施的场景,采用两剂(72% 覆盖率)和一剂(80% 和 90% 覆盖率),单剂 疫苗 疗效终身或减弱。我们评估了 宫颈癌 病例和避免的死亡。我们还使用支付意愿阈值从 500 美元/避免伤残调整生命年到 3,015 美元/避免伤残调整生命年(2023 美元)估计 9vHPV 的最大成本/剂量具有成本效益。我们还评估了 9vHPV 按当前成本(110 美元/剂)与 2vHPV(9.23 美元/剂)相比的增量成本效益比 (ICER)。结果:单剂 9vHPV 覆盖率达到 80%,与 2vHPV 相比,可避免多 7.9% 的 宫颈癌 病例和多 6.4% 的死亡(终身疗效)。具有成本效益的 9vHPV 最高价格(终身疗效,80% 覆盖率)范围从 15 美元(500 美元/DALY 避免阈值)到 45 美元/剂量(3,015 美元/DALY 避免阈值)。按照目前的市场成本,覆盖率达 90% 的单剂 9vHPV 超过了常用的成本效益阈值,避免的 ICER 为 10,480 美元/DALY(终身功效)和 8,806 美元/DALY(功效减弱)。结论:与 2vHPV 相比,实施 9vHPV 可以更大程度地减少 宫颈癌 负担,但需要降低 疫苗 成本才能使 9vHPV 在夸祖鲁-纳塔尔省具有成本效益。

papers.title: HPV vaccination and the risk of cancer in males
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The efficacy and effectiveness of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine in reducing the risk of invasive cervical cancer in females and head and neck cancer (HNC) in males have been demonstrated. However, the relationship between HPV vaccination in males and the subsequent risk of other potentially HPV-associated cancers are lacking. METHODS: We used the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network to conduct a retrospective cohort study. Males aged 9 to 45 years who did or did not receive the HPV vaccine between 2006 and 2024 were included. We assessed the association between HPV vaccination and the risk of cancer, carcinoma in situ, and precancerous lesions at: penis, anus, head and neck cancer (HNC), lungs, esophagus, stomach, prostate, colorectum. RESULTS: Males with HPV vaccination (n = 397,856) have lower hazard ratio (HR) for HNC. Some other potentially HPV-associated cancers also have lower HR in HPV-vaccinated males, including lung cancer, prostate cancer, and colorectal cancer. Vaccinated males were less likely to develop some precancerous lesions of anus, head and neck, esophagus, and stomach. CONCLUSIONS: Among males ages 9 to 45, HPV vaccination significantly reduces the risk of certain cancers and precancerous lesions. Further studies are needed to evaluate the protective mechanisms of HPV vaccination against various cancers.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cohort study investigated the association between HPV vaccination and cancer risk in males aged 9 to 45 years using the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network. Among 397,856 vaccinated males, significantly lower hazard ratios were observed for head and neck cancer, as well as for lung, prostate, and colorectal cancers. Vaccinated males also showed reduced risk of precancerous lesions in the anus, head and neck, esophagus, and stomach. The findings demonstrate that HPV vaccination significantly reduces the risk of multiple potentially HPV-associated cancers and precancerous lesions in males, extending beyond the previously established benefits for cervical cancer in females and head and neck cancer in males. While the results support broader vaccination recommendations, further research is needed to elucidate the protective mechanisms against various cancers.

papers.title_zh: HPV 疫苗接种 与男性患癌症的风险
papers.source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: The efficacy and effectiveness of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine in reducing the risk of invasive cervical cancer in females and head and neck cancer (HNC) in males have been demonstrated. However, the relationship between HPV vaccination in males and the subsequent risk of other potentially HPV-associated cancers are lacking. METHODS: We used the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network to conduct a retrospective cohort study. Males aged 9 to 45 years who did or did not receive the HPV vaccine between 2006 and 2024 were included. We assessed the association between HPV vaccination and the risk of cancer, carcinoma in situ, and precancerous lesions at: penis, anus, head and neck cancer (HNC), lungs, esophagus, stomach, prostate, colorectum. RESULTS: Males with HPV vaccination (n = 397,856) have lower hazard ratio (HR) for HNC. Some other potentially HPV-associated cancers also have lower HR in HPV-vaccinated males, including lung cancer, prostate cancer, and colorectal cancer. Vaccinated males were less likely to develop some precancerous lesions of anus, head and neck, esophagus, and stomach. CONCLUSIONS: Among males ages 9 to 45, HPV vaccination significantly reduces the risk of certain cancers and precancerous lesions. Further studies are needed to evaluate the protective mechanisms of HPV vaccination against various cancers.

papers.title: Insights of Vietnamese American Women on Cervical Cancer Screening and HPV Self-Sampling
papers.abstract: Abstract Vietnamese American women experience one of the highest cervical cancer incidence and mortality rates in the United States, largely due to low screening uptake. To inform strategies for reducing this burden, we explored the experiences and attitudes toward cervical cancer screening, including the perceptions on Human papillomavirus (HPV) self-sampling, among Vietnamese American women. Between April 2023 and July 2024, we conducted four focus groups and three individual interviews with 21 Vietnamese American women aged 30–65 residing in Southern California. Participants were stratified by nativity and age: Vietnam-born ages 30–49, Vietnam-born ages 50–65, and U.S.-born ages 30–49. All focus groups and interviews were conducted online and moderated by a bilingual researcher using semi-structured guides. Participants also watched videos on screening methods and shared their views. The discussions were recorded, transcribed, and thematically analyzed using Dedoose 10.0.59. Three themes emerged, with no differences across strata. First, structural and psychosocial barriers to physician-based screening were identified. Second, HPV self-sampling was viewed as a potential solution to these barriers, though there were mixed opinions regarding one’s ability to self-sample correctly, potential discomfort, and logistics related to obtaining a device and mailing samples. Third, other opportunities to improve screening uptake were identified, including a high willingness to undergo screening, the potential to capitalize on the strong trust in physicians, and the opportunities to leverage community-based resources. Our findings suggest that a multifaceted approach integrating HPV self-sampling and provider and community engagement has the potential to improve cervical cancer screening uptake among Vietnamese American women.
papers.journal: Journal of Racial and Ethnic Health Disparities

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2023 年 4 月至 2024 年 7 月期间,我们对居住在南加州的 21 名 30-65 岁越南裔美国女性进行了四次焦点小组访谈和三次个人访谈。参与者按出生地和年龄进行分层:越南出生的年龄为 30-49 岁,越南出生的年龄为 50-65 岁,美国出生的年龄为 30-49 岁。

papers.title: Opportunities and Barriers to HPV Vaccination Among Men Who Have Sex with Men and Related Sexual and Gender Minority Populations: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Clustering Analysis Using a Socio-Ecological Framework
papers.abstract: Background: Men who have sex with men (MSM) experience a disproportionate burden of human papillomavirus (HPV)-related disease, yet vaccination uptake remains uneven. With MSM as the key population of interest, this review synthesized evidence on uptake, willingness, multilevel barriers and opportunities, and vaccine-oriented outcomes among MSM and related sexual and gender minority populations when MSM-relevant findings could be extracted. Methods: Six databases were searched for original English- or Chinese-language studies published from 1 January 2010 to 31 December 2025. Findings were synthesized narratively. Barriers and opportunities were mapped using a five-level socio-ecological model; study-level willingness–uptake patterns were explored using K-means clustering as an exploratory analysis among the nine studies reporting both outcomes; and genotype-specific and immunogenicity findings were summarized separately. Results: Fifty-three studies involving 169,241 participants were included; 87.2% of participants were MSM, and 79% of studies were cross-sectional. Barriers and opportunities occurred across individual, provider-related interpersonal, organizational/institutional, community, and policy/societal levels. Recurrent paired mechanisms involved knowledge and trust, provider recommendation and communication, service accessibility, community support, and eligibility and affordability. Nine studies contributed data to the exploratory clustering analysis; seven fell into low-uptake clusters, including three with high willingness but low uptake, which may indicate a possible study-level implementation gap. Two studies reporting genotype prevalence and antibody responses provided limited biological context supporting vaccination before exposure and suggesting potential benefit from catch-up vaccination. Discussion: Among MSM and related sexual and gender minority populations, HPV vaccination is shaped by interacting individual and structural conditions, with MSM remaining the principal focus of the evidence base. Improving uptake is likely to require complementary strategies: universal, gender-neutral routine vaccination in adolescence before their sexual debut, and targeted catch-up for MSM who missed routine vaccination, supported by trusted provider endorsement, convenient service delivery, community engagement, and inclusive, affordable policy. The thematic counts were study-level and unweighted, and the nine-study clustering analysis was exploratory rather than definitive.

Methods: Six databases were searched for original English- or Chinese-language studies published from 1 January 2010 to 31 December 2025. Findings were synthesized narratively. Barriers and opportunities were mapped using a five-level socio-ecological model; study-level willingness–uptake patterns were explored using K-means clustering as an exploratory analysis among the nine studies reporting both outcomes; and genotype-specific and immunogenicity findings were summarized separately. Results: Fifty-three studies involving 169,241 participants were included; 87.2% of participants were MSM, and 79% of studies were cross-sectional. Barriers and opportunities occurred across individual, provider-related interpersonal, organizational/institutional, community, and policy/societal levels. Recurrent paired mechanisms involved knowledge and trust, provider recommendation and communication, service accessibility, community support, and eligibility and affordability. Nine studies contributed data to the exploratory clustering analysis; seven fell into low-uptake clusters, including three with high willingness but low uptake, which may indicate a possible study-level implementation gap. Two studies reporting genotype prevalence and antibody responses provided limited biological context supporting vaccination before exposure and suggesting potential benefit from catch-up vaccination. Discussion: Among MSM and related sexual and gender minority populations, HPV vaccination is shaped by interacting individual and structural conditions, with MSM remaining the principal focus of the evidence base. Improving uptake is likely to require complementary strategies: universal, gender-neutral routine vaccination in adolescence before their sexual debut, and targeted catch-up for MSM who missed routine vaccination, supported by trusted provider endorsement, convenient service delivery, community engagement, and inclusive, affordable policy. The thematic counts were study-level and unweighted, and the nine-study clustering analysis was exploratory rather than definitive.

papers.title_zh: 男男性行为者和相关性少数群体中 HPV 疫苗接种 的机会和障碍:使用社会生态框架的系统回顾和探索性聚类分析
papers.source_body_en: Background: Men who have sex with men (MSM) experience a disproportionate burden of human papillomavirus (HPV)-related disease, yet vaccination uptake remains uneven. With MSM as the key population of interest, this review synthesized evidence on uptake, willingness, multilevel barriers and opportunities, and vaccine-oriented outcomes among MSM and related sexual and gender minority populations when MSM-relevant findings could be extracted. Methods: Six databases were searched for original English- or Chinese-language studies published from 1 January 2010 to 31 December 2025. Findings were synthesized narratively. Barriers and opportunities were mapped using a five-level socio-ecological model; study-level willingness–uptake patterns were explored using K-means clustering as an exploratory analysis among the nine studies reporting both outcomes; and genotype-specific and immunogenicity findings were summarized separately. Results: Fifty-three studies involving 169,241 participants were included; 87.2% of participants were MSM, and 79% of studies were cross-sectional. Barriers and opportunities occurred across individual, provider-related interpersonal, organizational/institutional, community, and policy/societal levels. Recurrent paired mechanisms involved knowledge and trust, provider recommendation and communication, service accessibility, community support, and eligibility and affordability. Nine studies contributed data to the exploratory clustering analysis; seven fell into low-uptake clusters, including three with high willingness but low uptake, which may indicate a possible study-level implementation gap. Two studies reporting genotype prevalence and antibody responses provided limited biological context supporting vaccination before exposure and suggesting potential benefit from catch-up vaccination. Discussion: Among MSM and related sexual and gender minority populations, HPV vaccination is shaped by interacting individual and structural conditions, with MSM remaining the principal focus of the evidence base. Improving uptake is likely to require complementary strategies: universal, gender-neutral routine vaccination in adolescence before their sexual debut, and targeted catch-up for MSM who missed routine vaccination, supported by trusted provider endorsement, convenient service delivery, community engagement, and inclusive, affordable policy. The thematic counts were study-level and unweighted, and the nine-study clustering analysis was exploratory rather than definitive.

papers.title: Allele-specific chromatin modifications of HPV-associated extrachromosomal DNAs in cervical cancer
papers.abstract: Abstract Cervical cancer, a human papillomavirus (HPV) driven malignancy, is the fourth deadliest cancer in females. Approximately 25% of primary cervical cancers contain circular structures called extrachromosomal DNAs (ecDNAs), which can be entirely composed of human DNA (human-only ecDNAs) or a combination of HPV and human DNA sequences (HPV-human hybrid ecDNAs). Human-only ecDNAs harbour cancer-driving oncogenes, but epigenetic differences between human-only and HPV-human hybrid ecDNAs are unexplored. Here we report that 30% of cervical cancers contained at least one ecDNA. HPV-human hybrid ecDNAs contained more active enhancers and promoters than human-only ecDNAs and invariably contained the HPV oncogenes E6 and E7 . These ecDNAs also contained an allelic hypomethylation region associated with putative human promoters, as well as enrichments for motifs associated with recombination hotspots. By leveraging long-read WGS phasing data to separate ChIP-seq data into alleles, we revealed allele-specific peaks in enhancers and promoters on ecDNAs, of which HPV-human hybrid ecDNAs contained a higher density. Overall, we found HPV-human hybrid and human-only ecDNAs differed in their regulation, often at an allele-specific level. Our study more firmly establishes the importance of epigenome disruption in cervical cancer and how structural variation, particularly surrounding HPV integration sites, may shape the surrounding regulatory architecture.

papers.title: HPV Vaccination Knowledge, Perceptions and Beliefs Among School Health and Nutrition Supervisors in Bahawalpur District, Pakistan: A Cross- Sectional Study
papers.abstract: Abstract Cervical cancer, predominantly caused by Human Papillomavirus (HPV), remains the fourth most common cancer in women globally, with over 90% of deaths occurring in low- and middle-income countries. School Health and Nutrition Supervisors (SHNS) are the frontline school health cadre whose advocacy quality directly influences HPV vaccination uptake, and their knowledge and the adequacy of health system training targeting them is largely unexamined. This cross-sectional census survey used a validated structured self-administered questionnaire to assess HPV vaccination knowledge, perceptions and beliefs among all 58 actively deployed SHNS across 21 Union Councils of Bahawalpur District, South Punjab, Pakistan (September 2025 to April 2026). Respondents were predominantly male (69.0%), above 40 years of age (79.3%) and held postgraduate qualifications (98.3%). While 96.6% correctly identified the vaccination target age group and 82.8% recognised pre-debut vaccine efficacy, 55.2% harboured the systemic misconception that HPV vaccination provides 100% protection against cervical cancer — a belief most plausibly attributable to flawed or incomplete training content rather than individual inattentiveness, given that 82.8% receive training updates at least annually. Only 37.9% knew the correct two-dose schedule and 41.4% recognised the continuing necessity of post-vaccination cervical cancer screening. All 58 supervisors (100%) had recommended HPV vaccination in the previous 12 months. Education, gender, school type and geographic location were significant predictors of knowledge. These findings demonstrate that a motivated, well-educated workforce is being systematically under-informed by inadequate training content, with direct implications for the quality and clinical accuracy of vaccine promotion delivered to parents and students. Urgent reform of HPV training content, school-level communication protocols and locally adapted Urdu-language materials is required.

papers.abstract_original: Abstract Cervical cancer, predominantly caused by Human Papillomavirus (HPV), remains the fourth most common cancer in women globally, with over 90% of deaths occurring in low- and middle-income countries. School Health and Nutrition Supervisors (SHNS) are the frontline school health cadre whose advocacy quality directly influences HPV vaccination uptake, and their knowledge and the adequacy of health system training targeting them is largely unexamined. This cross-sectional census survey used a validated structured self-administered questionnaire to assess HPV vaccination knowledge, perceptions and beliefs among all 58 actively deployed SHNS across 21 Union Councils of Bahawalpur District, South Punjab, Pakistan (September 2025 to April 2026). Respondents were predominantly male (69.0%), above 40 years of age (79.3%) and held postgraduate qualifications (98.3%). While 96.6% correctly identified the vaccination target age group and 82.8% recognised pre-debut vaccine efficacy, 55.2% harboured the systemic misconception that HPV vaccination provides 100% protection against cervical cancer — a belief most plausibly attributable to flawed or incomplete training content rather than individual inattentiveness, given that 82.8% receive training updates at least annually. Only 37.9% knew the correct two-dose schedule and 41.4% recognised the continuing necessity of post-vaccination cervical cancer screening. All 58 supervisors (100%) had recommended HPV vaccination in the previous 12 months. Education, gender, school type and geographic location were significant predictors of knowledge. These findings demonstrate that a motivated, well-educated workforce is being systematically under-informed by inadequate training content, with direct implications for the quality and clinical accuracy of vaccine promotion delivered to parents and students. Urgent reform of HPV training content, school-level communication protocols and locally adapted Urdu-language materials is required.

papers.title: Predictors of routine HPV-based cervical cancer screening adoption in federally qualified health centers within a multi-state practice research network 2012-2022: retrospective observational study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer screening guidelines in the United States have evolved with the introduction of human papillomavirus (HPV)-based modalities, including co-testing in 2012 and primary HPV testing in 2018, in addition to Pap-only screening. However, adoption of these modalities in federally qualified health centers (FQHCs) has been underexplored. We examined longitudinal patterns of HPV-based cervical cancer screening adoption (e.g., proportion screened with co- and primary HPV testing) across three FQHC systems in Washington and Idaho and explored factors associated with receipt of HPV-based modalities. METHODS: Using electronic health record data, we identified the first routine cervical cancer screening among 11,316 individuals from 2012-2022 across 25 clinics within three FQHCs. Screening modality at the screening was classified as Pap-only, co-testing, or primary HPV testing. We quantified the proportion of each screening modality by year and FQHC from 2012-2022 and used multivariable logistic regression to estimate associations of factors (age, race, ethnicity, rurality, insurance status, primary care visits, and FQHC) with HPV-based screening for 2012-2018 and 2018-2022 guideline periods. RESULTS: The proportion of up-to-date screening in 2022 was 34.0%, 22.7%, and 37.6% for FQHCs A, B, and C, respectively. Among individuals receiving their first routine screening from 2012-2022, 59.1% underwent Pap-only, 38.8% co-testing, and 2.0% primary HPV testing, respectively. Pap-only was nearly universal in 2012 but declined to 57.0% by 2022, while co-testing increased to 41.0%. Primary HPV testing remained < 7.0% across all years and FQHCs. During the 2012-2018 guideline period, odds of co-testing (vs. Pap-only) were higher among Hispanic (aOR = 1.56; 95% CI, 1.35-1.80) and Black (aOR = 1.64; 95% CI, 1.18-2.28) individuals and screened at FQHC C (aOR = 4.21; 95% CI, 3.41-5.22). Odds were lower among rural (aOR = 0.20; 95% CI, 0.17-0.24) and uninsured patients (aOR = 0.51; 95% CI, 0.44-0.58). From 2018-2022, odds of co-testing were higher among individuals aged 40-59 and Black, lower at FQHC B (aOR = 0.48; 95% CI, 0.37-0.63), and higher at FQHC C (aOR = 1.34; 95% CI, 1.06-1.68). CONCLUSIONS: Adoption of HPV-based screening modalities increased over time and varied by patients' rurality, race, and ethnicity. Lower adoption in some organizations may reflect limited capacity/resources for adopting newer screening modalities, which could impact equitable access to screening.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 美国的 宫颈癌 筛查指南随着基于 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 的模式的引入而不断发展,除了巴氏涂片筛查之外,还包括 2012 年的联合检测和 2018 年的初级 HPV 检测。然而,在联邦合格的健康中心 (FQHC) 中采用这些模式的探索尚未充分。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们研究了华盛顿州和爱达荷州三个 FQHC 系统中基于 HPV 的 宫颈癌 筛查采用的纵向模式,并探讨了与接受基于 HPV 的方式相关的因素。利用电子健康记录数据,我们对 2012 年至 2022 年期间 3 个 FQHC 内 25 个诊所的 11,316 名个人进行了首次例行 宫颈癌 筛查。
elements_zh.methods: 筛查时的筛查方式分为仅巴氏涂片检查、联合检测或初次 HPV 检测。我们按年份和 FQHC 量化了 2012-2022 年每种筛查方式的比例,并使用多变量逻辑回归来估计因素(年龄、种族、民族、农村、保险状况、初级保健就诊和 FQHC)与 2012-2018 年和 2018-2022 年指南期间基于 HPV 的筛查的关联。
elements_zh.main_results: FQHC A、B、C 2022 年最新筛查比例分别为 34.0%、22.7% 和 37.6%。在 2012 年至 2022 年接受首次常规筛查的个体中,分别有 59.1% 的人接受了巴氏涂片检查,38.8% 的人接受了联合检测,2.0% 的人接受了初次 HPV 检测。2012 年,仅进行巴氏涂片检查几乎已普及,但到 2022 年,这一比例下降至 57.0%,而联合检测则增加至 41.0%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 随着时间的推移,基于 HPV 的筛查方式的采用不断增加,并且因患者的乡村、种族和民族而异。一些组织采用率较低可能反映出采用新筛查方式的能力/资源有限,这可能会影响筛查的公平性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为改善 FQHC 中 HPV 筛查的公平性所做的努力提供了信息,特别是对于农村和未参保人群。了解与采用相关的因素可以指导有针对性的干预措施,以提高筛查的采用率并减少 宫颈癌 差异。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于华盛顿和爱达荷州的三个 FQHC 系统,这可能会限制对其他地区或医疗机构的推广。尽管存在这些限制,大样本量和纵向设计为理解基于 HPV 的筛查采用模式提供了适度的证据。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 美国的 宫颈癌 筛查指南随着基于 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 的模式的引入而不断发展,除了巴氏涂片筛查之外,还包括 2012 年的联合检测和 2018 年的初级 HPV 检测。然而,在联邦合格的健康中心 (FQHC) 中采用这些模式的探索尚未充分。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们研究了华盛顿州和爱达荷州三个 FQHC 系统中基于 HPV 的 宫颈癌 筛查采用的纵向模式,并探讨了与接受基于 HPV 的方式相关的因素。利用电子健康记录数据,我们对 2012 年至 2022 年期间 3 个 FQHC 内 25 个诊所的 11,316 名个人进行了首次例行 宫颈癌 筛查。
analysis_zh.methods: 筛查时的筛查方式分为仅巴氏涂片检查、联合检测或初次 HPV 检测。我们按年份和 FQHC 量化了 2012-2022 年每种筛查方式的比例,并使用多变量逻辑回归来估计因素(年龄、种族、民族、农村、保险状况、初级保健就诊和 FQHC)与 2012-2018 年和 2018-2022 年指南期间基于 HPV 的筛查的关联。
analysis_zh.main_results: FQHC A、B、C 2022 年最新筛查比例分别为 34.0%、22.7% 和 37.6%。在 2012 年至 2022 年接受首次常规筛查的个体中,分别有 59.1% 的人接受了巴氏涂片检查,38.8% 的人接受了联合检测,2.0% 的人接受了初次 HPV 检测。2012 年,仅进行巴氏涂片检查几乎已普及,但到 2022 年,这一比例下降至 57.0%,而联合检测则增加至 41.0%。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 随着时间的推移,基于 HPV 的筛查方式的采用不断增加,并且因患者的乡村、种族和民族而异。一些组织采用率较低可能反映出采用新筛查方式的能力/资源有限,这可能会影响筛查的公平性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为改善 FQHC 中 HPV 筛查的公平性所做的努力提供了信息,特别是对于农村和未参保人群。了解与采用相关的因素可以指导有针对性的干预措施,以提高筛查的采用率并减少 宫颈癌 差异。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于华盛顿和爱达荷州的三个 FQHC 系统,这可能会限制对其他地区或医疗机构的推广。尽管存在这些限制,大样本量和纵向设计为理解基于 HPV 的筛查采用模式提供了适度的证据。

papers.title: Evaluation of HPV Knowledge Levels Among Healthcare Professionals and Medical Students: A Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study in Private Hospitals and Foundation Universities in Turkey.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To assess the knowledge and attitudes toward human papillomavirus (HPV) and HPV vaccination among healthcare professionals and medical students and to identify demographic and professional factors associated with variations in HPV knowledge. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 903 participants comprising medical doctors, medical students, nurses, and other allied healthcare personnel. HPV knowledge was measured using the validated 33-item Human Papillomavirus Knowledge Scale (HPV-KS), which evaluates four domains: general HPV knowledge, HPV screening tests, HPV vaccination, and the national HPV vaccination program. Demographic, educational, occupational, and geographical variables were also collected. Total and domain-specific scores were compared across gender, professional groups, and educational levels. RESULTS: The mean total HPV knowledge score was 19.23 out of 33, indicating moderate overall knowledge. Correct response rates were high for core factual items (e.g., HPV as the leading cause of cervical cancer), yet several misconceptions persisted, including misunderstandings about HIV/AIDS causation and HPV transmission dynamics. Male participants demonstrated significantly higher total knowledge (p = 0.008) and greater HPV screening test knowledge (p = 0.003) than females. Professional category did not yield significant differences in total scores although medical doctors and medical students showed slightly higher vaccination-related knowledge. Participants who were not physicians or medical students had higher screening and vaccination knowledge, whereas physicians and medical students scored higher on vaccination program knowledge. CONCLUSIONS: HPV knowledge among healthcare professionals and medical students was moderate, with persistent misconceptions across several domains. Gender-based differences and unexpected patterns among physicians and medical students suggest that existing curricula may not adequately address HPV and HPV vaccination. Strengthening formal education, integrating evidence-based HPV modules into health sciences training, and providing structured professional development are essential to enhancing HPV awareness, supporting vaccination advocacy, and improving preventive health practices.

analysis.study_design_and_population: A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted in private hospitals and foundation universities in Turkey, involving 903 participants, including medical doctors, medical students, nurses, and other allied healthcare personnel. papers.abstract_zh: 目的:评估医疗保健专业人员和医学生对 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 和 HPV 疫苗接种 的知识和态度,并确定与 HPV 知识变化相关的人口和专业因素。方法:这项横断面研究包括 903 名参与者,其中包括医生、医学生、护士和其他相关医疗人员。HPV 知识使用经过验证的 33 项 人乳头瘤病毒 知识量表 (HPV-KS) 进行测量,该量表评估四个领域:一般 HPV 知识、HPV 筛查测试、HPV 疫苗接种 和国家 HPV 疫苗接种 计划。还收集了人口、教育、职业和地理变量。对不同性别、专业群体和教育水平的总分和特定领域得分进行了比较。结果:HPV 知识总分平均为 19.23(满分 33 分),表明总体知识水平中等。核心事实项目的正确回答率很高(例如,HPV 是 传播 的主要原因),但一些误解仍然存在,包括对 HIV/艾滋病因果关系和 HPV 传播 动态的误解。男性参与者表现出明显高于女性的总知识 (p = 0.008) 和 HPV 筛查测试知识 (p = 0.003)。尽管医生和医学生的疫苗接种相关知识略高,但专业类别总分没有产生显着差异。非医生或医学生的参与者具有较高的筛查和 疫苗接种 知识,而医生和医学生在 疫苗接种 项目知识上得分较高。结论:医疗保健专业人员和医学生对 HPV 的了解程度一般,多个领域持续存在误解。医生和医学生之间基于性别的差异和意外模式表明,现有课程可能无法充分解决 HPV 和 HPV 疫苗接种。加强正规教育、将循证 HPV 模块纳入健康科学培训以及提供结构化专业发展对于提高 HPV 认识、支持 疫苗接种 宣传和改善预防性健康实践至关重要。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估医疗保健专业人员和医学生对 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 和 HPV 疫苗接种 的知识和态度,并确定与 HPV 知识变化相关的人口和专业因素。这一背景凸显了了解医疗机构中 HPV 相关知识差距对于改善预防措施的重要性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项多中心横断面研究在土耳其的私立医院和基础大学进行,涉及 903 名参与者,包括医生、医学生、护士和其他专职医疗人员。该研究主要针对医疗保健专业人员和医学生,收集了人口、教育、职业和地理变量的数据。
analysis_zh.methods: HPV 知识使用经过验证的 33 项 人乳头瘤病毒 知识量表 (HPV-KS) 进行评估,该量表评估四个领域:一般 HPV 知识、HPV 筛查测试、HPV 疫苗接种 和国家 HPV 疫苗接种 计划。比较了不同性别、专业群体和教育水平的总分和特定领域得分。
analysis_zh.main_results: HPV 知识总分平均为 19.23(满分 33 分),表明总体知识水平中等。对于核心事实项目(例如 HPV 是 传播 的主要原因)的正确回答率很高,但仍然存在一些误解,包括对 HIV/AIDS 因果关系和 HPV 传播 动态的误解。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解读为,虽然人们对 HPV 的了解程度中等,但误解仍然存在,尤其是在某些群体中。新颖之处在于强调医生和医学生之间基于性别的差异和意想不到的知识模式。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,加强正规教育并将基于证据的 HPV 模块纳入健康科学培训可以提高认识并支持 疫苗接种 的宣传,这对于预防 宫颈癌 等 HPV 相关疾病至关重要。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到横截面设计的限制,不允许进行因果推断。中等证据强度基于经过验证的知识量表以及人口和专业群体之间的分数比较。

papers.title: Synergistic U-bent geometry and bimetallic plasmonics for ultra-sensitive fibre-optic SPR biosensing of cervical cancer.
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer arises from uncontrolled proliferation of epithelial cells in the lower uterine cervix, primarily triggered by persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus strains. Timely and reliable detection of malignant cellular transformations is therefore essential for effective therapeutic intervention. Here, we report a highly sensitive plasmonic U-bent fibre-optic biosensor (FOB) integrated with Au and Ag nanocoatings for rapid identification of cervical cancer cells. This work is innovative in combining a U-bent fibre geometry, which enables robust waveguide propagation at a small bend radius (1-1.5 mm), with a bimetallic (Au-Ag) plasmonic interface, thereby significantly enhancing light-matter interaction and SPR sensitivity compared with conventional straight single and multi mode fibre sensors. The U-bent geometry markedly strengthens the interaction between leaky evanescent waveguide fields with the surrounding analyte, enabling enhanced plasmonic coupling compared with conventional straight fibre configurations. Detailed numerical simulations were employed to optimize critical structural parameters, including bend diameter, metallic layer thickness, and sensing length with different cancerous cells, resulting in substantial performance enhancement. Furthermore, the systematic optimization framework presented here provides a scalable pathway for translating high-performance FOBs from laboratory research to practical point-of-care (PoC) diagnostic platforms. The optimized sensor exhibits a maximum sensitivity of ∼34 050 nm RIU -1 in the RI range of 1.42-1.43, while maintaining sensitivities of approximately 22 000 nm RIU -1 across most of the investigated RI range. In addition to sensitivity, the resonance linewidth was assessed through a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of ∼77.5 nm, resulting in a figure of merit (FOM) of ∼25-30 RIU -1 and a limit of detection (LOD) of ∼1.3124 × 10 -3 RIU. This plasmonic fibre architecture provides a robust and scalable platform for high-precision optical diagnostics and exhibits strong potential for clinical translation. Moreover, the proposed design is compatible with laboratory-scale fabrication and industrial production, supporting PoC deployment.

The U-bent geometry improves plasmonic coupling by strengthening the interaction between waveguide fields and the surrounding analyte. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 宫颈癌 是由子宫颈下部上皮细胞不受控制的增殖引起的,主要是由高危 人乳头瘤病毒 菌株的持续感染引发的。因此,及时、可靠地检测恶性细胞转化对于有效的治疗干预至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在这里,我们报道了一种与金和银纳米涂层集成的高灵敏度等离子体 U 形弯曲光纤生物传感器(FOB),用于快速识别 宫颈癌 细胞。该研究是在实验室环境中进行的,通过数值模拟来优化结构参数。该传感器用不同的癌细胞进行了测试,以评估其性能。
elements_zh.methods: 采用详细的数值模拟来优化关键结构参数,包括弯曲直径、金属层厚度和不同癌细胞的传感长度,从而显着提高性能。除了灵敏度之外,还通过~77.5 nm的半峰全宽(FWHM)评估共振线宽,得到~25-30 RIU -1 的品质因数(FOM)和~1.3124 × 10 -3 RIU的检测限(LOD)。
elements_zh.main_results: 这项工作的创新之处在于将 U 形弯曲光纤几何形状与双金属 (Au-Ag) 等离子体界面相结合,从而能够在小弯曲半径 (1-1.5 mm) 下实现稳健的波导传播,从而与传统的直单模和多模光纤传感器相比,显着增强光与物质的相互作用和 SPR 灵敏度。U 形弯曲的几何形状显着增强了泄漏倏逝波导场与周围分析物之间的相互作用,与传统的直光纤配置相比,能够增强等离子体耦合。

papers.title_zh: 用于 宫颈癌 超灵敏光纤 SPR 生物传感的协同 U 形弯曲几何结构和双金属等离子体激元。
papers.source_body_en: Cervical cancer arises from uncontrolled proliferation of epithelial cells in the lower uterine cervix, primarily triggered by persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus strains. Timely and reliable detection of malignant cellular transformations is therefore essential for effective therapeutic intervention. Here, we report a highly sensitive plasmonic U-bent fibre-optic biosensor (FOB) integrated with Au and Ag nanocoatings for rapid identification of cervical cancer cells. This work is innovative in combining a U-bent fibre geometry, which enables robust waveguide propagation at a small bend radius (1-1.5 mm), with a bimetallic (Au-Ag) plasmonic interface, thereby significantly enhancing light-matter interaction and SPR sensitivity compared with conventional straight single and multi mode fibre sensors. The U-bent geometry markedly strengthens the interaction between leaky evanescent waveguide fields with the surrounding analyte, enabling enhanced plasmonic coupling compared with conventional straight fibre configurations. Detailed numerical simulations were employed to optimize critical structural parameters, including bend diameter, metallic layer thickness, and sensing length with different cancerous cells, resulting in substantial performance enhancement. Furthermore, the systematic optimization framework presented here provides a scalable pathway for translating high-performance FOBs from laboratory research to practical point-of-care (PoC) diagnostic platforms. The optimized sensor exhibits a maximum sensitivity of ∼34 050 nm RIU -1 in the RI range of 1.42-1.43, while maintaining sensitivities of approximately 22 000 nm RIU -1 across most of the investigated RI range. In addition to sensitivity, the resonance linewidth was assessed through a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of ∼77.5 nm, resulting in a figure of merit (FOM) of ∼25-30 RIU -1 and a limit of detection (LOD) of ∼1.3124 × 10 -3 RIU. This plasmonic fibre architecture provides a robust and scalable platform for high-precision optical diagnostics and exhibits strong potential for clinical translation. Moreover, the proposed design is compatible with laboratory-scale fabrication and industrial production, supporting PoC deployment.

papers.title: Oncogenic viruses and their role in oral cavity and oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma: a systematic review
papers.abstract: Oral cavity (OC) and oropharyngeal (OP) squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) represent a major global health concern, accounting for most of head and neck malignancies. These tumors arise from the epithelial lining of the OC and oropharynx and are characterized by aggressive local invasion, lymph node metastasis, and high morbidity and mortality. In addition to known risk factors such as tobacco and alcohol consumption, several oncogenic viruses, including human papillomavirus (HPV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), human herpesviruses (HHV) 1 and 2, cytomegalovirus (CMV) and Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCPyV), have been implicated in the development, progression, or prognosis. Detection of viral genomes within tumor tissues suggests a complex interplay between viral oncogenes, host immune responses, and environmental factors in carcinogenesis. This systematic review synthesizes current evidence on the contribution of oncogenic viruses to the etiology of OC and OP SCC. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, observational studies between January 2015 and December 2025 were identified through searches of PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science. Eligible studies were limited to human research and reporting viral detections. The results demonstrate a strong, consistent, and clinically relevant association between HPV infection and OP SCC, while evidence supporting a causal or prognostic role for non-HPV oncogenic viruses in OC and OP SCC remains limited and heterogeneous. Substantial methodological variability in viral detection approaches and epidemiological reporting was observed, underscoring the need for standardized assessment frameworks. Overall, these results support site-specific interpretation of viral oncogenesis and inform the development of targeted prevention, diagnostic stratification, and therapeutic strategies.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本系统综述重点关注致癌病毒,特别是 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 在口腔 (OC) 和口咽 (OP) 鳞状细胞癌 (SCC) 病因学中的作用。核心问题是综合关于这些病毒对 OC 和 OP SCC 的发生、进展或预后的贡献的当前证据。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 遵循 PRISMA 2020 指南,本次系统综述包括 2015 年 1 月至 2025 年 12 月的观察性研究,这些研究是通过 PubMed、Scopus 和 Web of Science 的搜索确定的。符合条件的研究仅限于报告病毒检测的人类研究。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述表明 HPV 感染与 OP SCC 之间存在强烈、一致且具有临床相关性的关联。然而,支持非 HPV 致癌病毒在 OC 和 OP SCC 中的因果或预后作用的证据仍然有限且异质。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 观察到病毒检测方法和流行病学报告存在显着的方法学差异,凸显了标准化评估框架的必要性。由于证据有限且异质性,非 HPV 致癌病毒在 OC 和 OP SCC 中的作用仍未得到解决。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 这些发现支持病毒肿瘤发生的位点特异性解释,并为 OC 和 OP SCC 的针对性预防、诊断分层和治疗策略的制定提供信息。

papers.title_zh: 致癌病毒及其在口腔和口咽鳞状细胞癌中的作用:系统评价
papers.source_body_en: Oral cavity (OC) and oropharyngeal (OP) squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) represent a major global health concern, accounting for most of head and neck malignancies. These tumors arise from the epithelial lining of the OC and oropharynx and are characterized by aggressive local invasion, lymph node metastasis, and high morbidity and mortality. In addition to known risk factors such as tobacco and alcohol consumption, several oncogenic viruses, including human papillomavirus (HPV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), human herpesviruses (HHV) 1 and 2, cytomegalovirus (CMV) and Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCPyV), have been implicated in the development, progression, or prognosis. Detection of viral genomes within tumor tissues suggests a complex interplay between viral oncogenes, host immune responses, and environmental factors in carcinogenesis. This systematic review synthesizes current evidence on the contribution of oncogenic viruses to the etiology of OC and OP SCC. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, observational studies between January 2015 and December 2025 were identified through searches of PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science. Eligible studies were limited to human research and reporting viral detections. The results demonstrate a strong, consistent, and clinically relevant association between HPV infection and OP SCC, while evidence supporting a causal or prognostic role for non-HPV oncogenic viruses in OC and OP SCC remains limited and heterogeneous. Substantial methodological variability in viral detection approaches and epidemiological reporting was observed, underscoring the need for standardized assessment frameworks. Overall, these results support site-specific interpretation of viral oncogenesis and inform the development of targeted prevention, diagnostic stratification, and therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Immunotherapy and Relevant Antibody–Drug Conjugates in Gynecologic Oncology: Recent Advances, Ongoing Challenges, and Future Directions
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors and antibody–drug conjugates have rapidly expanded treatment options for gynecologic malignancies, although the magnitude of benefit varies substantially across tumor types and biomarker-defined populations. This narrative review summarizes the biologic rationale, predictive biomarkers, pivotal clinical trials, regulatory approvals, guideline-supported strategies, and emerging directions for immune checkpoint blockade and antibody–drug conjugates in endometrial, cervical, and ovarian cancers. In endometrial cancer, molecular classification and mismatch repair status have transformed treatment selection, with PD-1 or PD-L1 blockade now integrated into first-line chemoimmunotherapy and recurrent disease management. HER2-directed and TROP-2-directed antibody–drug conjugates are also emerging as biomarker-directed strategies. In cervical cancer, human papillomavirus-driven tumor biology, PD-L1 expression, and tissue factor expression support the use of checkpoint inhibitors, antibody–drug conjugates, and therapeutic vaccine approaches across locally advanced and recurrent or metastatic settings. In ovarian cancer, single-agent checkpoint blockade has shown limited activity in unselected populations, but recent advances include biomarker-selected chemoimmunotherapy in platinum-resistant disease and clinically meaningful activity of folate receptor alpha-directed and HER2-directed antibody–drug conjugates. Across gynecologic cancers, key challenges include refining predictive biomarkers, optimizing sequencing after prior immunotherapy exposure, managing overlapping toxicities, and designing trials that enrich for biologically responsive subgroups. Future progress will depend on integrating molecular classification, immune contexture, ADC target expression, and patient-specific clinical factors into treatment selection.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注妇科恶性肿瘤的免疫疗法和抗体药物偶联物,特别检查它们在子宫内膜癌、宫颈癌和卵巢癌中的应用。中心问题围绕着这些 治疗 在不同肿瘤类型和生物标志物定义人群中的生物学原理、预测生物标志物、临床试验结果和新兴策略。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这是一篇叙述性综述,总结了子宫内膜癌、宫颈癌和卵巢癌中免疫检查点阻断和抗体药物偶联物的生物学原理、预测性生物标志物、关键临床试验、监管批准、指南支持的策略以及新兴方向。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 在子宫内膜癌中,分子分类和错配修复状态已经改变了 治疗 选择,PD-1 或​​ PD-L1 阻断现已纳入一线化学免疫治疗和复发性疾病管理。在 宫颈癌 中,人乳头瘤病毒 驱动的肿瘤生物学、PD-L1 表达和组织因子表达支持在局部晚期和复发或转移环境中使用检查点抑制剂、抗体药物偶联物和治疗 疫苗 方法。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 在妇科癌症中,关键挑战包括完善预测生物标志物、优化先前免疫治疗暴露后的测序、管理重叠毒性以及设计丰富生物反应亚组的试验。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的进展将取决于将分子分类、免疫背景、ADC 靶点表达和患者特异性临床因素整合到 治疗 选择中。

papers.title: Case report: Penile collision tumor comprising HPV-associated squamous cell carcinoma and malignant melanoma
papers.abstract: Collision tumors with squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) and malignant melanoma components are extremely rare. We report a case of a penile collision tumor with a component of HPV-associated SCC and malignant melanoma in a 61 year-old man. The patient underwent a partial penectomy and bilateral inguinal sentinel lymph node surgery. Microscopy showed a biphasic tumor with a component of SCC with warty-basaloid morphology, positive for HPV16 and 43, and a malignant melanoma associated with a BRAF mutation. This case posed diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to the absence of a precise TNM classification and documented treatment guidelines for this tumor type.

papers.title: Prevention is better than cure: Awareness and acceptance of the HPV vaccine for condyloma acuminata (CA) among college students who self-report no sexual experience.
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) types 6 and 11 cause 90% of condyloma acuminata (CA). Timely vaccination reduces CA-related disease burdens, especially among sexually inexperienced college students, a critical catch-up group for vaccination. Few studies investigate sexually inexperienced college students' views on CA and HPV vaccination, despite research on general student HPV awareness. This cross-sectional study was conducted in Guangdong in May 2017, and recruited college students who self-identified as having no prior sexual relations. Participants completed a WeChat-based online questionnaire to assess their knowledge of HPV, CA, and acceptance of HPV vaccination for CA. A total of 2037 valid questionnaires were collected and analyzed. Knowledge of CA (26.3%) and HPV (18.9%) was low among college students who self-reported no sexual experience, as was the HPV vaccination rate (2.6%). However, their acceptance of the HPV vaccine for CA was relatively high (54.7%). Respondents were more likely to have received the HPV vaccine for CA if they had heard of CA (OR = 1.40, 95% CI: 1.05-1.85), had actively learned about CA (OR = 1.62, 95% CI: 1.10-2.38), considered the vaccine safe (OR = 1.94, 95% CI: 1.03-3.65), and believed the vaccine effective in preventing CA (OR = 5.08, 95% CI: 2.05-12.59). Sexually inexperienced college students demonstrated insufficient knowledge of CA and HPV vaccines. Higher awareness of the safety and efficacy of the HPV vaccine, as well as knowledge about CA, were positive associated with the willingness to receive the HPV vaccine.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) types 6 and 11 cause 90% of condyloma acuminata (CA), and timely vaccination reduces CA-related disease burdens, especially among sexually inexperienced college students, a critical catch-up group for vaccination. Few studies investigate sexually inexperienced college students' views on CA and HPV vaccination, despite research on general student HPV awareness.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study was conducted in Guangdong in May 2017, and recruited college students who self-identified as having no prior sexual relations. Participants completed a WeChat-based online questionnaire to assess their knowledge of HPV, CA, and acceptance of HPV vaccination for CA. A total of 2037 valid questionnaires were collected and analyzed.
analysis.methods: The study analyzed associations between knowledge, awareness, and vaccination acceptance using logistic regression.
analysis.main_results: Knowledge of CA (26.3%) and HPV (18.9%) was low among college students who self-reported no sexual experience, as was the HPV vaccination rate (2.6%). However, their acceptance of the HPV vaccine for CA was relatively high (54.7%). Respondents were more likely to have received the HPV vaccine for CA if they had heard of CA (OR = 1.40, 95% CI: 1.05-1.85), had actively learned about CA (OR = 1.62, 95% CI: 1.10-2.38), considered the vaccine safe (OR = 1.94, 95% CI: 1.03-3.65), and believed the vaccine effective in preventing CA (OR = 5.08, 95% CI: 2.05-12.59).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Sexually inexperienced college students demonstrated insufficient knowledge of CA and HPV vaccines, yet their acceptance of the HPV vaccine for CA was relatively high. Higher awareness of the safety and efficacy of the HPV vaccine, as well as knowledge about CA, were positively associated with the willingness to receive the HPV vaccine.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for targeted education campaigns to improve knowledge about CA and HPV vaccines among sexually inexperienced college students, potentially increasing vaccination rates and reducing CA-related disease burdens.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was cross-sectional, limiting causal inference, and relied on self-reported data without biological verification of sexual experience or vaccination status. The evidence strength is moderate due to the large sample size but limited by the study design and potential self-report bias.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study investigated HPV and CA knowledge and vaccine acceptance among 2037 sexually inexperienced college students in Guangdong, China. Despite low knowledge of CA (26.3%) and HPV (18.9%), vaccine acceptance was relatively high (54.7%). Vaccination was associated with prior awareness of CA, active learning about CA, and beliefs in vaccine safety and efficacy. The findings suggest a need for targeted education to improve knowledge and increase vaccination rates in this critical catch-up group.

papers.title: Fingernail Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Scoping Review of Surgical Approaches and Clinical Decision Making.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Squamous cell carcinoma of the fingernail unit (nSCC) is a rare malignancy frequently misdiagnosed as benign nail disease, resulting in delayed diagnosis and heterogeneous management. OBJECTIVE: To characterize surgical management patterns of nSCC and determine if imaging and other clinical factors influence the decision to perform digit preservation techniques versus amputation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A scoping review of PubMed was performed to analyze the current literature from 2000 onward regarding surgical management of nSCC. Data on clinical presentation, tumor characteristics, imaging, treatment approach, and outcomes were extracted and synthesized descriptively. RESULTS: Eighty studies met inclusion criteria, predominantly case reports and small case series. NSCC commonly mimicked benign nail conditions, contributing to delayed diagnosis. Human papillomavirus-associated disease was described in recurrent, multifocal, and immunosuppressed cases. Imaging was reported in 50% of studies, most commonly plain radiography. Bone invasion, recurrent disease, and extensive local involvement were most frequently associated with amputation, whereas digit-sparing approaches, particularly Mohs micrographic surgery, were commonly used in localized disease without osseous involvement. CONCLUSION: Management of nSCC reflects a reproducible decision-making framework centered on disease extent, bone involvement, recurrence status, and preservation of function. Early recognition and timely biopsy may increase opportunities for digit-sparing treatment.

analysis.summary_en: This scoping review aimed to characterize surgical management patterns of fingernail squamous cell carcinoma (nSCC) and assess the influence of imaging and clinical factors on the decision to use digit preservation techniques versus amputation. The study analyzed 80 publications from 2000 onward, primarily case reports and small case series, highlighting the challenges in diagnosing nSCC due to its mimicry of benign nail conditions. Human papillomavirus (HPV) was associated with recurrent, multifocal, and immunosuppressed cases, and imaging was reported in 50% of studies, most commonly plain radiography. Bone invasion, recurrence, and extensive local involvement were linked to amputation, while digit-sparing approaches, especially Mohs micrographic surgery, were favored for localized disease without osseous involvement. The findings suggest a decision-making framework based on disease extent, bone involvement, recurrence status, and functional preservation. Early diagnosis through timely biopsy could enhance the potential for digit-sparing treatment. The evidence is descriptive and abstract-only, with no reported limitations or evidence strength assessment.

analysis_zh.main_results: 80 项研究符合纳入标准,主要是 病例报告 和小病例系列。在复发性、多灶性和免疫抑制病例中描述了 人乳头瘤病毒 相关疾病。50% 的研究报告了影像学检查,最常见的是平片。骨侵犯、复发性疾病和广泛的局部受累最常与截肢相关,而保留手指的方法,特别是莫氏显微手术,通常用于无骨受累的局部疾病。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: nSCC 的管理反映了以疾病范围、骨受累、复发状态和功能保留为中心的可重复决策框架。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 早期识别和及时活检可能会增加保留手指 治疗 的机会。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告局限性或证据强度。

the trial met its primary efficacy endpoint with histopathologic regression of lesions and targeted viral clearance, and ApolloBio plans to pursue a regulatory submission in China. • In March 2026, Nykode announced that its randomized clinical trial (Abili-T) in 1L R/M head and neck cancer is on track to deliver meaningful interim results by 2027. • In January 2026, BNT113 received Fast Track Designation from the US FDA for the treatment of HPV16+ HNSCC expressing PD-L1. • PDS Biotechnology indicated in its 2026 corporate presentation that Phase II clinical data for PDS0101 in cervical cancer are expected to be reported in H2 2026. • HPV16 remains the predominant oncogenic type, accounting for ≥60% in anogenital cancer sites and 44-91% in head and neck cancers. • According to the CDC, about 91% of anal cancer cases in the United States are thought to be attributable to HPV infection. • An estimated 26 million Americans have an oral HPV infection at any given time, of whom approximately 2,600 are infected with HPV16. • The total incident cases of HPV16+ Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma (OPSCC) in Japan were nearly 3,900 in 2025. • The HPV16+ Cancers Companies include Merck, Bristol Myers Squibb, Merus, Nykode Therapeutics, Roche, PDS Biotechnology, BioNTech, Cue Biopharma, Transgene, and others. • Promising HPV16+ Cancers Therapies include Petosemtamab (MCLA-158), Versamune HPV (PDS0101), BNT113, Abipapogene suvaplasmid (VB10.16), CUE-101, TG4001, and others. Get a Free sample for the HPV16+ Cancers Market Forecast, Size & Share Analysis Report @ https://www.delveinsight.com/sample-request/human-papillomavirus-16-positive-hpv16-cancers-market?utm_source=openpr&utm_medium=pressrelease&utm_campaign=akpr What are HPV16-Positive Cancers? HPV16+ Cancers are virus-driven epithelial malignancies primarily caused by persistent infection with human papillomavirus type 16, one of the most oncogenic HPV strains responsible for a significant proportion of cervical cancers and head & neck squamous cell carcinomas, particularly oropharyngeal tumors. These cancers arise when viral oncoproteins E6 and E7 disrupt key tumor suppressor pathways, leading to uncontrolled cellular proliferation, genomic instability, and malignant transformation of epithelial cells. Diagnosis begins with clinical suspicion based on symptoms or screening findings, followed by confirmation through biopsy and histopathological examination, which typically reveals squamous cell carcinoma. Once malignancy is established, HPV16 status is determined using molecular and immunohistochemical methods, most commonly HPV DNA genotyping and p16 immunohistochemistry, with HPV E6/E7 mRNA testing sometimes used for more definitive evidence of active viral oncogene expression.
